symbols.name: EventMap
symbols.description: Native events dispatched through `Events.on`. Each property is the exact callback argument tuple for that event.

properties.name: playerConnect
properties.description: Dispatched once a connecting player's body exists and can be resolved to a handle. The body has no pose yet -- `player.ready` is false until the owner reports one.

properties.name: playerDisconnect
properties.description: Dispatched while a player is leaving, before their body is destroyed, so the handle still reads. Anything keyed on the player must be cleaned up here: a dropped connection raises no other event.

properties.name: playerDied
properties.description:
Dispatched once per accepted death report. Call player.revive() to request revival; there is no automatic respawn.

`killer` is the player or server NPC whose blow took the last of the health, as the dying player's own client saw it -- null for a fall, a bleed-out, or anything without an identified attacker. `reason` is the game's own for that last write: `combat` for a blade or a bow, `fall`, `bleeding`, `poison` and so on.

type.name: [player: Player, killer: Player | Npc | null, reason: "unknown" | "combat" | "gunshot" | "starvation" | "collision" | "scripted" | "disintegrate" | "fall" | "poison" | "bleeding" | "selfHarm"]

properties.name: playerDamage
properties.description:
Dispatched when something takes health off a player: a weapon, an arrow, a fall, a collision, a scripted hit. Player combat and server NPC melee are raised by the server as it rules on them, after `playerHit` had its say, so `amount` is what the ruling takes; anything else is reported by the hit player's own client, which resolved it against its armour and its skills. It arrives ahead of the `playerDied` a killing blow causes.

`attacker` is the player or server NPC who dealt it, or null. `bodyPart` is where it landed, or null for damage that lands nowhere in particular. A player attacker's weapon is available through `rightHandItem` or `leftHandItem`; an NPC's equipped items are in `wearing`.

Bleeding, poison and hunger wear health down a tick at a time without raising this -- `bleeding`, `poisoning` and `hunger` are live numbers already. The tick that kills does arrive, with its own reason, just before the `playerDied` it causes.

type.name: [player: Player, attacker: Player | Npc | null, amount: number, bodyPart: "head" | "torso" | "leftArm" | "rightArm" | "leftLeg" | "rightLeg" | null, reason: "unknown" | "combat" | "gunshot" | "starvation" | "collision" | "scripted" | "disintegrate" | "fall" | "poison" | "bleeding" | "selfHarm"]

properties.name: playerAttack
properties.description: A melee swing aimed at another player was admitted by the server, including a miss. Raised once per attack generation, after presentation admission. Use it to track combat inactivity in your resource.

properties.name: playerCombatCancelled
properties.description: A resource called cancelCombat for this pair. Raised after the cancellation was sent to both players and their observers.

properties.name: playerHit
properties.description:
Dispatched when another player's blade or arrow, or a server NPC's melee attack, lands on a player, before anything is taken -- the place for teams, safe zones, friendly fire and damage rules. The game resolved the blow against the guard the victim really held -- whether it was blocked, perfectly or not, and where it landed -- and the server works out what a swing takes from there; it has checked that the swing was one it relayed and could still land, or that the arrow was one whose impact it accepted, and that the two stood within reach. Only what is ruled here comes off the victim's health, on every client at once.

Return `false` from a handler to refuse the blow: no health is taken and no `playerDamage` follows. NPC melee uses the victim client's native damage with `priced: false`; set `hit.damage` to change it. For priced player swings, scale `hit.modifiers` to change how a swing is worked out -- a stronger attack, weaker armour -- or set `hit.damage` to say outright what it takes: `0` for a blow that lands harmlessly, more for a heavier one. Either way the blow is still seen and heard: the blades met. Handlers run synchronously, so the decision cannot wait on anything awaited.

type.name: [player: Player, attacker: Player | Npc, hit: PlayerHit]

properties.name: playerInjured
properties.description: Dispatched when a limb becomes injured -- usually a blow landing there, sometimes a fall on both legs. `player.injuries` already says so. A limb hit again while injured stays injured and raises nothing new.

properties.name: playerInjuryHealed
properties.description: Dispatched when a limb injury is gone: it healed by itself, a bandage took it, or `player.heal` did.

properties.name: playerSpawning
properties.description:
Dispatched when a player's body needs somewhere to stand, while their own client waits on the answer behind its loading screen. This is the one moment a spawn can be chosen without anybody seeing the body move -- call `player.spawn(position)` from the handler and that becomes where they arrive.

Handlers run synchronously, so the choice has to be made in the handler itself rather than in something awaited from it. A handler that names no placement leaves the player at the level's own start point, which is the same tile for everybody.

`reason` says whether they are arriving or coming back: `join` for a connection, `respawn` after a death.

properties.name: playerAnimationEnd
properties.description:
Dispatched once when the animation a `playAnimation` request started is over. `fragment` is the request's. `reason` says how: `finished` when a one-shot played to its end, `interrupted` when it was playing and something cut it short (a hit, a weapon drawn, a teleport), `refused` when the game would not start it at all, `stopped` for `stopAnimation`, `replaced` for another `playAnimation`.

The first three come from the player's own client, sent from the moment the game's animation system ended it, so this is the place to chain the next animation. A `loop` never finishes by itself and only ends `stopped` or `replaced`. A request with no fragment -- one that only holds a prop or a tag -- raises nothing.

properties.name: playerCarrying
properties.description:
Dispatched when a player has picked up another player's body, before the server accepts it -- the place to decide who may carry whom. Return `false` from a handler and the carry is refused: the carrier's client is told to let go at once, and no `playerCarry` follows. Handlers run synchronously, so the decision cannot wait on anything awaited.

The pick-up is the game's own "grab" prompt, which it offers only over a body that is down -- dead or unconscious -- so a player a script revives at once is never there to carry. The carrier's game has already started the pick-up when this runs.

properties.name: playerCarry
properties.description: Dispatched once a carry is accepted: the carried body is on the carrier's shoulder on every client, and `carrier.carrying` names it. It rides there until `playerPutDown`.

properties.name: playerPutDown
properties.description: Dispatched once a carry is over, however it ended: the carrier dropped the body, `putDown` asked them to, the carried player was revived, or either of them left. A player who is leaving is still readable here; the event comes before their body is destroyed.

properties.name: playerCarryingItem
properties.description: Dispatched when a player starts a carry of their own, before the server accepts it: they chose the game's pick-up prompt over a carryable `groundItem`, or took an item from one of the world's own piles (`groundItem` null). Return `false` from a handler and the carry is refused -- the prop stays where it is, and a pile's item is let go at once. Handlers run synchronously, so the decision cannot wait on anything awaited. A carry a script ordered with `carryItem` is not asked. `item` is the item's name.

type.name: [player: Player, item: string, groundItem: GroundItem | null]

properties.name: playerCarryItem
properties.description: Dispatched once an item carry is accepted: everybody sees the player pick it up and carry it, and `player.carriedItem` names it. `groundItem` is the prop it was taken up from, still readable here and gone a moment later, or null. It is carried until `playerPutDownItem`.

type.name: [player: Player, item: string, groundItem: GroundItem | null]

properties.name: playerPutDownItem
properties.description: Dispatched once an item carry is over, however it ended: the player put it down, `putDownItem` asked them to, it went into a pile, or they left. `groundItem` is the carryable prop it became where it fell -- still falling, settling where the game's physics puts it -- or null when it went into a pile or they have no room left on the ground.

type.name: [player: Player, item: string, groundItem: GroundItem | null]

properties.name: playerSpawned
properties.description:
Dispatched once a joining player is really standing in the world: their level is up, their body is where `playerSpawning` put it, and the ground under it has loaded. Anything that acts on an arriving player -- kit, a welcome line, a marker -- belongs here rather than in `playerConnect`, which fires while they are still loading the level, or in `playerSpawning`, where the body is still mid-placement.

The player may still be looking at the game's loading screen; `playerReady` follows once they are not.

properties.name: playerReady
properties.description:
Dispatched once per connection, after `playerSpawned`, when the player can play: their own client reports that the game has taken its loading screen down. The game raises that moment itself -- it is its own gameplay-start signal, not a guess from timing.

That player's client resources were already running at `playerSpawned`, so this is not needed to make sure a `player.emit` is received. It is for what the player should actually see on arrival -- a welcome, a first page, a camera shot -- which shown earlier would play behind the loading screen. A client that never gets that far, or disconnects first, never raises it.

properties.name: playerStatsChanged
properties.description: After the server receives changed player stats, including poison strength, drunkenness, health loss and potion-related readings. Changes are snapshots batched per server tick. The first valid report and each new body establish a baseline. These are observations, not cancellable requests; the client can coalesce intermediate values. No cause is inferred. Use consumption vetoes and custom server effects to decide gameplay before it happens.

type.name: [player: Player, changes: { stat: "health" | "stamina" | "exhaust" | "hunger" | "bleeding" | "sleeping" | "consciousness" | "drunkenness" | "poisoning" | "charisma" | "visibility" | "conspicuousness" | "noise" | "dirtiness" | "bloodiness" | "smell" | "smellIntensity" | "fragrance" | "carriedWeight" | "inventoryCapacity" | "encumbrance" | "hangover" | "alcoholism" | "armorRating" | "overallArmorDefense" | "overallWeaponAttack" | "normalizedRunSpeed" | "runSpeedBase" | "morale"; previous: number; current: number }[]]

properties.name: playerConsuming
properties.description: Before reserving a food or potion unit or pot serving. Return false synchronously to refuse without spending stock or applying effects. Async handlers cannot veto. Do not apply replacement effects here: native use can still fail.

properties.name: playerConsumptionEffects
properties.description: After playerConsuming accepts, before reservation. Return false synchronously to consume without native nutrition, energy, alcohol, potion, spoilage or added pot poison effects. Apply custom effects in playerConsumed using player.setStat, addBuff and clearBuffs.

properties.name: playerPoisonAbsorbing
properties.description: Before applying a reserved pot meal's additional poison on its eating receipt. Return false synchronously to suppress it. Runs only when nativeEffects is true. Native food spoilage and item buffs can be replaced through playerConsumptionEffects and Buffs.claim.

properties.name: playerConsumed
properties.description: Once after the owning client confirms successful use. Use for custom stat changes and buffs after suppressing native effects. Missing receipts and expired or replaced bodies never raise it. Inventory uses also raise playerItemUsed.

properties.name: playerPreparing
properties.description: Dispatched when a player's game dried, smoked or cooked items, before the server converts them in its inventory. The game converts at once when its animation ends; nothing about it takes time. Return `false` from a handler to refuse it: the items stay as they were, and the player's game puts them back. Every handler runs, synchronously: handler promises are not awaited, so an async handler cannot refuse. To make it take time, refuse it, take the rows with `Inventory.remove` and give the products with `Inventory.add` when your timer is up. The inventory change is `dry`, `smoke` or `cook`. Only an accepted one earns the game's survival XP, which the server grants per unit converted as `player.addXp` grants XP: the player's own multipliers apply; `playerXpGaining`, `Progression.setXpRate`, `setXpBudget`, `setLevelCap` and `setNativeXp(false)` do not.

properties.name: playerCustomItemUse
properties.description: A validated custom-item action. The frozen row includes server-only data. Scripts decide what happens and explicitly consume items.

properties.name: playerInventoryChanged
properties.description: An inventory changed. Raised on the next server tick in the order the changes happened, once per inventory an operation touched: a transfer raises it for both players. A handler may change inventories; those changes arrive on a later tick. Every change of a player who disconnects is raised before `playerDisconnect`. Save from here to keep inventories across sessions -- the server keeps nothing itself.

properties.name: playerItemUsed
properties.description:
The player's game spent items: ate, drank, applied or fired them. Raised after the `playerInventoryChanged` that removed them. `item` is the class GUID.

This is the player's own game saying so: the server checked that the units existed and were of a kind that can be spent that way, and took them, but did not see the meal or the shot. A handler that rewards a use -- a heal, a buff -- can be had for the price of the item.

type.name: [player: Player, item: string, kind: "food" | "potion" | "ointment" | "shot", amount: number]

properties.name: playerInventoryReady
properties.description: A player's game shows their inventory for the first time this session. Their inventory exists from `playerConnect`; restore a saved one there with `Inventory.set`, and it is what they load in with.

properties.name: horseIntentDone
properties.description: A move or patrol leg reached its destination, was blocked, or failed. Intermediate path corners do not emit this event.

properties.name: horseSpawn
properties.description: Dispatched immediately after a horse is created and replicated, whether by `Horse.spawn`, the `/horse` command, or anything else.

properties.name: horseDestroy
properties.description: Dispatched while a horse is being despawned, including the despawn its owner's disconnect implies. The handle still resolves, so its owner and name can be read one last time.

properties.name: horseOwnerChanged
properties.description: Dispatched after a horse is handed to another player, or left ownerless -- by `giveTo`, or by its owner disconnecting while `destroyWithOwner` is false.

properties.name: horseMount
properties.description: Dispatched after a player climbs into a saddle and the horse's authority has been handed to their client.

properties.name: horseDismount
properties.description: Dispatched after a rider leaves a saddle, including the dismount a disconnect implies, the one a destroyed or dead horse forces, and the one a rider's own death forces.

properties.name: horseMounting
properties.description:
Dispatched when a player has climbed into a saddle, before the server accepts it -- the place to decide who may ride which horse. Return `false` from a handler and the ride is refused: the player's client is told to get back off, and no `horseMount` follows. Handlers run synchronously, so the decision cannot wait on anything awaited.

The player's own game has already started the mount when this runs, so a refusal plays the get-off.

properties.name: horseDamage
properties.description: Dispatched when health comes off a horse: a blade, an arrow, a fall. The client running the horse reports it, because its copy of the animal is the one whose soul counts -- a blow resolved on the attacker's machine is handed to it first -- so `amount` is what was really taken. `attacker` is the player who dealt it, or null.

type.name: [horse: Horse, attacker: Player | null, amount: number, reason: "unknown" | "combat" | "gunshot" | "starvation" | "collision" | "scripted" | "disintegrate" | "fall" | "poison" | "bleeding" | "selfHarm"]

properties.name: horseDeath
properties.description: Dispatched once when a horse dies, whatever killed it: its body falls where it stood, and anyone in the saddle has already been taken off (with a `horseDismount`). `killer` is the player whose blow took the last of the health, or null. It follows the `horseDamage` of the blow that caused it: the client running the horse reports both, in that order.

properties.name: horseGearChanging
properties.description: Dispatched when a player has changed a horse's gear -- in the game's own horse inventory screen -- before the server accepts it. `gear` is what the horse would wear. Return `false` from a handler and the change is refused: every copy of the horse, the player's own included, is dressed back in what it wore before. Not dispatched while `gearLocked` is set, which refuses first, nor for a script's own `setGear`. Handlers run synchronously.

type.name: [horse: Horse, player: Player | null, gear: { saddle: string | null; head: string | null; torso: string | null; shoe: string | null }]

properties.name: horseGearChanged
properties.description: Dispatched after a horse's gear changed on every client. `player` is the rider who changed it, or null for a script.

type.name: [horse: Horse, player: Player | null, gear: { saddle: string | null; head: string | null; torso: string | null; shoe: string | null }]

properties.name: dialogueChoice
properties.description: Dispatched when a player picks an option. The option's own id comes back, never its index, so a handler stays correct when the page is rebuilt with different rows. Anything the option costs is checked here, not when the page was built: `enabled` on the wire is a rendering hint and the server is what decides.

properties.name: dialogueClosed
properties.description: Dispatched when a conversation ends, whoever ended it. 0 completed, 1 the player cancelled, 2 another conversation replaced it, 3 it was interrupted -- a disconnect, most often.

properties.name: vendorTrade
properties.description: Dispatched once a deal has settled: everything in it has already moved, in one commit on the player's inventory whose playerInventoryChanged reason is `trade`. `balance` is what the player came out with in money units -- positive when the vendor paid them. What the player sold does not join the vendor's stock; add it with `setStock` here if this vendor resells.

type.name: [vendor: number, player: Player, bought: VendorTradeLine[], sold: VendorTradeLine[], balance: number]

properties.name: vendorClosed
properties.description: Dispatched when a trading session ends, whoever ended it. 0 the player closed the screen, 1 the server closed it, 2 another vendor replaced it, 3 the client could not bring the screen up, 4 the player left.

properties.name: playerPickpocketStart
properties.description:
Dispatched when a player's charge begins on the game's own Rob entry against another player, before the victim's pockets are opened to them -- the place to decide who may rob whom. Return `false` from a handler and the attempt is refused: the thief's minigame ends before its loot screen opens, and nothing else follows. Handlers run synchronously, so the decision cannot wait on anything awaited.

Whether the victim notices is the game's own rule, played on the thief's machine against the victim's body: it turns on the victim's facing and on both players' skills, exactly as against an NPC.

properties.name: playerPickpocketed
properties.description: Dispatched once a theft has settled: everything in `items` has already left the victim and reached the thief. The thief's loot screen is only a claim -- each line was taken from the victim first and only what really came out was handed over -- so `items` can be shorter than what the thief took, or empty when they closed the screen with nothing. Nothing else happens to either player: whether this is a crime, and what it costs, is the gamemode's.

properties.name: playerPickpocketCaught
properties.description: Dispatched when the victim noticed the thief, while charging or with the loot screen up. Nothing was taken, and no NPC reacts on the victim's behalf: the gamemode decides what being caught means.

properties.name: diceTurnStart
properties.description: A new turn begins, including turns after automatic busts.

properties.name: diceRoll
properties.description: The server dealt a roll. Includes all six face values and the mask rolled this time. When `player` is the NPC on the second seat and `reason` is `rolled`, the decision is the script's: answer with Dice.move.

properties.name: diceMove
properties.description: The server accepted Continue or Pass, from a player or through Dice.move. Invalid or repeated requests emit nothing.

properties.name: diceTurnEnd
properties.description: A turn ended by banking, busting, winning, or a match ending. A round means one player's turn.

properties.name: diceMatchStart
properties.description: Dispatched once a match has started and its players have been sent to the table. `second` is the Npc when one holds the second seat. Which seat throws first is drawn at random.

type.name: [match: number, first: Player, second: Player | Npc, targetScore: number]

properties.name: diceMatchEnd
properties.description: Dispatched once a match is over and both players have been told. `winner` is 0 when `first` won, 1 when `second` did, 255 when nobody did. `reason` is `won` (a seat banked the target score), `gaveUp` (a player left the table), `left` (a player disconnected, or the NPC was removed or died), `timedOut` (the seat to throw, player or NPC, did not move for three minutes), `failed` (a client could not play the table) or `stopped` (`Dice.stop`). A player or NPC who has gone since is null. Nothing changes hands on its own: what a match was played for is the gamemode's to settle here.

type.name: [match: number, first: Player | null, second: Player | Npc | null, winner: number, reason: string, firstScore: number, secondScore: number]

properties.name: craftingRefunding
properties.description: Synchronous decision before an unfinished craft settles, including when no native refund is due. Call refund() to request a full refund; return values are ignored. No handler or no call preserves native rules. JavaScript exceptions are logged and do not cancel a call already made. The callback expires on return; delayed calls do nothing. The `cancelled`, `interrupted` and `clientError` reasons are reported by the player's own client: a modified client can send any of them, so refunding on one lets that client keep its materials. Never grants a completed craft twice. craftingEnded follows the actual inventory changes.

properties.name: craftingStarting
properties.description: A player asks to open an alchemy table, or to begin a smithing recipe. Every handler runs; one returning literal `false` refuses it. An async handler cannot refuse.

properties.name: craftingStarted
properties.description: A batch is brewing, or a workpiece took its materials.

properties.name: craftingCompleting
properties.description: A batch or workpiece finished and its result is computed. Every handler runs; one returning literal `false` refuses it: alchemy ends the batch as failed, what was spent stays spent, and nothing is granted; smithing fails the workpiece, spending its failure share.

properties.name: craftingCompleted
properties.description: A result was granted, followed by `craftingEnded`. Raised after the `playerInventoryChanged` it caused.

properties.name: craftingEnded
properties.description: A batch or workpiece is over. Raised after the `playerInventoryChanged` of any refund.

properties.name: dogSpawn
properties.description: Dispatched immediately after a dog is created and replicated, whether by `Dog.spawn` or anything else.

properties.name: dogDestroy
properties.description: Dispatched while a dog is being despawned. The handle still resolves, so its owner and name can be read one last time.

properties.name: dogOwnerChanged
properties.description: Dispatched after a dog is handed to another player, or left masterless.

properties.name: dogModeChanged
properties.description: Dispatched after a dog's companion mode actually changes.

properties.name: propSpawn
properties.description: Dispatched immediately after a prop is created and replicated, whether by `Prop.spawn`, the `/prop` command, or anything else.

properties.name: propDestroy
properties.description: Dispatched while a prop is being despawned. The handle still resolves, so its model and its pose can be read one last time.

properties.name: propRest
properties.description: Dispatched when a `rigid` prop's body stops moving, whatever moved it: a script's `applyImpulse`, `setVelocity`, `wake` or `sleep`, a fall, or a player walking into it. The client simulating it says where, and every player already sees it there. This is that client's word, checked only to lie within 100 m of where the prop last rested or was spawned; a prop reported farther is put back there and raises nothing.

properties.name: cartSpawn
properties.description: Dispatched immediately after a cart is created and replicated, whether by `Cart.spawn`, the `/cart` command, or anything else.

properties.name: cartDestroy
properties.description: Dispatched while a cart is being despawned, after everyone in it has been let out. The handle still resolves, so its blueprint and its pose can be read one last time.

properties.name: cartEntering
properties.description: Dispatched before a player is put in a seat -- by their own use of the cart's prompt, or `putPlayer`. Return `false` from a handler and the seat is refused: nothing changes, and the player's game never climbs in. Handlers run synchronously.

properties.name: cartEnter
properties.description: Dispatched after a player is given a seat, named as in `cart.seats`; the `driver` seat's client runs the cart from here on.

type.name: [cart: Cart, player: Player | null, seat: string]

properties.name: cartExit
properties.description: Dispatched after a player leaves a seat: their own climb down, `removePlayer`, a disconnect, or the cart being destroyed.

type.name: [cart: Cart, player: Player | null, seat: string]

properties.name: vfxSpawn
properties.description: Dispatched immediately after a replicated particle effect is placed, whether by `Vfx.spawn`, a command, or anything else.

properties.name: vfxDestroy
properties.description: Dispatched while a replicated particle effect is being stopped. The handle still resolves, so its name and its pose can be read one last time.

properties.name: markerPlace
properties.description: Dispatched immediately after a ground marker is drawn, whether by `Marker.place`, a command, or anything else.

properties.name: markerRemove
properties.description: Dispatched while a ground marker is being removed. The handle still resolves, so its material and its pose can be read one last time.

properties.name: markerEnter
properties.description: Dispatched when a player walks into a marker whose `trigger` is on. The client detects the crossing and the server confirms it against the position it already replicates, so a claim it does not agree with never reaches here.

properties.name: markerExit
properties.description: Dispatched when a player walks out of a marker whose `trigger` is on. Not raised when the marker is removed, when `trigger` is turned off, or when the player leaves the world -- none of those is the player walking out.

properties.name: npcSpawn
properties.description: Dispatched immediately after an NPC is spawned or adopted, whether by `Npc.create`, a command, or anything else.

properties.name: npcInventoryReady
properties.description: Its initial inventory has been established. The default stock is censused once by its elected simulator; Inventory.set establishes authored stock immediately.

properties.name: npcHarvested
properties.description: An accepted butchering completion. The prepopulated stock is now accessible and every client applies the butchered appearance. Emitted once per life; save Inventory.get(npc) here too to persist the harvested flag.

properties.name: npcInventoryChanged
properties.description: Committed stock changes, including loot transfers. Save this stock and restore it with Inventory.set. Harvest completion is reported by npcHarvested.

properties.name: npcDestroy
properties.description: Dispatched while an NPC is being despawned. The handle still resolves, so what it was and where it stood can be read one last time.

properties.name: npcIntentDone
properties.description: Dispatched once when an NPC finishes what it was told to do. `status` is `reached` when it arrived, `blocked` when it could not make progress, or `failed` when the order could not be carried out at all, or when a patrol gives up. Server-planned intermediate corners do not raise this event, and neither does a change of simulator: a finished order is not reported twice. A follow, which never finishes, raises `reached` the first time it catches up and again only after a change of simulator. A patrol steps on this event, so a handler that re-orders the NPC here replaces the route rather than racing it.

properties.name: npcDamage
properties.description: Dispatched after health came off the ledger. For melee, the victim's simulator resolves the native hit and the server checks the accepted swing before changing health. `amount` is what was actually taken.

type.name: [npc: Npc, attacker: Player | Npc | null, amount: number]

properties.name: npcDeath
properties.description: Dispatched when the last of an NPC's health goes. The body stays as a corpse and the handle keeps resolving.

properties.name: npcRevive
properties.description: Dispatched when a dead NPC is brought back. Every client makes a new body for it.

properties.name: npcAnimationEnd
properties.description: Dispatched once when the animation a `playAnimation` request started is over; `fragment` is the request's. `reason` is `finished`, `interrupted`, `refused`, `stopped` or `replaced`, as for `playerAnimationEnd`. The first three come from the client simulating the NPC. One that nobody simulates plays nothing, so its one-shot ends `refused` as soon as it is asked for, and one cut off by a change of simulator ends `interrupted`: the new simulator does not replay what it did not see start.

properties.name: npcInteract
properties.description: Dispatched when a player presses use on an NPC whose `interactable` is on. The client reports the press and the server confirms the distance against the position it already replicates, so a claim it does not agree with never reaches here.

properties.name: npcSimulatorChange
properties.description: Dispatched when the client running an NPC changes -- somebody walked into range, out of it, or disconnected. `player` is null when it went dormant. Nothing about the NPC changes with it: intent, ledger and identity are the server's, and the new simulator re-derives from them.

properties.name: patrolWaypoint
properties.description: One accepted waypoint outcome; intermediate path corners do not emit it.

properties.name: patrolFinished
properties.description: A patrol ended, failed, or was replaced. Edits to its definition do not replace its snapshot.

properties.name: questTrackingChanged
properties.description: Dispatched when a player starts or stops following a quest in the game's journal, whichever way it happened: the track button, the game auto-tracking a quest that turns active, or the untrack that follows finishing or failing one. The client reports it -- following a quest is decided there and cannot be refused here -- so a handler reacts rather than vetoes. It fires only on an actual change, and only for a quest that player was given.

properties.name: groundItemSpawn
properties.description: Dispatched immediately after a stack is laid in the world and replicated, whether by `GroundItem.spawn`, the `/drop` command, or a player dropping something from their own inventory.

properties.name: groundItemDestroy
properties.description: Dispatched while a stack is being taken out of the world, including the removal a completed pickup performs. The handle still resolves, so its item and its pose can be read one last time.

properties.name: groundItemPickup
properties.description: Dispatched when a player's pickup has been granted and the stack is about to go, so what was taken and by whom can both still be read. It reports a pickup rather than deciding one -- the server has already told that client the stack is theirs by the time this is raised -- and `groundItemDestroy` follows it.

properties.name: gatheringHarvest
properties.description: A player picked a plant within their reach, and the server is about to give them the herb. Return false to refuse it: nothing is given and the plants stay. The proposal is frozen; every handler runs whatever an earlier one returned, and an async handler cannot refuse.

properties.name: gatheringHarvested
properties.description: A player was given a herb, after the `playerInventoryChanged` it caused. The plant and the same-kind plants harvested with it are picked for everyone in the virtual world until timed or scripted regrowth; nothing about them survives a restart.

properties.name: doorInteract
properties.description:
Dispatched when a player's client reports working a door, before the server applies it. `action` is `open`, `close`, `unlock` or `lockpick`; a key turned in the same use as the push arrives as `unlock` and then `open`, and refusing the `unlock` refuses the report without asking about the `open`. `keySide` says whether the player stood on the side with the keyhole, which is where an unlock needs a key.

Return false to refuse it: the door is put back on every client, the player's included, and nobody else sees it happen. Every handler runs whatever an earlier one returned, and an async handler cannot refuse. The server has already refused what the game's own rules forbid -- a player out of reach, a door the server locked, opening a locked door, picking a door with no keyhole, a door a script made unusable -- so this only sees what the game would allow.

The player's own client moves the door as soon as they use it and reports afterwards, so a refusal here reaches them a round trip later, as the door swinging back. It is the authority, for what only the server knows and for a client that ignored its own rules. To refuse without that, set `door.usable`, or refuse in the client's own `doorInteract`: both stop the use on the player's machine before anything moves.

type.name: [player: Player, door: Door, action: "open" | "close" | "unlock" | "lockpick", keySide: boolean]

properties.name: siegeEngineSpawn
properties.description: Dispatched immediately after a siege engine is built.

properties.name: siegeEngineDestroy
properties.description: Dispatched while a siege engine is being removed. The handle still resolves.

properties.name: siegeEngineReady
properties.description: Dispatched when an engine's load cycle finishes and it can fire.

properties.name: siegeEngineUse
properties.description: Dispatched when a player asks something of a `usable` engine, standing at it: to take its place (`operate`) or a free winch (`winch`) from the game's own prompt, or -- in its place -- to `load` it or `fire` it where they laid it, with the player as the attacker. Return false to refuse. `leave` reports a player stepping away from either and cannot be refused. A handler that works the engine itself should refuse, so it is not worked twice.

properties.name: siegeEngineDamage
properties.description: Dispatched when a blast takes `amount` off an engine with a `maxHealth`, before it is wrecked by it. `health` already reads what is left.

type.name: [engine: SiegeEngine, amount: number, attacker: Player | null]

properties.name: siegeEngineWreck
properties.description: Dispatched when an engine's health runs out. Its operator and crew have been let go, and a stone still in its sling went down with it.

properties.name: siegeFire
properties.description: Dispatched the moment an engine lets its projectile go, partway through the shot `fire` started.

type.name: [engine: SiegeEngine, attacker: Player | null, target: Vector3]

properties.name: siegeImpact
properties.description: Dispatched where a projectile came down: what the reporting player -- the attacker when near enough, else whoever is nearest the target -- saw it hit, checked against the arc it was thrown on, or the target itself when nobody could see it. Players within `damageRadius` have already been told to take their share, and NPCs have taken theirs. `engine` is null when it was destroyed while the stone was in the air.

type.name: [engine: SiegeEngine | null, position: Vector3, attacker: Player | null]

properties.name: siegeLadderSpawn
properties.description: Dispatched immediately after a siege ladder is placed.

properties.name: siegeLadderDestroy
properties.description: Dispatched while a siege ladder is being removed. The handle still resolves.

properties.name: siegeLadderUse
properties.description: Dispatched when a player asks to push a `usable` ladder from the walk at its top, or to raise a fallen one from beside its foot. Return false to refuse.

properties.name: siegeLadderFall
properties.description: Dispatched when a pushed ladder hits the ground. Anyone who was on it was thrown off as it began to fall, and took the game's own fall.

properties.name: siegeLadderRaise
properties.description: Dispatched when a raised ladder leans on its wall again and can be climbed.

properties.name: stonePileSpawn
properties.description: Dispatched immediately after a stone pile is placed.

properties.name: stonePileDestroy
properties.description: Dispatched while a stone pile is being removed. The handle still resolves.

properties.name: stonePileThrow
properties.description: Dispatched when a player takes a stone off a pile. The game's own stone throwing has already lifted it and heaves it over the wall at once, so it cannot be refused; make the pile not `usable` to stop the next one.

properties.name: stoneImpact
properties.description: Dispatched where a thrown stone first met something, as its thrower saw it, checked to lie within 30 m of its pile. Players within the pile's `damageRadius` have been told to take their share, and NPCs have taken theirs.

type.name: [pile: StonePile | null, position: Vector3, attacker: Player]

properties.name: areaEnter
properties.description: Dispatched when a body comes to be inside an enabled area: it walked or rode in, or the area was created, moved, reshaped or enabled around it. The server decides this itself from the pose it already replicates, by the game's own rule for that kind of area, so a client cannot claim it. `matchingVirtualWorld` is false when a script area bound to one world is crossed by a body in another; a level area is in every world.

type.name: [area: Area, entity: Player | Horse | Cart | Npc, matchingVirtualWorld: boolean]

properties.name: areaExit
properties.description: Dispatched when a body stops being inside an area: it walked out, or the area was moved, reshaped, disabled or destroyed. A body that leaves the server entirely -- a player disconnecting, a horse despawned -- raises nothing here; its own event already says it is gone.

type.name: [area: Area, entity: Player | Horse | Cart | Npc, matchingVirtualWorld: boolean]

properties.name: worldResourcesReady
properties.description: Raised once after every configured world export has loaded successfully, including an empty list. WorldResource.ready is true inside the handler. A script starting later must check WorldResource.ready first; the event is not replayed. Do not await this event inside resourceStart: exports load after script startup. Handler promises are not awaited.

properties.name: stashSpawn
properties.description: A container now exists: a scripted chest, a virtual stash, or one the level places, built in a virtual world the first time anything there asked for it. Every container starts empty; restore saved contents here with `setInventory`. The level's containers in the global world are built before any resource runs, so restore those from `resourceStart` by walking `Stash.all()`.

properties.name: stashOpen
properties.description: A player holds a container view. Physical chests report the native opening; virtual stashes report the server grant before requesting the native screen.

properties.name: stashClose
properties.description: A player no longer has a container open: they closed it, walked away, died or changed world (`lostAccess`), sent nothing for two minutes, left, or the container went.

properties.name: stashInventoryChanged
properties.description: What a container holds changed. `player` moved the units -- `change.reason` is `deposit` or `withdraw`, and their inventory raises `playerInventoryChanged` too -- or is null for a script's `addItem`, `removeItem` or `setInventory`, or `destroy` when the container went with something in it. Save from here to keep contents across restarts: the server keeps nothing itself. A linked child's `stash` is the one the player used; its stock is its master's.

type.name: [stash: Stash, player: Player | null, change: InventoryChange]

properties.name: stashDestroy
properties.description: A container is about to go. Raised after its close and its contents' removal, while it can still be read.

properties.name: stashInteract
properties.description:
Dispatched for a physical chest prompt or virtual stash open(player), before access is granted. For a prompt: the player's client holds the game's own handler until the server answers. `action` is `open`, `unlock` -- a key turned, which opens it in the same use -- or `lockpick`, the minigame starting; a successful pick then opens it without asking again.

Return false to refuse it: the prompt does nothing, and no transfer screen, key or minigame ever appears. Every handler runs whatever an earlier one returned, and an async handler cannot refuse. The server has already refused what the game's own rules forbid -- a player out of reach, a container another player has open, opening a locked one, picking one that cannot be -- so this only sees what the game would allow. Virtual opening has no distance check; world, player readiness, lock and exclusive access checks still apply. Closing is never asked.

properties.name: playerChat
properties.description: Dispatched when a player submits a plain chat line. Turn `Chat.setDefaultRelay(false)` off to own delivery yourself.

properties.name: playerCommand
properties.description: Dispatched when a player's chat line begins with `/` and no built-in command claimed it. A `/` line is never relayed to anyone else.

properties.name: worldDayChange
properties.description: Dispatched when the world clock crosses midnight, whether it walked over or `World.setTime` jumped past. The day it carries is the one that just began.

properties.name: worldWeatherChange
properties.description: Dispatched when the sky starts blending to another time-of-day preset, from `World.setWeather` or the `/world weather` command. It is raised when the blend starts, not when it settles.

properties.name: playerWeaponHit
properties.description: Dispatched when a player's swing meets something solid that is not a body: a tree, a wall, a rock, a prop, the ground. Once per thing per attack, at the first contact, as the game itself counts it. `hit` is named as a trace names it -- `category` tells a tree from a rock, and `levelObject` is what `LevelEdit.apply` takes to fell or break it -- with `distance` measured from the player's feet. It is that player's client's word, checked only to lie within 8 m of them and in the server's level, and at most 16 a second are taken from one player. Fists and kicks are not reported, and neither is a blow on a player, an NPC or an animal, which `playerHit` and the damage events cover.

properties.name: playerCustomBuffApply
properties.description: A native custom effect instance attached. A refresh and each additional stack raise this event after the owner reports them.

properties.name: playerCustomBuffTick
properties.description: A reported active custom effect reached its tickInterval on the server clock. At most one callback per instance per server update; missed ticks are skipped. Native modifiers and duration use the owner's simulation clock.

properties.name: playerCustomBuffRemove
properties.description: One custom instance left the body. Expired also covers native removal. Disconnect clears lifecycle callbacks for this connection.

properties.name: playerBuffAdded
properties.description: Dispatched when a status effect appears on a player's body. `source` says whether this server added it; `native` means the game did -- a potion they drank, an injury they took. It fires for whatever they are already carrying when their client first reports in, so a handler sees the full picture without asking for it.

properties.name: playerBuffRemoved
properties.description: Dispatched when a status effect leaves a player's body. `server` is a removal this server asked for; `expired` is everything else -- it ran out, or the game replaced it. Effect timers run on each player's own machine, so the server never expires one itself.

properties.name: playerBuffBlocked
properties.description: Dispatched when the game tried to give a player an effect of a kind this server claimed, and their client turned it down. This is the other half of `Buffs.claim`: the drink was still drunk and the item still consumed, so the handler decides what really happens -- usually `player.addBuff` with the resource's own rule applied. Nothing raises it until something is claimed, and repeats of the same effect are limited to twice a second per player.

properties.name: playerXpGaining
properties.description: Dispatched when a player's own game produced XP -- a hit landed, a lock picked, a page read -- and asks for it. Return `false` to refuse it; the gain then never happens. `xp` is before this server's rate and the player's own multipliers. `source` is the game's name for what caused it: `Attack`, `LockpickingResult` and so on, or empty. Nothing is asked while `Progression.setNativeXp(false)` is in force.

type.name: [player: Player, track: string, xp: number, source: string]

properties.name: playerXpGained
properties.description: Dispatched when XP landed on a player's character, from their game or from this server, after every multiplier.

properties.name: playerLevelUp
properties.description: Dispatched when one of a player's tracks reaches a new level. `perkPoints` is what that track's tree now has unspent.

type.name: [player: Player, track: string, level: number, perkPoints: number]

properties.name: playerPerkLearning
properties.description: Dispatched when a player confirmed a perk on the perk screen and every rule of the game allows it: the tree's level, the parent perk, the exclusive partner, a point to spend, and this server's block list. Return `false` to refuse it; the point is not spent and their client raises `progressionPerkRefused`.

properties.name: playerPerkAdded
properties.description: Dispatched when a perk appeared on a player's character: learnt on the perk screen, given by this server, or granted by the game on its own -- a codex entry, a recipe, a combat move it teaches.

properties.name: playerPerkRemoved
properties.description: Dispatched when a perk left a player's character: taken or respecced by this server, or removed by the game.

properties.name: playerProgressionRejected
properties.description: Dispatched when a player's client reported progression this server never ordered: a track that rose further than any gain it granted could take it, or a perk-screen perk nobody learnt. The report is kept -- the game has no way to take a level back -- so what happens to the player is the handler's call; a kick is the usual answer.

properties.name: resourceStart
properties.description: Dispatched after a resource entry point has run and immediately before the resource becomes running.

properties.name: resourceStop
properties.description: Dispatched while a resource is stopping, before its stop callback, timers, exports and event handlers are cleaned up.

properties.name: entityStateChange
properties.description: Dispatched when one key of an entity's state changes: on the server when a script writes it, on a client when the write arrives. `value` is undefined when the key was removed and `previous` is undefined when it held nothing before, so a stored null stays distinguishable from an absent key. The entity is whatever the game's WrapScriptEntity answers, and the base Entity handle by default.

type.name: [entity: Entity, key: string, value: any, previous: any]

properties.name: consoleCommand
properties.description: Dispatched for a line typed into the server console that no built-in command (help, ensure, refresh, ...) claimed. `args` is the rest of the line, split on whitespace. The console is the operator's, so this is the place for commands no player may run.

properties.name: playerConnecting
properties.description: Dispatched when a player asks to join, before the connection exists: they hold no player slot, are not counted as online, and are sent nothing -- no resource list, no download, no body. The request waits until every handler has returned and every Promise a handler returned has settled, then it is let in if a player slot is free (otherwise it is refused as full). `connection.reject()` turns it away instead, and so does a handler that throws or rejects, or handlers that have not settled within the server's admission timeout (30 seconds by default, restarted by every `connection.update()`). With no handler at all, every request is let in at once.

symbols.name: PlayerStat
symbols.description: Writable player stats, in native units. Use getStat and the server's setStat.

properties.name: Health
properties.description: Current health, in native units. Zero can kill.

properties.name: Stamina
properties.description: Current stamina; the game continues spending and regenerating it.

properties.name: Exhaust
properties.description: Current energy reserve; higher means better rested.

properties.name: Hunger
properties.description: Current nourishment; higher means better fed.

symbols.name: DerivedPlayerStat
symbols.description: Read-only computed player stats. Use getDerivedStat; these values cannot be passed to setStat.

properties.name: Bleeding
properties.description: Total bleeding strength.

properties.name: Sleeping
properties.description: Sleepiness; above zero means asleep.

properties.name: Consciousness
properties.description: Consciousness; zero means knocked out.

properties.name: Drunkenness
properties.description: Native drunkenness value.

properties.name: Poisoning
properties.description: Native poisoning value; not every named poison changes this value.

properties.name: Charisma
properties.description: Effective charisma.

properties.name: Visibility
properties.description: Effective visibility.

properties.name: Conspicuousness
properties.description: Effective conspicuousness.

properties.name: Noise
properties.description: Effective noise.

properties.name: Dirtiness
properties.description: Native dirtiness reading; reading it does not clean the body or equipment.

properties.name: Bloodiness
properties.description: Native bloodiness reading.

properties.name: Smell
properties.description: Native smell reading.

properties.name: SmellIntensity
properties.description: Native smell intensity.

properties.name: Fragrance
properties.description: Native fragrance reading.

properties.name: CarriedWeight
properties.description: Carried weight in the same units as InventoryCapacity.

properties.name: InventoryCapacity
properties.description: Native carrying capacity, including applicable equipment effects.

properties.name: Encumbrance
properties.description: Native encumbrance reading.

properties.name: Hangover
properties.description: Native hangover reading.

properties.name: Alcoholism
properties.description: Computed alcoholism reading, not the persistent soul resource.

properties.name: ArmorRating
properties.description: Effective armor rating.

properties.name: OverallArmorDefense
properties.description: Overall armor defense.

properties.name: OverallWeaponAttack
properties.description: Overall weapon attack.

properties.name: NormalizedRunSpeed
properties.description: Normalized run speed; not world-space velocity.

properties.name: RunSpeedBase
properties.description: Native base run speed.

properties.name: Morale
properties.description: Native morale reading.

symbols.name: Appearance
symbols.description:
How a player's body looks: four of the game's own character-component names, and the gender whose catalog they come from.

A part left out, or set to an empty string, means "leave that one alone" -- the body keeps whatever it would have had. An appearance with every part empty is the default body, which is what everyone wears until something chooses otherwise.

properties.name: gender
properties.description: Which half of the game's character-component tree the four names come from. Not one of the four: a body's gender comes from its soul, and a name from one tree means nothing under the other, so this travels with them and is applied first.

properties.name: body
properties.description: The skin: complexion and build. One of `Appearances.options("body", gender)`, or empty.

properties.name: head
properties.description: The face. One of `Appearances.options("head", gender)`, or empty.

properties.name: hair
properties.description: The hairstyle, including its colour -- the game ships each style recoloured rather than colouring one. One of `Appearances.options("hair", gender)`, or empty.

properties.name: beard
properties.description:
The beard. Male only -- the female tree has none -- and one of `Appearances.beards(head)`, or empty.

Not every beard goes with every face: they are modelled per head, and a body asked for a pair that was never modelled refuses the whole appearance rather than quietly losing the beard.

symbols.name: AppearanceOption
symbols.description: One entry of the game's character-component tree: something a body can be given for one part.

properties.name: name
properties.description: What to put in the part. This is the game's own node name.

properties.name: part
properties.description: Which part it fills.

properties.name: gender
properties.description: Which tree it came out of. An option is only valid on a body of the same gender.

properties.name: group
properties.description: The option this one is a variation of, or null when it stands on its own. The game ships a hairstyle once per colour, all derived from the same style node, so grouping by this is what turns 262 hairstyles into a list somebody can read.

symbols.name: SoulStats
symbols.description: The three character attributes a body's soul carries, in the game's own units.

properties.name: strength
properties.description: Attribute value, or 0 while the body has published no soul.

properties.name: agility
properties.description: Attribute value, or 0 while the body has published no soul.

properties.name: vitality
properties.description: Attribute value, or 0 while the body has published no soul.

symbols.name: SoulSkills
symbols.description: The nine skills a hit or a draw is evaluated against, in the game's own units.

properties.name: fencing
properties.description: Skill level, or 0 while the body has published no soul.

properties.name: survival
properties.description: Skill level, or 0 while the body has published no soul.

properties.name: defense
properties.description: Skill level, or 0 while the body has published no soul.

properties.name: sword
properties.description: Skill level, or 0 while the body has published no soul.

properties.name: heavyWeapons
properties.description: Skill level, or 0 while the body has published no soul.

properties.name: marksmanship
properties.description: Skill level, or 0 while the body has published no soul.

properties.name: dagger
properties.description: Skill level, or 0 while the body has published no soul.

properties.name: largeWeapons
properties.description: Skill level, or 0 while the body has published no soul.

properties.name: unarmed
properties.description: Skill level, or 0 while the body has published no soul.

symbols.name: TrackInfo
symbols.description: One skill or stat a player levels, as the game's own tables describe it.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The name every progression verb takes, as the game's tables spell it: `weapon_sword`, `thievery`, `strength`.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: Whether it is a skill or one of the stats the skills sit on.

properties.name: cap
properties.description: The highest level the game lets it reach.

properties.name: induced
properties.description: True for fencing alone: it is never earned, the game derives it from the five weapon skills, so XP handed to it is refused.

symbols.name: PerkInfo
symbols.description: One perk, as the game's own perk tables describe it.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The perk's `perk_name`, unique across the tables, and the spelling every perk verb takes alongside its GUID.

properties.name: id
properties.description: The perk's GUID.

properties.name: uiName
properties.description: The localisation key the perk screen shows, or empty for a perk it never shows.

properties.name: track
properties.description: The track whose points pay for it: a track name, `main` for the main-level bank, or null for a perk no player's tree carries.

properties.name: level
properties.description: The level that track has to reach before the perk can be learnt. 0 for none.

properties.name: parent
properties.description: The perk that has to be owned first, or null.

properties.name: visibility
properties.description: `visible` perks are the ones on the perk screen and the only ones a player can learn; `hidden` ones appear once something grants them; `system` ones implement game features and are never shown.

properties.name: kinds
properties.description: What the perk does when owned, from the game's side tables: `buff` (a real status effect), `script`, `technique` (a combat move), `ability`, `param` (rewrites a game rule), `companion` (the dog), `recipe`, `codex`. Empty for a perk that only gates others.

properties.name: autolearnable
properties.description: Whether the game grants it on its own once its requirements are met, rather than on the perk screen.

symbols.name: TrackProgress
symbols.description: Where a player stands on one track.

properties.name: level
properties.description: The level reached.

properties.name: xp
properties.description: XP earned towards the next level, in the game's own units.

properties.name: xpToNext
properties.description: XP the next level costs in total, from the start of this one. `xp / xpToNext` is the bar the character sheet draws.

properties.name: perkPoints
properties.description: Unspent perk points in this track's tree.

symbols.name: TrackLevels
symbols.description: A player's level on every track, keyed by track name.

properties.name: stealth
properties.description: The level reached.

properties.name: horse_riding
properties.description: The level reached.

properties.name: fencing
properties.description: The level reached.

properties.name: thievery
properties.description: The level reached.

properties.name: alchemy
properties.description: The level reached.

properties.name: craftsmanship
properties.description: The level reached.

properties.name: drinking
properties.description: The level reached.

properties.name: survival
properties.description: The level reached.

properties.name: weapon_sword
properties.description: The level reached.

properties.name: heavy_weapons
properties.description: The level reached.

properties.name: marksmanship
properties.description: The level reached.

properties.name: weapon_large
properties.description: The level reached.

properties.name: weapon_unarmed
properties.description: The level reached.

properties.name: scholarship
properties.description: The level reached.

properties.name: houndmaster
properties.description: The level reached.

properties.name: strength
properties.description: The level reached.

properties.name: agility
properties.description: The level reached.

properties.name: vitality
properties.description: The level reached.

properties.name: speech
properties.description: The level reached.

properties.name: prestige
properties.description: The level reached.

symbols.name: ProgressionSnapshot
symbols.description: Everything a server needs to put a player's progression back: plain JSON a resource can store however it likes. A player starts every session with a fresh character, so this is how progression outlives a disconnect.

properties.name: tracks
properties.description: Level and XP into the next level, per track name.

properties.name: perks
properties.description: Every perk owned, by name.

properties.name: perkPoints
properties.description: Unspent points per tree: track names, and `main`.

symbols.name: MovementMode
symbols.description: The pace rule a server puts on one player. Both halves default to off, and a call to `setMovementMode` states both of them.

properties.name: walkByDefault
properties.description: Whether walking, rather than jogging, is the pace this player keeps coming back to. A preference: they start each body walking and return to it after every sprint, and their own toggle key works normally in between.

properties.name: walkEnforced
properties.description: Whether this player may not run or sprint at all. A rule rather than a preference: it holds the engine's own movement permissions, so the toggle key and the sprint key both stop raising the pace, and lifting it hands back whatever the body had before.

symbols.name: DamagePasses
symbols.description: One number per damage type a blow is worked out in. A blade's stab, slash and smash are priced separately and added; a blow runs only the passes its attack and weapon call for.

properties.name: stab
properties.description: The stab pass.

properties.name: slash
properties.description: The slash pass.

properties.name: smash
properties.description: The smash pass.

symbols.name: PlayerHitModifiers
symbols.description: Scales a `playerHit` handler puts on the server's price of a melee blow, each 1 until a handler changes it. The server works the blow out again with them, step by step as the game does: a heavier attack has to get through the same armour and the same block, so doubling `attack` does not simply double the damage. Never negative.

properties.name: attack
properties.description: Scales the attacker's attack in every pass, after their weapon, strength, skill and the swing itself.

properties.name: defense
properties.description: Scales the victim's armour where the blow landed.

properties.name: block
properties.description: Scales what the victim's block put up. Nothing for a blow that was not blocked.

properties.name: health
properties.description: Scales the health the blow takes, once everything else is worked out. The game's own cap of 200 a blow is applied before it, so this can go past it.

symbols.name: PlayerHit
symbols.description: A player or NPC blow, as `playerHit` shows it before the referee rules. `damage` is what the blow will take and `modifiers` scale how the server works it out; a handler may change either, from any resource, and the next handler sees the change. Every other field describes what happened and is read-only in effect. It is live only while the handlers run: one kept for later reads `damage` and `modifiers` as undefined and changes nothing.

properties.name: damage
properties.description: Health the blow takes. For melee between players the server works it out itself, the way the game does, from the attacker's weapon and its wear, both players' strength and skills, the armour the victim wears where it landed, the block and the perks and buffs it can vouch for; for NPC melee or an arrow it is what the victim's own game worked out. Set it and it stands as set: `modifiers` are then ignored. Never negative.

properties.name: engineDamage
properties.description: Health the game itself took for the blow on the machine that saw it land. Matches `damage` unless a perk that depends on the moment -- a heavy weapon's, a first strike's -- was in play, which the server leaves out.

properties.name: priced
properties.description: Whether the server worked `damage` out itself: true for a swing, false for an arrow.

properties.name: weapon
properties.description: The attacker's weapon as 32 hex digits, or null for a bare hand.

properties.name: attack
properties.description: The attacker's attack in each pass, after the swing's own strength and before `modifiers`.

properties.name: armor
properties.description: The victim's armour in each pass where the blow landed, before `modifiers`.

properties.name: blockDefense
properties.description: What the victim's block put up, or 0 when nothing blocked it.

properties.name: bodyPartCoefficient
properties.description: How much the place it landed multiplies the damage by: 1.5 for the head, 1 for the torso, 0.7 for a limb.

properties.name: modifiers
properties.description: Scales on the server's price; see `PlayerHitModifiers`. Ignored for an arrow.

properties.name: stamina
properties.description: Stamina the blow cost the victim. Already spent: stamina decides their next block, which cannot wait for a ruling.

properties.name: bodyPart
properties.description: The limb it landed on, or null for none in particular.

properties.name: reason
properties.description: The game's own reason for the damage: `combat` for a blade or a bow.

properties.name: source
properties.description: Whether it was a swing or an arrow.

properties.name: blocked
properties.description: The victim's block caught it.

properties.name: perfectBlock
properties.description: The victim's perfect block caught it. The game takes nothing for one.

properties.name: blockBroken
properties.description: The victim's block gave way under it.

symbols.name: Injuries
symbols.description: Which of a player's limbs carry an injury, one flag per limb. An injury is the game's own: it lowers the stamina ceiling (`healthyStamina`), can bleed, and heals slowly by itself or at once with a bandage or `player.heal`.

properties.name: head
properties.description: Whether the head is injured.

properties.name: torso
properties.description: Whether the torso is injured.

properties.name: leftArm
properties.description: Whether the left arm is injured.

properties.name: rightArm
properties.description: Whether the right arm is injured.

properties.name: leftLeg
properties.description: Whether the left leg is injured.

properties.name: rightLeg
properties.description: Whether the right leg is injured.

symbols.name: Player
symbols.description: A connected KCDC player and the body they occupy.

constructor.name: constructor
constructor.description: Creates a script wrapper for an existing connected player with this ID; it neither connects nor spawns anyone.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

functions.name: toString
functions.description: Formats this player handle for logging and debugging.

returns.description: The player's network entity ID and nickname.

functions.name: getStat
functions.description: Reads the latest reported stat in native units. Returns zero when no valid body snapshot exists; check player.ready to distinguish that from a real zero. Throws for an unknown stat or invalid arguments.

parameters.name: stat
parameters.description: A PlayerStat value.

functions.name: getDerivedStat
functions.description: Reads a computed stat from the latest body snapshot. Bleeding, Sleeping, Consciousness, Drunkenness and Poisoning follow the body as it changes; the others are sampled about every 250 ms to a hundredth of a native unit, then replicated. Values use native units and can be negative; they are not universally percentages. Returns zero without a valid snapshot. Throws for an unknown stat or invalid arguments. These readings do not override another player's native calculations.

parameters.name: stat
parameters.description: A DerivedPlayerStat value.

functions.name: getTrack
functions.description: Where this player stands on one track: level, XP towards the next one, and unspent perk points.

parameters.name: track
parameters.description: A track name, from `Progression.tracks()`.

returns.description: The progress, or null before their client's first report. Throws for a track name the tables do not carry.

functions.name: hasPerk
functions.description: Whether this player owns a perk.

parameters.name: perk
parameters.description: A perk's name or GUID.

returns.description: True when their last report carried it.

functions.name: addXp
functions.description: Grants XP on one track, through the game's own path on the player's client -- so their perks' XP multipliers apply, a level crossed pops the game's own level-up, and a level grants its perk points. Rates, budgets and caps do not apply: those rule over what a player earns, and this is the server giving.

parameters.name: track
parameters.description: A track name. Not `fencing`: the game derives it from the weapon skills.

parameters.name: xp
parameters.description: XP, in the game's own units.

returns.description: True when the order went out. Throws for an unknown track or an xp that is not positive.

functions.name: setLevel
functions.description: Sets an exact level and clears its XP remainder, including on a live player. Increases use native XP effects and grant points; decreases notify native property listeners and recompute induced skills. Decreasing does not remove perks or revoke points: change those explicitly, or restore a complete snapshot.

parameters.name: track
parameters.description: A track name. Not `fencing`.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Exact level, from zero to the track cap; resets XP inside that level.

returns.description: True when the order went out; false for a level past the cap.

functions.name: setXp
functions.description: Sets a track's total earned XP exactly, including reductions inside a level and across levels. Does not revoke perks or unspent points.

parameters.name: track
parameters.description: A progression track other than fencing.

parameters.name: xp
parameters.description: Absolute cumulative XP from level zero, in game XP units. Quantized down to 1/128 XP; cannot exceed the track cap.

returns.description: True when the order went out; false for an unavailable player or XP above the cap.

functions.name: removeXp
functions.description: Subtracts unscaled cumulative XP from the reported track plus pending orders. Requires the first progression report. Level and remainder can both decrease; perks and points stay unchanged.

parameters.name: track
parameters.description: A progression track other than fencing.

parameters.name: xp
parameters.description: Positive XP to remove, at least 1/128. Clamps at zero total XP.

returns.description: True when the order went out.

functions.name: addPerk
functions.description: Gives this player a perk outright, spending no point and skipping the perk screen's requirements. It still has to be one the game can add: an owned or blocked perk is turned down by the game itself.

parameters.name: perk
parameters.description: A perk's name or GUID.

returns.description: True when the order went out. Throws for an unknown perk.

functions.name: removePerk
functions.description: Takes a perk away. The point it cost is not refunded; `respecPerks` is the way to hand points back.

parameters.name: perk
parameters.description: A perk's name or GUID.

returns.description: True when the order went out. Throws for an unknown perk.

functions.name: addPerkPoints
functions.description: Gives this player unspent perk points in one tree, on top of what their levels earned.

parameters.name: track
parameters.description: The tree to add to: a track name, or `main` for the main-level bank.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: How many, from 1 to 65535.

returns.description: True when the order went out.

functions.name: respecPerks
functions.description: The game's own respec: every perk learnt on the perk screen is taken away and every tree's points are rebuilt from the player's current levels. Perks the game granted on its own stay.

returns.description: True when the order went out.

functions.name: restoreProgression
functions.description: Restores the supplied tracks exactly, including lower levels and XP remainders on live players. Supplied perks replace the reported perk set, and supplied point banks are set after progression events drain. Omitted sections stay unchanged. The entire snapshot is validated before any order is sent. Fencing is recomputed from weapon skills. A restore is not a gain: a raised track shows no level-up popup and grants no perk points.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: What `player.progression` returned, as the resource stored it.

returns.description: True when every order went out.

functions.name: revive
functions.description: Requests revival of this player after playerDied.

returns.description: True when sent; false when disconnected, no death was reported, or revival was already requested.

functions.name: cancelCombat
functions.description: Ends melee combat between these two players and retires their pending blows against each other. Other opponents are left alone. A later attack can start combat again. Consent and timeout rules belong to your resource.

parameters.name: opponent
parameters.description: The other player. Both sides are cancelled.

returns.description: True when sent; false for disconnected players, the same player, or different virtual worlds.

functions.name: spawn
functions.description:
Puts this player somewhere, as a spawn rather than as a teleport: their client holds the body still until there is real ground under it, so it cannot fall through a world that has not streamed in yet.

Called from a `playerSpawning` handler this *is* the answer to that request -- the player is still behind their loading screen, and nothing is seen. Called at any other time it moves a player who is already in the world, which is visible.

Nothing else names a spawn: with no handler calling this, everybody arrives at the level's own start point, because every client asks the game for the identical map start.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Where the body goes; a Vector3 or any object carrying x, y and z.

parameters.name: rotation
parameters.description: Which way they face: a Quaternion, or a Vector3 of Euler degrees.

returns.description: True when the placement was accepted; false for a position that is not somewhere in the world, or a player with no connection to ask.

functions.name: teleport
functions.description: Asks this player's own client to put them somewhere else. The owning client is authoritative for its body's pose, so this is a request that lands on their next frame rather than a write.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: World-space destination; a Vector3 or any object carrying x, y and z.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: Optional name for the destination, echoed back in the client's own teleport panel. Display only.

returns.description: True when the request went out; false when the position is not finite or the player has no connection to ask.

functions.name: playAnimation
functions.description:
Makes this player's body play one of the game's animations, on their own screen and on everybody else's -- a wave, a bow, a woodcutter's swing with the axe in hand. It is state rather than a one-off: a player who streams in or joins while it plays sees it too, and it lasts until `stopAnimation` or the next `playAnimation`, even after a one-shot has finished.

A new `playAnimation`, `stopAnimation` and `teleport` cut a running animation at once rather than waiting for it to finish. The game can cut it short too: a hit, a fall or drawing a weapon ends it, and so can the player walking off from one that leaves the legs free. `loop` starts it again when that happens, and keeps a one-shot going pass after pass with no gap between them.

`playerAnimationEnd` fires once when the animation this request started is over, and says how. A loop ends only by being stopped or replaced.

A hand tag is only half of holding something. `r_bucket` makes the body move as if it carried a bucket, but the bucket itself is a `props` entry.

parameters.name: fragment
parameters.description: A Mannequin fragment, as `Animations.list` names it. `""` plays none and only puts the props and tags on, which with a hand tag like `r_bucket` makes the player carry something while they walk.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `clip` plays a clip the server streams instead of a fragment (`animations/kcdc/<resource>/wave.caf`, the fragment left `""`), `tags` pick the variant, `loop` repeats it until stopped, `lockMovement` holds the player still, `props` puts up to two models in their hands.

type.name: { clip?: string; tags?: string; loop?: boolean; lockMovement?: boolean; props?: { item?: string; model?: string; hand?: 'right' | 'left'; joint?: string; position?: Vector3 | Partial<Vector3>; rotation?: Quaternion | Vector3 | Partial<Vector3> } | { item?: string; model?: string; hand?: 'right' | 'left'; joint?: string; position?: Vector3 | Partial<Vector3>; rotation?: Quaternion | Vector3 | Partial<Vector3> }[] }

returns.description: True when the request went out; false for a player with no body yet. Throws for a prop or option it cannot use.

functions.name: stopAnimation
functions.description:
Ends what `playAnimation` started at once, takes its props away and hands the body back to the game. A stance tag the animation set goes with it, so without `standUp` a seated player pops upright.

The stand-up is an animation of its own: it raises its own `playerAnimationEnd`, fragment `StandUp` or `GetUp`, once the player is on their feet, and a `playAnimation` during it replaces it.

parameters.name: options
