parameters.description: `standUp` plays the game's own way back to standing when the animation held the body in a sitting or lying stance tag (`sittingNoTable`, `lyingGround`): `StandUp` or `GetUp`, in the variant that fits that stance. Without it, or for a stance the game authors no way out of (`beggarKneel`), the body goes straight back to standing.

returns.description: True when the request went out; false for a player with no body yet.

functions.name: setFacialExpression
functions.description:
Sets this player's facial expression, on their own screen and on everybody else's, alongside whatever their body plays. It is state: a player who streams in sees it, and it lasts until the next call.

The expression is the eyes, brows and mood. It never moves the mouth -- the game's own `FE_DialogueSpeaking` animates only the eyes and leaves the mouth to the voice line being spoken. `setTalking` is the mouth.

A mood tag is one of the body's own tags, so it can change the mood of the body's idle too, for as long as the expression holds.

parameters.name: fragment
parameters.description: A fragment on the face's own scope: `FE_Default`, `FE_DialogueIdle` or `FE_DialogueSpeaking` for a held mood, or an `ADLG_FA_*` gesture (`ADLG_FA_Smile`, `ADLG_FA_Wink`, `ADLG_FA_Laugh`, `ADLG_FA_Surprise`...) that plays once. `""` hands the face back to the game.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `tags` pick the variant: for the `FE_*` fragments the mood, `happy`, `angry`, `sad`, `nervous`, `pensive`, `arogant` or `drunk`, as `Animations.list("FE_")` spells them.

returns.description: True when the request went out; false for a player with no body yet. Throws for an argument it cannot use.

functions.name: setTalking
functions.description:
Moves this player's mouth as if they were talking, on their own screen and on everybody else's, until told to stop -- for text chat, voice chat or a scene. It is a looping talk animation, not lip-sync: it follows no words.

The game's own lip-sync wins while it plays a voice line on the same body, and the loop comes back after it.

parameters.name: talking
parameters.description: Whether the mouth moves.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: How: `neutral` (the default), `happy`, `drunk` or `chew`.

returns.description: True when the request went out; false for a player with no body yet. Throws for a style it does not know.

functions.name: setAppearance
functions.description:
Asks this player's own client to wear a different body -- face, hair, beard and skin. The owning client is authoritative for its body, so this is a request that lands on their next frame rather than a write; read `player.appearance` back to see what they actually put on.

Gender is applied before the parts, because it decides which half of the game's catalog the names come from -- and it is the one part of this with a price. A soul's gender lives on its archetype, so changing it moves the player to the game's own counterpart archetype, which also carries four authored numbers: base armour, the conspicuousness and visibility pair, and unarmed attack. Nothing reads those on the puppets other people see, but on the body its owner plays they are a real change. Ask for a gender only when you mean it; a male-to-male change never touches the archetype.

Everyone starts as Henry, so a server that wants people to tell each other apart has to call this.

Face and beard travel together whether or not both are named. Beards are modelled per face, so changing either into a pair that was never modelled is refused whole rather than applied without the beard; `Appearances.beards` says which pairs are real.

parameters.name: appearance
parameters.description: The parts to change. Anything left out keeps what the player is wearing, and an empty string hands that part back to the game. Names come from `Appearances.options`, except the beard, which comes from `Appearances.beards`.

returns.description: True when the request went out; false for a name that is not in the catalog, a gender it does not belong to, a beard that face cannot wear, or a player with no connection to ask.

functions.name: setWorldBuilderEnabled
functions.description: Grants or revokes World Builder access for this player. Multiplayer connections start without access. Enabling allows F7 and the client MapEditor.open API; disabling also closes an open editor. The permission lasts until changed or disconnected and does not affect other players. Offline editing is always allowed.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Whether this player may open World Builder.

returns.description: True when the permission was sent; false for a player with no connection. Throws unless enabled is a boolean.

functions.name: setMovementMode
functions.description:
Puts a pace rule on this player. `walkByDefault` makes walking the pace they keep coming back to and leaves their own key working; `walkEnforced` forbids running and sprinting outright, and their key stops mattering.

The two are different things and both are worth having: a default is a preference, an enforcement is a rule. Nothing about either goes out to anybody else -- the pace every other player draws comes from this body's own published animation tags, so a walking player already looks like one everywhere.

A default holds across sprints. The game itself ends every sprint in a jog, deliberately, so the client puts the walk back once the sprint is over rather than during it, and a player who chose to jog keeps jogging: only the pace the sprint took is given back. On a gamepad the stick's own deflection decides the pace, which the rule neither reads nor overrides.

Enforcement holds the engine's own run and sprint permissions, the same pair the game clears while somebody carries a body, and hands back what it found when the rule is lifted. Sprinting cannot shake it off.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: The whole rule. A key left out is off, because the server keeps no copy of what this player is currently under.

returns.description: True when the rule went out; false for a player with no connection to ask.

functions.name: giveItem
functions.description: Grants items into this player's inventory, which the server holds; their game shows them on the next tick and announces them with its own "You received" toast. `Inventory.add` does the same, can set the items' properties, and can leave out the toast.

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: Item class GUID, or the exact name the game's own item tables use.

parameters.name: amount
parameters.description: How many to grant; defaults to 1, and at most 10000.

returns.description: True when the items were added; false for an unknown item, an amount outside 1..10000, or a player with no inventory.

functions.name: takeItem
functions.description: Takes items of a class out of this player's inventory, across its rows, all of them or none. The server holds the inventory, so the promise is already settled when it is returned; it stays a promise so existing scripts keep working. Their game announces the loss with its own toast; `Inventory.remove` can leave it out. To move items between players use `Inventory.transfer`, which cannot lose them half way.

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: Item class GUID, or the exact name the game's own item tables use. The same spelling `giveItem` takes.

parameters.name: amount
parameters.description: How many units to take; defaults to 1, and at most 10000. Zero is refused rather than read as "all of them".

returns.description: An object carrying `removed` (the amount when it happened, otherwise 0), `requested`, `ok`, and `reason` (empty on success, otherwise the inventory code, such as `insufficientItems`).

type.name: Promise<{ removed: number; requested: number; ok: boolean; reason: string }>

functions.name: dropInventory
functions.description: Moves this player's items into a container spawned at their body, as a death drop: `playerInventoryChanged` (reason `drop`) and `stashInventoryChanged` follow, then the container is anyone's to open. At most 128 rows go. What happens to it next -- who may loot it, when it goes -- is the script's.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `keepEquipped` keeps the units their body wears or holds.

returns.description: The container, or null when there was nothing to drop or the player has no inventory.

functions.name: setOutfit
functions.description: Dresses this player in one of the game's own outfits. Every piece of clothing they wear comes off and stays in their inventory, and a new set of the outfit's clothes is added and worn; weapons and everything else are left as they are. Their game dresses them a moment later, as it does after `Inventory.set`.

parameters.name: preset
parameters.description: One of the game's own outfits for this player's gender, by a name from `Player.outfitPresets(player.appearance.gender)` or its GUID.

returns.description: True when the inventory was changed; false for a preset that is not in the catalog or is the other gender's, a player with no inventory, or an inventory with no room.

functions.name: getInventory
functions.description: Reads this player's inventory; the same as `Inventory.get(player)`.

returns.description: A copy of it, or null for a player who is not connected.

functions.name: addBuff
functions.description:
Puts a status effect on this player's body. The server runs no effects of its own, so this asks their client rather than writing anything, and it lands a moment later -- `hasBuff` right after this call still says false. Watch `playerBuffAdded` for the moment it is really on.

The ask is not a promise, either: the game refuses an effect that conflicts with one already there, and a second drink folds into the first rather than stacking.

parameters.name: buff
parameters.description: Buff GUID, or the exact name the game's own buff tables use. `Buffs.find` resolves either.

returns.description: True when the instruction went out; false for an unknown buff or a player with no connection to ask.

functions.name: removeBuff
functions.description: Asks this player's own client to take a status effect off: the exact instance when a report named one, and every instance of that definition otherwise.

parameters.name: buff
parameters.description: Buff GUID, or the exact name the game's own buff tables use.

returns.description: True when the instruction went out; false for an unknown buff or a player with no connection to ask.

functions.name: clearBuffs
functions.description: Clears every effect in one of the game's own families at once: one call for all poisons, or all bleeding, without naming them. `Buffs.tags` lists the families. Note that `World.setTime` does not fast-forward effects -- their time runs off each client's frame delta and never reads the calendar -- so a scripted sleep has to clear what it means to end.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: An effect family, from `Buffs.tags` -- `poison`, `bleed`, `alcohol_drunk`, `unconscious`.

returns.description: True when the instruction went out; false for a tag no buff table uses or a player with no connection to ask.

functions.name: hasBuff
functions.description: Whether this player's last report carried that status effect.

parameters.name: buff
parameters.description: Buff GUID, or the exact name the game's own buff tables use.

returns.description: True when it did; false for an unknown buff, or a player who has reported nothing yet.

functions.name: setStat
functions.description: Sets health, stamina, energy or nourishment on the living body. Call once player.ready is true. Lowering health raises playerDamage with a null attacker; a fatal change also raises playerDied with a null killer. Zero health can kill. Does not clear buffs or revive; normal regeneration and consumption continue.

parameters.name: stat
parameters.description: Writable PlayerStat; derived stats are rejected.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Finite native value from 0 to 1000000, clamped to the native maximum. Positive health must exceed 0.00001; positive values must not underflow to zero.

returns.description: True when sent, not confirmation of application; false for a missing, unready or dead body. Throws for invalid arguments or a read-only stat. Requests for a previous life are discarded. Read getStat after the client's next report to observe the result.

functions.name: setHealth
functions.description: Sets this living player's health, raising or lowering it. Lowering raises playerDamage with a null attacker and the amount removed; a fatal change also raises playerDied with a null killer. This includes restoring a lower saved value. Zero can kill; this never revives a dead player. Leaves injuries, poison and bleeding in place. Call after playerSpawned or playerReady when restoring a saved value. The client applies the request asynchronously; health continues to show its last report until a new one arrives.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Health in the same units as player.health. Clamped to maxHealth on the player's client.

returns.description: True when sent; false when the body is missing, not ready or dead. Throws unless value is a finite number from 0 to 1000000, with positive health greater than 0.00001 after conversion to native float units. A request for a life that has since ended is ignored.

functions.name: setHunger
functions.description: Sets this living player's nourishment, raising or lowering it. Call after playerSpawned or playerReady when restoring a saved value. The client applies the request asynchronously; hunger continues to show its last report until a new one arrives.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Nourishment in the same units as player.hunger. Higher means better fed. Clamped to maxHunger on the player's client.

returns.description: True when sent; false when the body is missing, not ready or dead. Throws unless value is a finite number from 0 to 1000000 that does not round from positive to zero in native float units. A request for a life that has since ended is ignored.

functions.name: heal
functions.description:
Nurses this player back, on their own client and with the game's own recipe -- the one its quests use for a full heal: the `remove_injuries` and `remove_all_posions` cures, which each wipe their whole kind of effect as they land, then health raised through the soul's own setter, the way a potion raises it. What comes off raises `playerInjuryHealed` and `playerBuffRemoved` as usual.

It does not revive anybody: a dead player stays dead until `revive`.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: What to restore; everything when left out. `health`: true or absent for all of it, a number to raise it to that much (never lowers it), false to leave it. `injuries`: clear every limb injury, and with it the bleeding a badly hurt limb causes. `poisons`: clear every poison. `bleeding`: clear the standalone bleeding effect.

type.name: { health?: number | boolean; injuries?: boolean; poisons?: boolean; bleeding?: boolean }

returns.description: True when the orders went out; false for a player with no connection to ask. Throws for a health that is not a finite, non-negative number.

functions.name: setDisguise
functions.description:
Draws this player as a static mesh instead of themselves -- a barrel, a haystack, a cart wheel -- on their own screen and on everybody else's. It is state: a player who streams in or joins sees it too, and it lasts until the next call.

Only the look and the collision change. The body is hidden rather than replaced, and its collision cylinder is resized around the mesh, so the player walks and is traced against in roughly the mesh's shape -- a client's `World.raycast` with `mode: "anything"` finds them where the mesh is drawn, and says which player it found. The mesh turns with the body. They keep everything else a person has: they can still be hurt, bleed and die, and nothing stops them drawing a weapon, which a gamemode that does not want that has to take away.

The game's own camera sits in the head, which the mesh now covers: pair this with the client's `Camera.setThirdPerson` for the disguised player. Nametags are not touched; `setNametagVisible` is the call for that. NPCs still see a person.

The owning client is authoritative for its body, so this is a request that lands on their next frame; `player.disguise` reads what they actually have on.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: A mesh from the prop catalog, by its `objects/...cgf` path or its file stem, or one this server streams by its full path -- anything `Prop.spawn` takes. Null puts the player back in their own body.

returns.description: True when the request went out; false for a player with no connection to ask. Throws for a model the catalog does not carry.

functions.name: setVisible
functions.description:
Stops drawing this player's body, or draws it again -- on their own screen and on everybody else's. The body goes with everything on it: what it wears, the weapons on its back and belt, and whatever it is holding. It is state, like a disguise: somebody who streams in or joins sees nothing of a hidden player either, and it lasts until the next call or until they leave.

Nothing but the drawing changes. They stand where they stood, keep their collider, their soul and their weapons, so a hidden player still blocks a doorway, can still be hit and traced against, still fights and still dies -- and the NPCs around them never stopped seeing a person. Nametags are separate; `setNametagVisible` is the call for that.

Their own camera sits in their head, so a hidden player simply sees no arms in first person. The owning client is authoritative for its body, so this is a request that lands on their next frame; `player.visible` reads what they actually have.

parameters.name: visible
parameters.description: False to stop drawing this player's body, true to draw it again.

returns.description: True when the request went out; false for a player with no connection to ask. Throws unless `visible` is a boolean.

functions.name: dismount
functions.description: Takes this player out of whatever saddle they are in: their own client gets them off, and `horseDismount` is raised.

returns.description: The horse they were taken off, or null when they were not riding one.

functions.name: putDown
functions.description: Has this player put down the body on their shoulder, with the game's own put-down. It is an instruction to their client, so the carry ends when that put-down lands: `playerPutDown` follows then, and `carrying` reads null from that moment.

returns.description: True when the order went out; false when they carry nobody or have no connection.

functions.name: carryItem
functions.description:
Has this player carry an item in their arms, the way the game's own people carry firewood, sacks and baskets: the carrying walk, and the put-down at the end. While it is carried they walk, since the game has no running with a load.

It is an instruction to their client, so the carry lands when that client reports it: `playerCarryItem` and `carriedItem` follow. A carry a script ordered is not put to `playerCarryingItem`. The item never enters their inventory. Put down -- with the game's own key or `putDownItem` -- it falls from their hands and becomes a carryable `GroundItem` where it lands, which `playerPutDownItem` hands over and anybody can take up again.

Their hands have to be free -- a drawn weapon or a torch makes their game refuse the carry, and nothing is reported.

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: What to carry. A name from `Animations.props()` whose `hand` the game has a carrying walk for -- the baskets (`basket_full_wood`, `basket_b_apples`, `stonebasket`, `eggbasket`, `shoppingbasket`), `firewoodChipsHand`, the buckets (`waterBucket`, `milkBucket`), and for a man only the sacks (`sack`, `sack_miller`), `barrel` and `crate_with_silver` -- puts a new one straight into their hands. A `GroundItem` of such a class has them pick that one up off the ground with the game's own bend-down; it has to be a single item within their reach.

returns.description: True when the order went out; false when they cannot act, are riding, already carry an item or a body, the stack is not resting within their reach or somebody else is taking it, or they have no connection. Throws for an item with no carrying walk, or none for this player's body.

functions.name: putDownItem
functions.description: Has this player put down the item in their arms, with the game's own put-down. It is an instruction to their client, so the carry ends when that put-down lands: `playerPutDownItem` follows then.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `immediate` lets go at once, without the put-down.

returns.description: True when the order went out; false when they carry no item or have no connection.

functions.name: mount
functions.description: Puts this player in a horse's saddle. Everyone near enough to watch sees it the way it was asked for -- the get-on, or the instant seat -- while a client that only streams the rider in later finds them already seated. It is an instruction to their client, so the seat is reported back like any other mount: `horseMounting` can still refuse it, and `horseMount` and `player.horse` follow once it lands. The player has to be standing near the horse; teleport them beside it first.

parameters.name: horse
parameters.description: The horse to get on.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `instant` puts them straight into the seat, as the game's own forced mount does; by default they play the get-on a player plays at a horse.

returns.description: True when the order went out; false when the horse is dead or somebody else is riding it, or the player has no connection.

functions.name: outfitPresets
functions.description: The game's own outfits, from its clothing presets: what `player.setOutfit` and `Npc.setOutfit` dress a body in. Many belong to one named character.

parameters.name: gender
parameters.description: Only the outfits authored for this gender. The game will not put a man's clothes on a woman or the reverse, so `player.setOutfit` takes only the presets of the player's own `appearance.gender`.

returns.description: Preset names, men's first, each gender's in name order.

functions.name: all
functions.description: Lists every player currently connected, including those whose body has no pose yet.

returns.description: One handle per connected player, in no particular order.

functions.name: getById
functions.description: Looks a player up by their network entity ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

returns.description: The player's handle, or null when no connected player has that ID.

properties.name: nickname
properties.description: The name this player connected under, or an empty string once their body is gone.

properties.name: playerIndex
properties.description: Connection slot this player holds, or 65535 when unassigned. Stable for the length of the session and reused afterwards.

properties.name: appearance
properties.description:
What this player's body looks like, as their own client last published it. Every part is empty until something chooses one, which is the default body -- and why everyone looks the same until a resource says otherwise.

Read back rather than assumed after `setAppearance`: the owning client is authoritative for its own body, so a new look appears here once they have actually put it on.

properties.name: disguise
properties.description: The prop-catalog mesh this player's body is drawn as, by its `objects/...cgf` path, or null while they look like themselves. Published by their own client, so it follows `setDisguise` once they have actually put it on.

properties.name: visible
properties.description: Whether this player's body is drawn at all -- itself, what it wears and what it carries. True for everybody until something hides them. Published by their own client, so it follows `setVisible` once they have actually stopped drawing. A hidden player is only invisible: they still stand where they stand, still collide, can still be hit, and NPCs still see them.

properties.name: ready
properties.description: Whether this player's body has both a pose and a soul, which is what everyone else waits for before spawning a puppet for them. False for the first moments of a connection.

properties.name: alive
properties.description: Whether this player has health left. False also while no soul has been published.

properties.name: canAct
properties.description: Whether the body can be driven at all: alive, conscious and not asleep.

properties.name: healthPercent
properties.description: Health as a percentage from 0 to 100 -- what the nametag bar draws. Derived from the pair behind it, so it survives a maximum that changes.

properties.name: health
properties.description: Current health, in the game's own units. 0 while no soul has been published.

properties.name: maxHealth
properties.description: Health capacity, in the game's own units.

properties.name: stamina
properties.description: Current stamina, in the game's own units.

properties.name: maxStamina
properties.description: Stamina capacity, in the game's own units. Collapses to 0 for a tick around death, which is real rather than a bad read.

properties.name: healthyStamina
properties.description: The stamina ceiling the body's injuries currently allow, which is at or below maxStamina.

properties.name: exhaust
properties.description: Current energy reserve, in the game's own units. Higher means better rested.

properties.name: maxExhaust
properties.description: Maximum energy reserve, in the game's own units.

properties.name: hunger
properties.description: Current nourishment, in the game's own units.

properties.name: maxHunger
properties.description: Nourishment capacity, in the game's own units.

properties.name: bleeding
properties.description: How heavily the body is bleeding; 0 when it is not.

properties.name: sleeping
properties.description: Sleepiness the game has accumulated for this body; above 0 means asleep.

properties.name: consciousness
properties.description: How conscious the body is; 0 is knocked out.

properties.name: drunkenness
properties.description: How drunk the body is; 0 is sober.

properties.name: poisoning
properties.description: How poisoned the body is; 0 is clean.

properties.name: strength
properties.description: Strength, in the game's own units.

properties.name: agility
properties.description: Agility, in the game's own units.

properties.name: vitality
properties.description: Vitality, in the game's own units.

properties.name: relativeStats
properties.description: The same three attributes as the engine's relative values, which is what its own modifiers are expressed in.

properties.name: skills
properties.description: The nine combat and survival skills a hit or a draw is evaluated against. Read as a whole rather than one at a time: the snapshot carries them together.

properties.name: relativeSkills
properties.description: The same nine skills as the engine's relative values.

properties.name: velocity
properties.description: On the owning machine, the velocity the body's own animation was driven by this frame, not the one its physics settled on. Everywhere else, measured from successive replicated positions.

properties.name: lookDirection
properties.description: World-space direction the head and eyes are turned towards. Zero while the body has reported none.

properties.name: inAir
properties.description: Whether the body is off the ground -- fallen or mid-jump -- as its own physics reports it, debounced past the flicker a stair step causes.

properties.name: crouched
properties.description: Whether this player is crouched, as their own game's crouch action reports it. False once their body is gone.

properties.name: physicsProfile
properties.description: The ragdoll physics profile the body is in, or 255 when it has none to report.

properties.name: fistsUp
properties.description: Whether this player has their fists -- or their weapon -- up. Stays true after the arm comes down, which is how the engine holds it.

properties.name: guard
properties.description: The arm guard in the engine's own levels: 0 arms down, 1 the guard a player holds.

properties.name: combatZone
properties.description: Which direction of the combat star this player is aiming at, as a row of the game's zone table, or -1 when they are aiming at none.

properties.name: rightHandItem
properties.description: Item class drawn in the right hand as 32 hex digits, or an empty string when the hand is empty. A class rather than an item: no engine-local identifier crosses the wire.

properties.name: leftHandItem
properties.description: Item class drawn in the left hand as 32 hex digits, or an empty string when the hand is empty.

properties.name: equipment
properties.description: Item classes this player is wearing, each as 32 hex digits. What they actually have on rather than a preset, so a bare body reads as an empty array.

properties.name: visorClosed
properties.description: Whether this player has a helmet visor down, as their own game reports it. False when they wear no helmet with a visor, and once their body is gone. There is no setter: the player raises and lowers it in their own game.

properties.name: level
properties.description: The player's main level, the one the game derives from the stats, as their client last reported it. 0 until the first report.

properties.name: levels
properties.description: The level of every skill and stat, keyed by track name, as this server last accepted it. All zero until the first report.

properties.name: perks
properties.description: Every perk the player owns, by name.

properties.name: progression
properties.description: Everything about this player's progression, as plain JSON to store however the resource likes. A player starts every session with a fresh character, so `restoreProgression` with a stored snapshot is how progression outlives a disconnect. Null until their client's first report.

properties.name: mounted
properties.description: Whether this player is in a saddle.

properties.name: carrying
properties.description: The player whose body this one carries on their shoulder, or null. Set once `playerCarry` has fired, cleared once `playerPutDown` has.

properties.name: carriedBy
properties.description: The player carrying this one's body, or null.

properties.name: carriedItem
properties.description: The item this player carries in their arms, by its item name, or null. Set once `playerCarryItem` has fired, cleared once `playerPutDownItem` has.

properties.name: horse
properties.description: The horse this player is riding, or null when they are on foot.

properties.name: dog
properties.description: The dog companion this player has, or null when they have none. One dog per player, as in the game.

properties.name: buffs
properties.description:
The status effects on this player's body, as their own client last reported them: potions, poison, injury, drunkenness, illness, unconsciousness, and anything this server added. Perks and equipment effects are not in here -- they follow state that already replicates.

This is the list of *named effects*. For how drunk, poisoned, hurt or tired someone actually is, read `drunkenness`, `poisoning`, `bleeding`, `consciousness`, `hunger` and `exhaust` instead: those are live numbers and need no name to look up.

Empty until the player's client sends its first report, shortly after they connect; `playerBuffAdded` fires for whatever it was already carrying.

properties.name: injuries
properties.description:
Which limbs are injured, as the player's own client last reported them -- the same report `buffs` reads, named by limb so nobody has to know the six buff names. All false until the first report arrives. `playerInjured` and `playerInjuryHealed` fire as a flag changes.

What an injury does is the game's own: a hurt head, torso or arm weakens its stats, a hurt leg takes away running and sprinting, and a badly hurt limb bleeds. Everybody else sees the consequences rather than the injury: the owner's slower pace, the lower stamina ceiling, bleeding, and the hurt gait the game plays once health is low. The game has no leg-specific limp animation, so there is nothing more to show.

symbols.name: Consumption
symbols.description: A server-validated serving. Item properties and pot poison come from server state; changing the snapshot does not change the decision.

properties.name: source
properties.description: Where the serving comes from.

properties.name: item
properties.description: Native food or potion item class GUID.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: Native food type; potions use the game's food type 1.

properties.name: baseEffects
properties.description: Native table inputs before item condition, spoilage, perks or soul modifiers. Health effects may run over time. These are not promised final stat deltas. Null when the catalog has no row.

type.name: { buff: string | null; health: number; energy: number; nourishment: number; alcohol: number } | null

properties.name: rowId
properties.description: Inventory row, or null for a pot meal.

properties.name: potGuid
properties.description: Cooking pot GUID, or null for an inventory item.

properties.name: metadata
properties.description: Server item properties, including condition. Empty for a pot meal.

properties.name: poison
properties.description: Additional cooking pot poison buff GUID, or null. Spoilage and the item's own effects are part of nativeEffects.

properties.name: nativeEffects
properties.description: Whether native nutrition, energy, alcohol, potion and spoilage effects are allowed. Final in playerConsumed.

symbols.name: Preparation
symbols.description: Items a player's game dried on a drying rack, smoked in a smokehouse or cooked at a fire, and what the server is about to make of them. Frozen: a handler can refuse it, not change it.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: A drying rack dries herbs and food; a smokehouse smokes food; a fire cooks food.

properties.name: station
properties.description: The drying rack, smokehouse or fire the player stands at, as `<level>:<guid>`; the same on every machine and across restarts. A fire's guid is its cook pot's, as `CookPot.get` takes it.

properties.name: items
properties.description: Each inventory row about to be taken: `amount` units of class `item`, which become class `product`.

type.name: { id: string; item: string; amount: number; product: string }[]

symbols.name: AnimalLootItem
symbols.description: One candidate from the game's animal loot preset; probability and inventory population belong to the gamemode.

properties.name: item
properties.description: Item class GUID.

properties.name: amount
properties.description: Maximum authored unit count.

properties.name: fraction
properties.description: Authored quantity fraction, not a drop probability.

properties.name: variation
properties.description: Uniform variation around the quantity fraction.

properties.name: food
properties.description: The item is food.

properties.name: harvester
properties.description: Tagged as a special Harvester part in the game data. This is metadata; the gamemode decides eligibility.

symbols.name: InventoryUnit
symbols.description: A count of units from one row.

properties.name: id
properties.description: The row.

properties.name: amount
properties.description: How many of its units.

symbols.name: InventoryRow
symbols.description: A stack of one item class with one set of properties. Two rows never hold the same class with equal properties unless a restore put them there. Stackable custom rows merge only with matching properties. Nonstackable custom rows each contain one unit.

properties.name: id
properties.description: The row's identity within its owner's inventory. Stable while the row exists; save it with the row and pass it back to `Inventory.set`.

properties.name: item
properties.description: Item class GUID.

properties.name: name
properties.description: Internal table name, or Items.register id for a custom type. Display overrides are in metadata.custom.name.

properties.name: amount
properties.description: Units in the row.

properties.name: quality
properties.description: Quality, from 1 up to the class's maximum. Same as `metadata.quality`.

properties.name: health
properties.description: Absolute item health. Same as `metadata.health`.

properties.name: condition
properties.description: Health as a fraction of what this quality allows, 0 to 1. Same as `metadata.condition`.

properties.name: equipped
properties.description: Units the body wears or holds: reported by a player, authored stock for an NPC. Reads include them; pass them to `Inventory.set` to dress a restored body.

properties.name: metadata
properties.description: Every property the server keeps: `quality`, `health`, `condition`, and on missiles `poison` (a buff GUID) and `poisonCharges`, and `onEquipBuffs` (buff GUIDs). Custom items also carry `custom: { name?, description?, data? }`. Data stays server-side. A default is left out. Pass it back as it is to keep an item exactly.

symbols.name: InventoryState
symbols.description: One player's or NPC's inventory as the server holds it.

properties.name: ready
properties.description: For a player, their game shows this revision. For an NPC, its initial stock has been established. Wait for `playerInventoryReady` or `npcInventoryReady` respectively.

properties.name: revision
properties.description: Advances by one with every change. Pass it as a request's `revision` to refuse the request if anything changed in between.

properties.name: items
properties.description: Every row.

properties.name: harvested
properties.description: NPC stock only: the carcass has already been harvested. Pass it to Inventory.set when restoring a corpse; absent preserves its existing state.

properties.name: quickslots
properties.description: The current native outfit's quick-access assignments and selections, using row IDs. Null until reported or restored. Save with items and pass both to Inventory.set.

symbols.name: InventoryQuickslots
symbols.description: The current outfit's weapon and item quickslots. Indices are zero-based; each array has four entries. Empty references are null.

properties.name: weapons
properties.description: Four weapon slots, each with primary and secondary row IDs. A row may appear in several slots.

type.name: { primary: string | null; secondary: string | null }[]

properties.name: items
properties.description: Four item slots, containing row IDs or null. Save equipped belts and pouches with the inventory rows to retain slot capacity.

properties.name: activeWeapon
properties.description: Selected weapon slot, 0 through 3.

properties.name: activeItem
properties.description: Selected item slot, 0 through 3.

symbols.name: InventoryChange
symbols.description: What one operation did to one inventory.

properties.name: revision
properties.description: The revision the operation produced.

properties.name: reason
properties.description: `add`, `remove`, `properties`, `set`, `transfer`, `wear` when the player's game wore an item down in use, `use` for food, potions and ointments, `shot` for a fired round, `pickpocket`, `trade` for a vendor deal, `repair` for a repair kit, `sharpen` for a grindstone, `dry`, `smoke` and `cook` for a drying rack, a smokehouse and a fire, `drop` for `player.dropInventory`, `loot`, `npcDeposit`, `harvest`, `outfit`, or the ground, stash and gathering reasons. `equipment` reports an equipment or quickslot change: items is empty, the item revision does not advance, and Inventory.get returns the new snapshot.

properties.name: items
properties.description: Only the rows that changed. `before: null` is a new row and `after: null` an emptied one.

type.name: { id: string; before: InventoryRow | null; after: InventoryRow | null }[]

symbols.name: InventoryResult
symbols.description: What an inventory operation did.

properties.name: ok
properties.description: It happened. Nothing changes when it did not.

properties.name: code
properties.description: Empty on success, otherwise why not: `inventoryUnavailable`, `invalidRequest`, `staleRevision`, `invalidItem`, `invalidItems`, `invalidAmount`, `unknownItem`, `insufficientItems`, `inventoryCapacity`, `sameInventory`, `invalidEquipment`, or a property policy code (`invalidMetadata`, `unknownItemClass`, `questItem`, `invalidQuality`, `immutableItemHealth`, `invalidItemHealth`, `contradictoryItemHealth`, `invalidCreationSentinel`, `unsupportedPoisonProperties`, `unsupportedOnEquipBuffs`).

properties.name: revision
properties.description: The revision after the operation; for a transfer, the source's. 0 when refused.

properties.name: items
properties.description: The rows that received units: the row an `add` merged into or created, a transfer's rows in the target, every row a `set` wrote. Empty for `remove`.

symbols.name: Inventory
symbols.description: Player and NPC inventories. The server holds the stock and clients project it. Native NPC default stock is censused once by its elected simulator; `Inventory.set` establishes scripted stock immediately. Other NPC writes require ready stock. Every operation happens at once and in full, or not at all. `revision` is optional everywhere: give the one you read to refuse the operation when the inventory changed since.

functions.name: classes
functions.description: Lists every equippable item the server knows: the game's own and those the running resources' KCD2 mods add through their item table patches. Names are table identifiers; nameKey is the native localization key. Maximum quality is the same bound Inventory.add enforces.

type.name: { id: string; name: string; nameKey: string; category: string; maximumQuality: number; quest: boolean }[]

functions.name: get
functions.description: Reads a player's or NPC's inventory.

returns.description: A copy, or null for an owner that no longer exists.

functions.name: add
functions.description: Gives an owner items of a class, 1 to 10000 at a time. `item` is the class GUID or the exact name the game's own item tables use, the same spelling `giveItem` takes. Left-out properties mean quality 1 at full condition; `metadata.quality` asks for a higher tier, up to what the class is made in, and `invalidQuality` refuses one past it. The units join the row that already holds this class with these properties, if there is one. A player's game announces them with its own "You received" toast unless `notify` is false.

type.name: { item: string; amount: number; metadata?: Record<string, unknown>; revision?: number; notify?: boolean }

functions.name: remove
functions.description: Takes exact units from named rows, every one of them or none. A player's game announces the loss with its own toast unless `notify` is false.

type.name: { units: InventoryUnit[]; revision?: number; notify?: boolean }

functions.name: updateCustom
functions.description: Updates only named custom fields. Null resets a display override or clears data. Supplied data replaces the old object. The whole row keeps its identity, amount and native properties.

type.name: { id: string; name?: string | null; description?: string | null; data?: Record<string, unknown> | null; revision?: number }

functions.name: setProperties
functions.description: Replaces a row's properties. The row keeps its identity and amount. It replaces rather than merges: carry over anything you want to keep, and give `health` or `condition`, not two that disagree.

type.name: { id: string; metadata: Record<string, unknown>; revision?: number }

functions.name: set
functions.description: Replaces an owner's whole inventory, which is how a saved one comes back. It is never announced in the player's game. Rows keep the ids they are given (letters, digits and `-_:.`, up to 64) and get new ones when they have none. `equipped` is how many units of a gear row the body wears, up to 48 in all; their game dresses in them. Optional quickslots restores assignments and selected slots in the current native outfit; every referenced ID must occur in items. Invalid shape or missing references returns invalidQuickslots before changing anything. Omitted or null quickslots leaves assignment to the game's normal equipment handling. Native item eligibility and slot capacity still apply. An empty list clears the inventory.

type.name: { items: { id?: string; item: string; amount: number; metadata?: Record<string, unknown>; equipped?: number }[]; quickslots?: InventoryQuickslots | null; revision?: number; harvested?: boolean }

functions.name: transfer
functions.description: Moves exact units between players or NPCs with their properties, all or nothing. They join matching rows in the target, so the target's row ids are the ones in the result's `items`. The script decides access, distance and consent. Players' games announce what they lost and gained unless `notify` is false.

type.name: { units: InventoryUnit[]; sourceRevision?: number; targetRevision?: number; notify?: boolean }

functions.name: getItemPrice
functions.description: What the game prices one unit of an item at, in money units, worked out the way the game does it. `pristine` is the price at the best health its quality allows, `current` at its own health. Quality changes the price only through that health. The metadata reads as `Inventory.add` reads it -- left out, quality 1 at full condition -- so `Inventory.getItemPrice(row.item, row.metadata)` prices a row. This is the item's own worth: what the game's shopkeepers would ask depends on their terms and the haggling, and a `Vendor` charges whatever its script says.

parameters.name: metadata
parameters.description: The item's properties, as a row's `metadata` holds them.

returns.description: Null for a class the server does not know, or metadata `Inventory.add` would refuse.

functions.name: setItemName
functions.description:
Changes what every player's game calls an item, in their inventory, the shops, loot and anywhere else the game names it; null gives the game its own name back. Every player sees it, including those who join later, until the server stops.

The game does not name classes one by one: many classes show the same name -- every kite shield is a Kite Shield -- and renaming one renames all of them. The result lists them. A name is up to 128 bytes with no control characters, and is not translated.

returns.description: The GUIDs of every class that now shows this name.

functions.name: setItemStats
functions.description:
Rewrites the combat numbers of an item class on every player's game, now and for whoever joins later, until the server stops; null gives the class its authored numbers back. The game keeps these on the class, not the item -- every `longsword` shares one row, and the hit calculation reads it on every swing -- so a change here reaches every copy of that class at once and takes effect on the next hit, with nothing to re-equip. A set that names only some stats leaves the others as authored, and replaces the previous set whole.

Which names a class takes depends on its table element: a `MeleeWeapon` has `attack`, `attackModStab`/`Slash`/`Smash`, `defense`, `strReq`, `agiReq`; `Armor`, `Helmet` and `Hood` have `defenseStab`/`Slash`/`Smash`, `noise`, `strReq`; a `MissileWeapon` has `power`, `limbResistance`, `defense`, `strReq`, `agiReq`; `Ammo` has `attackStab`/`Slash`/`Smash`, `powerMod`. Any other name, a name the element lacks, or a class that is none of these throws. Per-player or per-item numbers are not what this does: for those, put a buff on the body (`player.addBuff`, `horse.addBuff`) with a `weaponAttack`, `weaponDefense` or `attackSpeed` modifier from `Buffs.register`, or register a class of your own with `Items.register`.

type.name: { attack?: number; attackModStab?: number; attackModSlash?: number; attackModSmash?: number; defense?: number; strReq?: number; agiReq?: number; defenseStab?: number; defenseSlash?: number; defenseSmash?: number; noise?: number; power?: number; limbResistance?: number; attackStab?: number; attackSlash?: number; attackSmash?: number; powerMod?: number } | null

returns.description: True when the numbers were written; false when the class carries none of these stats.

functions.name: getItemStats
functions.description: What this server has rewritten on a class with `setItemStats`, by stat name. The authored numbers are not listed: the server does not carry the game's tables.

returns.description: The overridden stats, or null for a class left as authored.

symbols.name: Items
symbols.description: Server-defined resource items, drawn with an existing game appearance or with their own model and icon. Register types before restoring their instances.

functions.name: register
functions.description: Registers an immutable miscellaneous type and returns its stable GUID. Identical repeats succeed; conflicts throw. Defaults: empty description, price 0, stackable true, usable false, useLabel Use. visual names a miscellaneous item, crafting material or document whose model, material and icon the type borrows; without it, model and icon are required. model is a path relative to Objects/, as the game's item tables write it, which the game prefixes with Objects/ itself (a path starting with objects/ throws) and completes with .cgf when it has no extension: a model the resource streams as stream/objects/kcdc/<resource>/box.cgf is kcdc/<resource>/box.cgf. It draws the item on the ground, in hand and in the inventory preview, and needs a physics proxy for the item to be picked up from the ground: a model without one shows but cannot be picked up. material is a material path in the same form, allowed only with model; without it the model's own material is used. icon is a base64 PNG of at most 256 KiB and 4096x4096 pixels; it is scaled to the stock 64x64 icon size, aspect kept.

type.name: { name: string; description?: string; visual?: string; model?: string; material?: string; icon?: string; weight: number; price?: number; stackable?: boolean; usable?: boolean; useLabel?: string }

symbols.name: Horse
symbols.description: Replicated KCD2 horse handle.

constructor.name: constructor
constructor.description: Creates a script wrapper for an existing horse with this ID; use Horse.spawn() to spawn one.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

functions.name: toString
functions.description: Formats this horse handle for logging and debugging.

returns.description: The horse ID, its soul, and its rider.

functions.name: destroy
functions.description: Despawns this horse on every client after emitting horseDestroy.

functions.name: moveTo
functions.description: Routes an unridden horse over the server navigation mesh. Mounting cancels the order. Returns false without a mesh, for a dead or mounted horse, or invalid input.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Destination in world coordinates.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Defaults to walking and a 1.5 metre arrival radius.

functions.name: patrol
functions.description: Patrols using the NPC route state machine. Requires a loaded mesh and an alive, unridden horse. Mounting cancels the patrol.

parameters.name: points
parameters.description: One to 256 waypoints.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Defaults to walking, looping, and no wait.

functions.name: hold
functions.description: Cancels navigation and holds an unridden horse where it stands. Does not take control from a rider.

functions.name: giveTo
functions.description: Makes this horse another player's. Every client makes it that player's horse in the game's own terms -- theirs is never a stolen horse -- and `horseOwnerChanged` follows. Ownership decides nothing about who may ride it: that is `horseMounting`'s to refuse. Throws when `player` is not a connected player.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: The horse's new owner, or null to leave it ownerless.

functions.name: rearAndThrowDown
functions.description: Rears the horse on every client so it throws its rider off. The game's own animation, not a pose.

returns.description: True when the request went out; false when nobody is riding it.

functions.name: pullDownRider
functions.description: Has a player pull this horse's rider down, on every client.

parameters.name: attacker
parameters.description: The player dragging the rider out of the saddle.

returns.description: True when the request went out; false when nobody is riding it.

functions.name: dismountRider
functions.description: Takes whoever is in the saddle out of it: their own client is told to get off, and `horseDismount` is raised.

returns.description: The player taken off, or null when the saddle was already empty.

functions.name: kill
functions.description: Kills this horse on the client running it, the way any other death happens there: the body falls, anyone riding it comes off, and `horseDeath` follows with a null killer and the reason `scripted`.

returns.description: True when the horse was alive; false when it was already dead.

functions.name: revive
functions.description: Brings a dead horse back where it lies, at its full health.

returns.description: True when the horse was dead; false when it was alive.

functions.name: wake
functions.description: Brings a knocked-out horse round now, the way the game cuts a knockout short: the client running it ends the knockout and the horse gets up on every client. Its health is left as it is -- a knockout in place of a death leaves 1. The request reaches that client a moment later, so `unconscious` stays true until it reports the horse up.

returns.description: True when the request went out; false when the horse is not knocked out, is dead, or no client is running it.

functions.name: setGear
functions.description: Dresses this horse in exactly this gear on every client, the one running it included: what it wore before is taken off. Throws on an item that is not horse gear, one keyed under the wrong slot, or a caparison (`torso`) with no saddle under it. Not subject to `gearLocked` or `horseGearChanging`, which govern players; `horseGearChanged` follows with a null player.

parameters.name: gear
parameters.description: A preset from `Horse.gearPresets()` (`horse_noble05`), or item class names or GUIDs by slot from `Horse.gearItems()`, where a missing key or null leaves that slot empty; `{}` is a bare horse.

type.name: string | { saddle?: string | null; head?: string | null; torso?: string | null; shoe?: string | null }

returns.description: True when the gear was written; false when the horse is gone.

functions.name: equipGear
functions.description: Puts one piece of gear in its own slot, replacing what was there and keeping the rest.

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: An item class name or GUID from `Horse.gearItems()`.

returns.description: True when it was put on; false for an item that is not horse gear, a caparison on a horse with no saddle, or a horse that is gone.

functions.name: removeGear
functions.description: Takes one piece of gear off. Removing the saddle removes the caparison too, since it lies on the saddle.

parameters.name: slot
parameters.description: The slot to empty.

returns.description: True when something was taken off; false when the slot was already empty.

functions.name: addBuff
functions.description: Puts a status effect on this horse, on every client: the one running it, every observer's copy and whoever joins later. A horse's stats are its soul's derived stats and the game itself moves them with buffs -- horseshoes carry `rsb+0.04`, the race boosts `mst+30,rms+0.01`, horse plate `courage+5,mst+10` -- so this is how a server changes a horse's speed (`runSpeed`, `moveSpeed`), stamina (`stamina`), courage (`courage`) or carrying capacity (`carryCapacity`); `Buffs.register` builds an effect from those modifiers. The list is state rather than a one-off order: a copy that loses the effect, or a body re-spawned after a level change, is given it again. Throws for a name that is not a buff.

parameters.name: buff
parameters.description: Buff GUID, the exact name the game's own buff tables use, or the id of one registered with `Buffs.register`.

returns.description: True when it is on the horse's list, already or now; false for a horse that is gone or one already carrying sixteen.

functions.name: removeBuff
functions.description: Takes one of the server's effects off this horse, on every client. Effects the game put on the horse itself are not on the list and are left alone.

parameters.name: buff
parameters.description: Buff GUID, table name or registered id.

returns.description: True when it was on the list; false otherwise.

functions.name: hasBuff
functions.description: Whether this server has put that effect on the horse. The server's own record, so it answers at once; it says nothing about effects the game gave the horse.

parameters.name: buff
parameters.description: Buff GUID, table name or registered id.

returns.description: True when it is on the list.

functions.name: clearBuffs
functions.description: Takes every effect this server put on the horse off again.

returns.description: True when there was something to take off.

functions.name: spawn
functions.description: Spawns and replicates a horse.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Optional world-space spawn position; omitted components default to zero.

parameters.name: rotation
parameters.description: Optional initial orientation: a Quaternion, or a Vector3 of Euler angles in degrees.

parameters.name: soul
parameters.description: Optional breed from `Horse.breeds()` (`pebbles`), or a soul GUID from the game's tables; omitted spawns the generic riding horse.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Optional name every client shows for the horse; omitted leaves the name its soul carries.

parameters.name: gear
parameters.description: Optional gear the horse is born wearing on every client, as `setGear` takes it; `{}` spawns it bare. Omitted, it wears the game's own tack: a named horse's own preset, or one of the generic ones (`horse_common01`, `horse_common02`).

type.name: string | { saddle?: string | null; head?: string | null; torso?: string | null; shoe?: string | null }

returns.description: The newly spawned horse handle.

functions.name: gearPresets
functions.description: The game's own sets of horse tack, from its clothing presets: the generic `horse_common`, `horse_noble`, `horse_nomad` and `horse_draft` families, and the named horses' own. Any of them goes to `setGear` or `Horse.spawn` by name.

returns.description: Preset names, alphabetical.

functions.name: gearItems
functions.description: Every item class a horse can wear, from the game's own tables: saddles, bridles and chanfrons, caparisons and trappings, horseshoes.

parameters.name: slot
parameters.description: Only the gear for this slot; omitted lists all of it.

returns.description: Item class names, saddles first.

functions.name: breeds
functions.description: The horses `Horse.spawn` knows by name: every horse the game gives a character of its own -- the ones its traders sell and the named horses of its quests -- plus `horse`, the generic one.

returns.description: Breed names, `horse` first and the rest alphabetical.

functions.name: all
functions.description: Lists every horse the server currently has.

returns.description: One handle per live horse, in no particular order.

functions.name: getById
functions.description: Looks a horse up by its network entity ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

returns.description: The horse's handle, or null when no live horse has that ID.

properties.name: navigationStatus
properties.description: The current route's status: idle, running, reached, blocked, or failed.

properties.name: buffs
properties.description: The effects this server has put on the horse, as `addBuff` names them: the table name of a native effect, the registered id of a custom one, in the order they were added.

properties.name: gear
properties.description: What this horse wears, by slot: `saddle` (the saddlebags are part of it, and so is the carrying capacity they add), `head` (a bridle or chanfron), `torso` (a caparison), `shoe`. Item class names, null for an empty slot. A spawned horse wears the game's own tack for it unless `Horse.spawn` said otherwise. The gear changes the horse's stats as well as its look.

type.name: { saddle: string | null; head: string | null; torso: string | null; shoe: string | null }

properties.name: gearLocked
properties.description: While true, players' own changes to this horse's gear are refused and put back, before `horseGearChanging` is asked. Scripts can still change it. False by default.

properties.name: soul
properties.description: GUID of the soul this horse was spawned against, which decides its appearance.

properties.name: name
properties.description: Name every client shows for this horse. Assignment renames it on all of them; empty means the name its soul carries stands. A rider keeps the name it mounted with until it dismounts.

properties.name: inventoryCapacity
properties.description: What this horse can carry, in the game's own weight units, or 0 before any client has reported it. Derived by the engine, so read-only.

properties.name: riderId
properties.description: Network ID of the player in the saddle, or 0 when the horse is riderless.

properties.name: rider
properties.description: The player in the saddle, or null when the horse is riderless.

properties.name: mounted
properties.description: Whether a player is currently riding this horse.

properties.name: ownerId
properties.description: Network ID of the player this horse belongs to, or 0 when it is nobody's. Not necessarily its rider.

properties.name: owner
properties.description: The player this horse belongs to, or null when it is nobody's. Set with `giveTo`.

properties.name: destroyWithOwner
properties.description: Whether this horse is despawned when its owner disconnects. True by default. Set it to false to keep the horse in the world: it is left ownerless instead (`horseOwnerChanged` with a null player) until `giveTo` hands it to someone. Saving it across server restarts is the script's own business.

properties.name: health
properties.description: Health, as the client running this horse last reported it off the animal's own soul -- 0 before any client has. Assigning sets it on that client, clamped to `maxHealth`; 0 kills. A dead horse ignores the write: `revive` is what brings one back.

properties.name: maxHealth
properties.description: The most health this horse can have, from its soul; 0 before any client has run it.

properties.name: stamina
properties.description: Stamina, as its client last reported it -- the bar the game draws for a ridden horse, spent by galloping. Read-only: the game runs it.

properties.name: maxStamina
properties.description: The most stamina this horse can have; 0 before any client has run it.

properties.name: alive
properties.description: False once the horse has died. A dead horse is still an entity: its body stays where it fell, nobody can ride it, and `revive` or `destroy` are the ways out.

properties.name: unconscious
properties.description: True while the client running this horse reports it knocked out: alive, but lying where it fell. The game knocks a horse out rather than killing it when it holds the horse immortal, as it holds a player's own horse. The horse comes round by itself when the knockout wears off, some minutes later, as in the game, or at once with `wake`. False for a dead horse, and before any client has run this one.

symbols.name: DialogueOption
symbols.description: One row of a page.

properties.name: id
properties.description: What comes back on `dialogueChoice` when this row is picked. An id, never an index, so a handler stays correct when the page is rebuilt with different rows.

properties.name: text
properties.description: The line the player reads. Server-authored text reaches the game's own list as written; it is not a localization key.

properties.name: enabled
properties.description: Draws the row greyed and unpickable when false. A rendering hint only -- the server re-checks the choice when it arrives, so nothing a row costs may rely on this.

symbols.name: DialoguePage
symbols.description: A line and the options under it.

properties.name: line
properties.description: Shown above the options. Omit it for a list with no preamble.

properties.name: onRight
properties.description: Draws the list on the right of the screen instead of the left.

properties.name: options
properties.description: The rows, at least one and at most eight. A page with none is refused.

symbols.name: Dialogue
symbols.description:
Conversations the server drives on a player, in the game's own dialogue list.

A conversation is attached to nothing. It runs on a player and what it is about -- a smith, a notice board, a chest, a timer -- is this gamemode's own business, held in its own closures. That is deliberate and it has a cost: nothing here watches distance, line of sight or whether anyone died, because none of that is knowable without the relationship it refuses to hold. Close the conversation yourself when the fiction says it should end.

functions.name: open
functions.description: Opens a conversation and shows its first page. A player already in one has it closed with reason 2 first, because the game has a single choice list and stacking them would lie about which is live.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: NetworkID of the player the conversation runs on.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The first page. `options` is required and carries at most 8 rows; each needs an `id` and a `text`, and may set `enabled`. `line` and `onRight` are optional.

returns.description: The session id, or 0 when the page was unusable or the player is gone.

functions.name: update
functions.description: Replaces the page a live conversation is showing. Each page carries a generation the client echoes, so an answer still in flight against the page this replaces is dropped rather than misapplied.

parameters.name: session
parameters.description: The session to advance.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to show instead.

returns.description: False when that session has already ended.

functions.name: close
functions.description: Ends a conversation and takes the list off that player's screen.

parameters.name: session
parameters.description: The session to end.

returns.description: False when the session had already ended.

functions.name: sessionOf
functions.description: The conversation that player is in.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: NetworkID of the player to ask about.

returns.description: The session id, or 0 when they are not in one.

symbols.name: VendorOptions
symbols.description: How a vendor starts out.

properties.name: name
properties.description: Shown in the server's log only. The trade screen names whoever keeps the shop.

properties.name: purse
properties.description: Money units the vendor starts with, and all it can pay out. Omit it for a purse that never runs out.

properties.name: buys
properties.description: Whether the vendor takes the player's items at all. On by default; `setBuyPrices` says which ones.

symbols.name: VendorStockRow
symbols.description: One thing a vendor sells.

properties.name: item
properties.description: The item class, by GUID or by the game's own item name.

properties.name: amount
properties.description: How many the vendor has. A row the players buy out disappears.

properties.name: price
properties.description: What one costs, in money units -- the amount of the game's `money` item, which is also what `player.giveItem('money', n)` hands out.

properties.name: metadata
properties.description: Item properties, including custom display overrides and private data. Preserved when bought.

symbols.name: VendorBuyRow
symbols.description: One thing a vendor buys from players.

properties.name: item
properties.description: The item class, by GUID or by the game's own item name.

properties.name: price
properties.description: What the vendor pays for one, in money units.

symbols.name: VendorTradeLine
symbols.description: One settled line of a deal.

properties.name: metadata
properties.description: Exact item properties, including private custom data. Sold variants appear as separate lines.

properties.name: item
properties.description: The item class GUID.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The game's own name for the item class.

properties.name: amount
properties.description: How many changed hands.

properties.name: price
properties.description: What one was priced at when the deal settled.

symbols.name: Vendor
symbols.description:
Price lists and purses the server owns, traded on the game's own shop screen.

A vendor is attached to nothing: open one in front of a player from wherever the gamemode decides the counter is -- `npcInteract`, a dialogue option, a command. The screen is a preview. Its prices come from here, and pressing Trade sends a basket that the server re-prices, settles and moves itself; nothing the client shows is trusted.

Prices count in money units, the amount of the game's `money` item.

functions.name: create
functions.description: Creates a vendor with nothing to sell and nothing it buys.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Name, starting purse and whether it buys. All optional.

returns.description: The vendor id.

functions.name: destroy
functions.description: Closes every session at the vendor and forgets it. A deal settles the moment its basket arrives, so none is ever left half done.

parameters.name: vendor
parameters.description: The vendor to remove.

returns.description: False when there was no such vendor.

functions.name: setStock
functions.description: Replaces what a vendor sells. Every player with its screen open sees the new shelf straight away, and a basket priced against the old one is refused.

parameters.name: vendor
parameters.description: The vendor to stock.

parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: Everything it sells, at most 128 rows and each item class once. Replaces the old list.

returns.description: False when there is no such vendor.

functions.name: setBuyPrices
functions.description: Replaces what a vendor buys from players and what it pays. Anything not listed is shown at no value and a basket selling it is refused.

parameters.name: vendor
parameters.description: The vendor to change.

parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: Everything it buys, at most 128 rows and each item class once. Replaces the old list.

returns.description: False when there is no such vendor.

functions.name: setPurse
functions.description: Sets what a vendor can pay out. Deals keep it current: what players pay goes in, what they are paid comes out.

parameters.name: vendor
parameters.description: The vendor to change.

parameters.name: purse
parameters.description: Money units it holds, or null for a purse that never runs out.

returns.description: False when there is no such vendor.

functions.name: getPurse
functions.description: What a vendor holds.

parameters.name: vendor
parameters.description: The vendor to ask about.

returns.description: Money units, or null for a purse that never runs out or a vendor that does not exist.

functions.name: open
functions.description: Opens the game's own trade screen on a player. A player already trading has that session closed with reason 2 first, because the game has one trade screen.

parameters.name: vendor
parameters.description: The vendor to trade with.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: NetworkID of the player to show it to.

parameters.name: npc
parameters.description: NetworkID of the NPC who keeps the shop. The screen shows that NPC as the trader; omit it to trade with nobody in particular.

returns.description: The session id, or 0 when the vendor or the player is gone.

functions.name: close
functions.description: Takes the trade screen off that player.

parameters.name: session
parameters.description: The session to end.

returns.description: False when the session had already ended.

functions.name: sessionOf
functions.description: The trading session a player is in.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: NetworkID of the player to ask about.

returns.description: The session id, or 0 when they are not trading.

functions.name: vendorOf
functions.description: The vendor a session trades with.

parameters.name: session
parameters.description: The session to ask about.

returns.description: The vendor id, or 0 when the session has ended.

symbols.name: PickpocketLine
symbols.description: One item class that left a victim's pockets for a thief's.

properties.name: item
properties.description: The item class GUID.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The game's own name for the item class.

properties.name: amount
properties.description: How many moved.

symbols.name: DiceTableInfo
symbols.description: A dice table placed by the current level. The catalog includes quest-layer tables that may not currently be loaded on a client.

properties.name: id
properties.description: The table's GUID as sixteen lowercase hex digits: the level's own, or the one a placed table's clients build it under.

properties.name: placed
properties.description: Whether a script or a World Builder export placed the table, rather than the level.

properties.name: position
properties.description: The world-space midpoint between the table's two seat alignment points, in metres. The behavior entity itself may be offset from this interaction centre.

properties.name: seats
properties.description: The two sitting smart-object GUIDs, in native seat order. Compare with a seated player's seatGuid; these are not the minigame's alignment tagpoints.

symbols.name: DiceMatchOptions
symbols.description: How a dice match is played.

properties.name: targetScore
properties.description: The score that wins, banked at the end of a turn. 2000 when omitted, at most 100000.

properties.name: firstName
properties.description: First seat's scoreboard label, up to 64 UTF-8 bytes without control characters. Empty or omitted uses the native label.

properties.name: secondName
properties.description: Second seat's scoreboard label. Each client maps the seat to its local or opponent column.

symbols.name: DiceProgressEvent
symbols.description: An accepted server dice action. Notifications describe server decisions, which can precede the native animation. Seats and die-mask bits start at zero; turns and rolls start at one.

properties.name: match
properties.description: Match ID.

properties.name: player
properties.description: Network ID of the acting player, or of the NPC on the second seat.

properties.name: seat
properties.description: Acting seat: 0 for first, 1 for second.

properties.name: turn
properties.description: Turn number across both seats, starting at 1.

properties.name: roll
properties.description: Roll within the turn; 0 before its first roll.

properties.name: moveIndex
properties.description: Number of accepted moves so far.

properties.name: turnScore
properties.description: Unbanked points in this turn, before they are lost on a bust or banked on a pass.

properties.name: totalScore
properties.description: This seat's banked score.

properties.name: faces
properties.description: Six pip values (1 through 6) in die-index order on diceRoll; empty on other events. rolledMask identifies the dice rolled this time.

properties.name: rolledMask
properties.description: Bit mask of dice rolled, on diceRoll; zero otherwise.

properties.name: heldMask
properties.description: Bit mask of dice selected in the accepted move; zero otherwise.

properties.name: points
properties.description: Points added by diceMove or banked by a passed diceTurnEnd; zero otherwise.

properties.name: reason
properties.description: continue or pass on diceMove; bust or rolled on diceRoll; pass, bust, won, gaveUp, left, timedOut, failed, or stopped on diceTurnEnd; empty on diceTurnStart.

symbols.name: Dice
symbols.description:
Dice matches between two players, or a player and a server NPC, on the game's own dice table.

Both players sit down at the dice table nearest them and play it as they would against an NPC, the other player's body opposite. Every throw is dealt and every move checked by the server, by the game's own scoring rules; badges and dice perks are off, so a match is decided by the dice and the decisions alone.

An Npc may hold the second seat. Its body sits opposite the player, its throws are dealt like anyone's, and its decisions are the script's: `diceRoll` says what it threw, `Dice.move` plays its move.

functions.name: tables
functions.description: Lists the dice tables players in a virtual world can play at, and their seats: the level's own, minus any a level edit took out of that world, and every table `SmartObject.spawn` or a World Builder export placed there or in the global world. Readiness and occupancy belong to the gamemode.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world whose tables to list; the global one when omitted.

returns.description: The tables, in no particular order.

functions.name: start
functions.description: Starts a match. Both players must stand together, within a few metres, at a dice table, and neither may be playing already. An NPC is held to the same: it must stand at the table with the player, in the same virtual world. Throws an Error saying why when it cannot start.

parameters.name: first
parameters.description: NetworkID of the player on the table's first seat.

parameters.name: second
parameters.description: NetworkID of the player on the second seat, or of a living human Npc to seat there and play through Dice.move.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: The target score. Optional.

returns.description: The match id.

functions.name: move
functions.description: Plays the move of the NPC on the second seat, checked by the rules a player's move is. Legal only while it is the NPC's turn and its throw is on the table, so after a `diceRoll` naming it with reason `rolled`; calling it from that handler is supported. An accepted move raises `diceMove` and what follows from it. The NPC forfeits like a player when no move is accepted for three minutes.

parameters.name: match
parameters.description: Match ID.

parameters.name: heldMask
parameters.description: Bit mask of the dice to set aside, bit 0 for die 0 through bit 5 for die 5, among those `diceRoll` reported in `rolledMask`. Every die in it must count towards a scoring combination.

parameters.name: pass
parameters.description: True banks the turn after scoring the held dice, if any. False scores them, which needs at least one, and throws the rest.

returns.description: False, with nothing changed, when the match has ended or has no NPC seat, it is not the NPC's turn, or the move is not legal.

functions.name: setNames
functions.description: Changes both scoreboard labels on the next native scoreboard refresh. Empty restores a native label. Names allow at most 64 UTF-8 bytes and no control characters.

parameters.name: match
parameters.description: Match ID.

parameters.name: first
