parameters.description: First seat label.

parameters.name: second
parameters.description: Second seat label.

returns.description: False if the match has ended.

functions.name: stop
functions.description: Ends a match with nobody winning; both tables close.

parameters.name: match
parameters.description: The match to end.

returns.description: False when it had already ended.

functions.name: matchOf
functions.description: The match a player is in.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: NetworkID of the player to ask about.

returns.description: The match id, or 0.

symbols.name: CraftStartProposal
symbols.description: A table a player is about to open, or a workpiece about to take its materials. Frozen: a handler can refuse it, not change it.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: Which craft.

properties.name: station
properties.description: Station id, as `Crafting.stations` names it.

properties.name: virtualWorld
properties.description: The player's virtual world; each world has its own stations.

properties.name: recipe
properties.description: Smithing only: the recipe id the player chose, as `Crafting.recipes` keys it.

properties.name: continuationOf
properties.description: The batch this one follows at a table the player kept, or empty for a fresh entry. Always empty for smithing.

symbols.name: CraftStartedEvent
symbols.description: A batch that is now brewing, or a workpiece whose materials were taken.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: Which craft.

properties.name: session
properties.description: The batch's or workpiece's session id.

properties.name: station
properties.description: Station id.

properties.name: virtualWorld
properties.description: The station's virtual world.

properties.name: recipe
properties.description: Smithing only: the recipe being worked.

properties.name: continuationOf
properties.description: The previous batch at this table, or empty for the first. Always empty for smithing.

symbols.name: CraftCompletionProposal
symbols.description: What a finished batch or workpiece is about to grant, computed by the server. Frozen: a handler can refuse it, not change it.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: Which craft.

properties.name: session
properties.description: The session id.

properties.name: station
properties.description: Station id.

properties.name: outcome
properties.description: `failed` brews the game's failed potion. A smithing proposal is always `success`: a failed workpiece grants nothing to review.

properties.name: recipe
properties.description: The recipe the brew matched, or empty when it matched none; the smithing recipe worked.

properties.name: grade
properties.description: The product's native rank; for smithing, its item quality tier.

properties.name: product
properties.description: Item class GUID of what would be granted, or empty when nothing is: a zero alchemy yield, or a smithing quest product its quest creates.

properties.name: amount
properties.description: How many.

properties.name: quality

symbols.name: Crafting
symbols.description: Crafting catalogs, station occupancy, alchemy and smithing sessions, and alchemy recipe knowledge. Held in memory for each connection; nothing is saved.

functions.name: isAvailable
functions.description: True: alchemy and smithing are both ruled by the server. Omitted kind checks alchemy.

functions.name: stations
functions.description: The stations players in a virtual world can craft at: the level's own, minus any a level edit took out of that world, and every station `SmartObject.spawn` or a World Builder export placed there or in the global world. Does not load deferred layers or bypass quests.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world whose stations to list; the global one when omitted.

functions.name: recipes
functions.description: Every recipe enabled by server DLC policy: the game's, then streamed mods' and scripts' in the order they were added. A mod's table patch row with a game recipe's id replaces it in place. The player must be connected but does not change the list. Catalog presence does not establish knowledge or skill.

functions.name: registerRecipe
functions.description: Adds an alchemy or smithing recipe for the rest of the server's life. The server brews and forges it by the same rules as the game's recipes, `Crafting.recipes` lists it, and every client, including one that joins later, adds it to the game's own recipe book and smithy. Registering the same definition again does nothing. Throws for a malformed definition, an item the catalog does not know, an id the game or another resource uses, or a different definition under an id already registered.

functions.name: session
functions.description: The player's alchemy session or the table they kept between batches, else their smithing workpiece, else null.

functions.name: occupancy
functions.description: Who holds a station. World defaults to 0. Null for an unknown station.

functions.name: cancel
functions.description: Ends the player's session as leaving the station would, and their game closes it. Alchemy: wholly unmilled groups go back to the inventory, the rest is spent. Smithing: the workpiece fails, spending its failure share. `craftingEnded` follows next tick. False when there was nothing to end.

functions.name: knowledge
functions.description: The player's recipe knowledge: recipe id to a mask of its 29 authored steps, 536870911 when the whole recipe is known. A recipe not listed is unknown. Starts empty every session; save it from `craftingCompleted` or here and restore it with `setKnowledge`.

functions.name: setKnowledge
functions.description: Sets which steps of one recipe the player knows, and sends it to their game's recipe book. 0 forgets the recipe. False for an unknown recipe, a mask above 536870911, or a player who is not connected.

symbols.name: Dog

functions.name: giveTo

parameters.name: player

functions.name: spawn
functions.description: Spawns and replicates a dog companion for a player.

functions.name: all

functions.name: getById

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

returns.description: The dog's handle, or null when no live dog has that ID.

properties.name: soul
properties.description: GUID of the soul this dog was spawned against, which decides its appearance.

properties.name: name
properties.description: Name every client shows for this dog. Assignment renames it on all of them; empty means the name its soul carries stands.

properties.name: ownerId
properties.description: Network ID of the player this dog belongs to, or 0 when it has no master.

properties.name: owner
properties.description: The player this dog belongs to, or null when it has no master.

properties.name: destroyWithOwner
properties.description: Whether this dog is despawned when its owner disconnects. True by default. Set it to false to keep the dog in the world: it is left masterless instead (`dogOwnerChanged` with a null player), and with nobody's game running its brain it stands where it was until `giveTo` hands it to someone. Saving it across server restarts is the script's own business.

properties.name: objective

symbols.name: Prop
symbols.description: Replicated static mesh handle.

constructor.name: constructor
constructor.description: Creates a script wrapper for an existing prop with this ID; use Prop.spawn() to spawn one.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

functions.name: toString
functions.description: Formats this prop handle for logging and debugging.

returns.description: The prop ID, its model, its physics and its scale.

functions.name: destroy
functions.description: Despawns this prop on every client after emitting propDestroy.

functions.name: applyImpulse
functions.description: Pushes a `rigid` prop's body and wakes it. The nearest player's client simulates the body and every other player sees the pose it streams. `propRest` is raised once it stops.

parameters.name: impulse
parameters.description: The push in kg m/s, world space. The body's velocity changes by this divided by its mass, so a heavy prop needs a large number.

parameters.name: point
parameters.description: Where the push lands, in world space. Off the centre of mass it also turns the body, which is what topples a tall one. Omitted, it lands on the centre of mass.

parameters.name: angularImpulse
parameters.description: A twist on top, in kg m^2/s about each world axis.

returns.description: True when it was sent to the client simulating the prop; false when the prop is gone or is not `rigid`, a value is not finite or is out of range, or no player is within 60 m to simulate it.

functions.name: setVelocity
functions.description: Sets a `rigid` prop's velocity outright, whatever its mass, and wakes it. `propRest` is raised once it stops.

parameters.name: velocity
parameters.description: Its new velocity in m/s, world space, up to 200.

parameters.name: angularVelocity
parameters.description: Its new spin in radians per second about each world axis, up to 100. Omitted, it stops turning.

returns.description: True when it was sent to the client simulating the prop; false when the prop is gone or is not `rigid`, a value is not finite or is out of range, or no player is within 60 m to simulate it.

functions.name: wake
functions.description: Starts a resting `rigid` prop simulating where it lies, so it falls if nothing holds it up. `propRest` is raised once it stops.

returns.description: True when it was sent to the client simulating the prop; false when the prop is gone or is not `rigid`, a value is not finite or is out of range, or no player is within 60 m to simulate it.

functions.name: sleep
functions.description: Stops a `rigid` prop's body where it is, in mid-air if need be. It wakes again when something hits it or a script moves it. `propRest` then reports where it stopped. To fix a prop in place for good, set `physics` to `static` once `propRest` has been raised.

returns.description: True when it was sent to the client simulating the prop; false when the prop is gone or is not `rigid`, a value is not finite or is out of range, or no player is within 60 m to simulate it.

functions.name: resetPhysics
functions.description: Stops a `rigid` prop's body and puts it back where it was spawned, for every player. Raises no `propRest`.

returns.description: True when it was put back; false when the prop is gone or is not `rigid`.

functions.name: spawn
functions.description: Spawns and replicates a static mesh from the game's own object catalog.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Mesh to build, as either a full catalog path (`objects/manmade/barrels/barrel_a.cgf`) or its file stem (`barrel_a`). A stem several meshes share resolves to the first of them, so pass the path when it matters which. A mesh this server streams -- a `.cgf` in a resource's `stream/objects/kcdc/<resource>/` folder -- is named by its full path, `objects/kcdc/<resource>/chair.cgf`; a player whose game does not have it yet sees the prop as soon as it does.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Optional world-space spawn position; omitted components default to zero.

parameters.name: rotation
parameters.description: Optional initial orientation: a Quaternion, or a Vector3 of Euler angles in degrees.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: Uniform size or separate X/Y/Z sizes, each from 0.01 to 100. Omitted uses the mesh size. Nonuniform collision follows the native engine limitations.

parameters.name: physics
parameters.description: Optional collision: `static` (the default), `rigid` or `none`.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world the prop belongs to; omitted puts it in the global one.

returns.description: The newly spawned prop handle.

functions.name: all
functions.description: Lists every prop the server currently has.

returns.description: One handle per live prop, in no particular order.

functions.name: getById
functions.description: Looks a prop up by its network entity ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

returns.description: The prop's handle, or null when no live prop has that ID.

functions.name: destroyAll
functions.description: Despawns props, emitting propDestroy for each one.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to clear; omitted clears every one of them.

returns.description: How many props were removed.

properties.name: model
properties.description: Catalog path of the mesh this prop was built from, e.g. `objects/manmade/barrels/barrel_a.cgf`. Read-only: the collision is built from the mesh when the entity is spawned and never re-read, so a prop is the model it was created with.

properties.name: modelName
properties.description: File stem of the mesh, e.g. `barrel_a`, which is the short name `Prop.spawn` also accepts.

properties.name: modelGroup
properties.description: Browsing bucket the mesh sits in, e.g. `manmade/structures`; `kcdc/<resource>` for a mesh the server streams.

properties.name: physics
properties.description: What this prop's collision does: `static` collides but never moves, `rigid` falls and can be pushed, `none` has none at all. Assignment rebuilds the prop on every client. A rigid one is simulated by the nearest player's client within 60 m, and every other player sees the pose it streams; with nobody that near, it stays where it last rested.

properties.name: mass
properties.description: A `rigid` prop's mass in kilograms, given to its body as it is built; 0, the default, takes the mass the mesh's collision gives it. Up to 100,000; a value outside 0 to 100,000 is ignored. Set it for a mesh whose collision carries no mass, such as a tree's: without one, every client builds such a prop as a `static` one, which stands still and cannot be pushed, and logs why. Assignment rebuilds the prop on every client, so set it before pushing it.

properties.name: scale
properties.description: Uniform scale, from 0.01 to 100; a value outside that is clamped into it. Assignment rebuilds the prop on every client, because the collision is sized from the scale at spawn and never re-read.

symbols.description: Replicated particle effect handle.

functions.description: Stops this effect on every client that can see it, after emitting vfxDestroy.

functions.name: spawn
functions.description: Places a particle effect in the world and leaves it running. It is a replicated entity, so the interest grid streams it to whoever comes near and takes it away again when they leave -- which is what a campfire, a torch or a plume of smoke needs and what `burst` cannot do. How far it streams is taken from the effect's own draw distance, between 25 and 250 metres.

parameters.name: effect
parameters.description: Effect to place, spelled as the game's particle libraries spell it -- `WH_Particels.fires.campfire_a`. `Vfx.list()` is the whole vocabulary.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Optional world-space position; omitted components default to zero.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `rotation` aims the emitter; `scale`, `countScale`, `speedScale` and `timeScale` multiply what the effect authored; `strength` feeds its strength curves; `pulsePeriod` restarts it on that many seconds; `prime` starts it already running, which is what a fire wants. `durationMs` is ignored here -- a placed effect lasts until it is destroyed.

type.name: { rotation?: Quaternion | Vector3; scale?: number; countScale?: number; speedScale?: number; timeScale?: number; strength?: number; pulsePeriod?: number; prime?: boolean; durationMs?: number }

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world the effect belongs to; omitted puts it in the global one.

returns.description: The newly placed effect handle.

functions.name: burst
functions.description: Plays an effect once for the players who can see the point it happens at, and keeps nothing. Recipients are chosen by the effect's own draw distance -- there is no point telling a client about something its engine would not draw -- so a blood spray reaches the people standing there and nobody else. A player who arrives afterwards sees nothing, which is the right answer for a spark and the wrong one for a campfire; use `spawn` for those.

parameters.name: effect
parameters.description: Effect to play, spelled as the game's particle libraries spell it.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Where it happens, in world-space metres.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: As `spawn`, and here `durationMs` does apply: how long each client keeps the emitter, two seconds by default and a minute at most.

type.name: { rotation?: Quaternion | Vector3; scale?: number; countScale?: number; speedScale?: number; timeScale?: number; strength?: number; pulsePeriod?: number; prime?: boolean; durationMs?: number }

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world; omitted uses the global one.

returns.description: How many clients were told.

functions.name: burstOn
functions.description: Plays an effect once on a replicated entity, where it follows that entity: blood on the body that was hit, sparks on the weapon that struck. A client that has not streamed the entity in drops it rather than playing it somewhere else.

parameters.name: effect
parameters.description: Effect to play, spelled as the game's particle libraries spell it.

parameters.name: entity
parameters.description: What to hang it on: any replicated handle -- a Player, Prop, Horse or Dog -- or a bare network entity ID.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: As `burst`, plus `offset`: where the emitter sits in the entity's own space, in metres, up to 8 m from its origin.

type.name: { offset?: Vector3; rotation?: Quaternion | Vector3; scale?: number; countScale?: number; speedScale?: number; timeScale?: number; strength?: number; pulsePeriod?: number; prime?: boolean; durationMs?: number }

returns.description: How many clients were told.

functions.name: all
functions.description: Lists every replicated effect the server currently has.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to list; omitted lists every one of them.

returns.description: One handle per live effect, in no particular order.

functions.name: getById
functions.description: Looks a replicated effect up by its network entity ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

returns.description: The effect's handle, or null when no live effect has that ID.

functions.name: destroyAll
functions.description: Stops replicated effects, emitting vfxDestroy for each one.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to clear; omitted clears every one of them.

returns.description: How many effects were stopped.

functions.name: list
functions.description: Every effect name the shipped game declares, in order. Mined from the game's particle libraries at build time, so it is the same list the client has.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: Keep only the names starting with this, e.g. `WH_Particels.fires` or `collisions.combat`.

returns.description: The matching names.

properties.name: effect
properties.description: Name of the particle effect this is playing, e.g. `WH_Particels.fires.campfire_a`. Read-only: every spawn parameter is read once when the emitter is created, so an effect is the one it was placed as.

properties.name: library
properties.description: Particle library the effect came out of, e.g. `WH_Particels`, which is the part of the name before the first dot.

properties.name: group
properties.description: Authored bucket inside that library, e.g. `fires`.

properties.name: scale
properties.description: Multiplies every size the effect authored, from 0.01 to 32; a value outside that is clamped into it. Assignment rebuilds the emitter on every client that can see it, so the effect restarts.

properties.name: countScale
properties.description: Multiplies how many particles are emitted, from 0.01 to 16. Assignment restarts the effect.

properties.name: speedScale
properties.description: Multiplies emission speed, from 0 to 16. Assignment restarts the effect.

properties.name: timeScale
properties.description: Multiplies how fast the emitter's own time runs, from 0.01 to 16. Assignment restarts the effect.

properties.name: strength
properties.description: Feeds the effect's own strength curves, from -1 to 1; -1 leaves them where the effect authored them. Assignment restarts the effect.

properties.name: pulsePeriod
properties.description: Seconds between restarts of the whole emitter, from 0 to 600; 0 never restarts it. Assignment restarts the effect.

parameters.name: id

symbols.name: Camera
symbols.description: One player's view, directed from the server. A shot is sent and forgotten: the server keeps no record of it, so a player who reconnects or changes level has their own view until they are sent another.

functions.name: setShot
functions.description:
Films one player's view from a fixed point: what a cutscene, an intro or a kill cam is made of. It holds until `clearShot`, or glides on to the next `setShot`.

This is the client's `Camera.setShot`, sent to that player; whichever of the two comes last wins. Nothing about the player's controls changes, and nothing about where their body is: their character stays where it stood, drawn head and all for as long as the camera is looking at it from outside its eyes. A player flying with `NoClip` refuses the shot.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: Whose view to film.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `position` is where the camera stands and `lookAt` the point it faces, both in world space. `duration` is how long it takes to get there from wherever the player's view is, in milliseconds: 0, the default, is a cut, and the most is 60000. `fov` is the vertical field of view in degrees, 20 to 120; leave it out to keep the player's own.

type.name: { position: Vector3; lookAt: Vector3; duration?: number; fov?: number }

returns.description: True when the shot was sent, false when `position` and `lookAt` are the same point.

functions.name: clearShot
functions.description: Gives a player their own view back. Harmless for a player without a shot.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: Whose view to give back.

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: How long the glide back into the player's eyes takes, in milliseconds: 0, the default, is a cut, and the most is 60000.

returns.description: True when it was sent.

symbols.name: Marker
symbols.description: Replicated ground marker handle.

constructor.name: constructor
constructor.description: Creates a script wrapper for an existing marker with this ID; use Marker.place() to draw one.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

functions.name: toString
functions.description: Formats this marker handle for logging and debugging.

returns.description: The marker ID, its material and its size.

functions.name: remove
functions.description: Removes this marker from every client that can see it, after emitting markerRemove.

functions.name: place
functions.description: Puts a marker in the world and leaves it there. It is a replicated entity, so the interest grid streams it to whoever comes near and takes it away again when they leave -- which is what a zone or a checkpoint needs and what a one-shot message cannot do. How far it streams is taken from its own extent, between 50 and 400 metres.

parameters.name: material
parameters.description: Decal material to project, spelled as the game's own data spells it -- `materials/decals/chalk_cross`. `Marker.list()` is the whole vocabulary.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Optional world-space position; omitted components default to zero.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `shape` picks what it is made of -- `decal` projects onto the surface under it, the rest stand in the world as meshes and can be seen from below a ridge. `rotation` aims it, so a marker laid on a wall is the same call with a different rotation; `size` and `height` are its extent in metres; `spin` and `bob` give a mesh marker motion; `color` tints it.

type.name: { shape?: 'decal' | 'cylinder' | 'sphere' | 'chevron' | 'cube' | 'plane'; rotation?: Quaternion | Vector3; size?: number; height?: number; spin?: number; bob?: number; color?: number; trigger?: boolean }

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world the marker belongs to; omitted puts it in the global one.

returns.description: The newly drawn marker handle.

functions.description: Lists every replicated marker the server currently has.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to list; omitted lists every one of them.

returns.description: One handle per live marker, in no particular order.

functions.name: getById
functions.description: Looks a replicated marker up by its network entity ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

returns.description: The marker's handle, or null when no live marker has that ID.

functions.name: removeAll
functions.description: Removes markers, emitting markerRemove for each one.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to clear; omitted clears every one of them.

returns.description: How many markers were removed.

functions.name: list
functions.description: Every decal material the shipped game preloads, in order. Mined from the game's own material folder at build time, so it is the same list the client has.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: Keep only the names starting with this, e.g. `materials/decals/burglar`.

returns.description: The matching names.

properties.name: material
properties.description: Decal material this marker is drawn with, e.g. `materials/decals/chalk_cross`. Read-only: a decal node reads its material once, so a marker is the one it was placed as.

properties.name: group
properties.description: Subfolder the material came out of under `materials/decals/`, empty at the top level.

properties.name: shape
properties.description: What the marker is made of: `decal` for the projected one, or `cylinder`, `sphere`, `chevron`, `cube` or `plane` for a mesh standing in the world. Read-only: changing it is a rebuild, so place a new marker instead.

properties.name: size
properties.description: How wide the marker is, in metres, from 0.25 to 64; a value outside that is clamped into it. Assignment restates it in place rather than rebuilding, and widens how far the marker streams.

properties.name: height
properties.description: How tall a mesh marker stands, in metres, from 0.25 to 64. Ignored by `decal`, `sphere` and `plane`, which are sized by width alone.

properties.name: spin
properties.description: Degrees per second the marker turns about its own up axis, from -720 to 720; 0 stands still. Played on each client's own clock, so two players need not see it at the same angle. Ignored by `decal`.

properties.name: color
properties.description: Packed 0xRRGGBBAA tint, or 0 for the material as it ships. The shipped material is shared by everything that names it, so a tint is a private clone rather than a write to the original -- which is why assignment rebuilds the marker.

properties.name: trigger
properties.description: Whether clients watch the local player against this marker's volume and report crossings, which is what raises `markerEnter` and `markerExit`. Off by default: a marker nobody listens to should cost nothing but its draw.

properties.name: bob
properties.description: How far the marker rises and falls from its resting height, in metres, up to 4; 0 stands still. Played on each client's own clock. Ignored by `decal`, which cannot leave the surface it projects onto.

constructor.name: constructor

It is a replicated entity that is never culled by distance -- a blip is for finding something far away -- so it reaches players however far they are and whenever they join, and assigning `position` moves it for all of them. `setVisibleTo` works on it like on any entity.

returns.description: The new blip handle.

functions.name: all
functions.description: Lists every blip the server currently has.

properties.name: type
properties.description: Which of the game's own compass icons the blip draws as, by the game's own name for it -- `Blip.types()` lists them. Assigning a name the game does not know leaves the blip as it was.

properties.name: markState
properties.description: The mark's state, forwarded to the compass and map movies as-is -- what the client Blip calls `state`, renamed here because every entity's `state` is its StateBag. What a given value draws is undocumented; 0 is what a fresh game mark carries.

properties.name: label
properties.description: The blip's name on the map screen, shown verbatim in place of the name the game gives its icon type; empty keeps that name. Cut to 64 bytes. The compass has no text, so it never shows this.

The map legend's switch for the blip's icon type hides it like one of the game's own.

properties.name: class

It is what a World Builder map's `world` array carries. `WorldRayHit.levelObject` names the object a trace met in the form `apply` takes.

constructor.name: constructor
constructor.description: Wraps an edit the server already holds; use LevelEdit.apply to make one, or WorldResource for a whole export.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

functions.name: toString
functions.description: Formats this edit for logging and debugging.

returns.description: Its id, kind, object and what it does to it.

functions.description: Moves the object for every player, collision included.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Where the object stands instead.

parameters.description: Its orientation: a Quaternion, or Euler angles in degrees. Left out, it keeps the last move's.

functions.name: apply
functions.description: Takes an object the level placed out of the world, moves it, or swaps it for another mesh, for every player in the virtual world -- whenever they join, and however far away they are. Collision goes with it. An edit already made to the same object in that world is restated rather than doubled, so applying one twice changes nothing. Kept in memory only: apply it again on boot. A `WorldRayHit.levelObject` is a definition already: spread it and add what to do, as in `LevelEdit.apply({ ...hit.levelObject, model: stump })`.

functions.description: Looks an edit up by its network entity ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

returns.description: The edit, or null when no live edit has that ID.

functions.name: restoreAll
functions.description: Drops edits, giving every player the objects back as the level had them.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to clear; omitted clears every one of them.

returns.description: How many edits were dropped.

properties.name: id
properties.description: Immutable network entity identifier.

properties.name: exists
properties.description: False once the edit has been restored; every other read then returns its empty value.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: Whether the object is a brush, found by its mesh and where the level put it, or a level entity, found by its EntityGuid.

properties.name: name
properties.description: A brush's mesh path, or the name the level gives the entity.

properties.name: guid
properties.description: An entity's level EntityGuid as sixteen lowercase hex digits; empty for a brush.

properties.name: virtualWorld
properties.description: The virtual world whose players see the edit, fixed when it was applied.

properties.name: hidden
properties.description: Whether the object is taken out of the world: not drawn and not solid. Assignment takes it out or puts it back for every player, keeping any move.

properties.name: moved
properties.description: Whether the object stands somewhere other than where the level placed it; `move` and `clearMove` change it.

properties.name: model
properties.description: The mesh standing in the object's place, or empty. Assigning a prop catalog path or a mesh this server streams swaps the object for it on every player: the object goes, collision included, and the mesh stands where it stood -- or where `move` put it -- as solid static scenery. A felled tree leaves its stump this way. Assigning an empty string gives the object back. Throws for any other path.

functions.description: Reads server-owned stock and worn row counts. Inventory.get/add/remove/setProperties/set/transfer also accept Npc handles. Default native stock becomes ready at npcInventoryReady; Inventory.set may provide it before a body exists.

functions.name: remove
functions.description: Despawns this NPC everywhere, after emitting npcDestroy.

functions.name: hold
functions.description: Cancels whatever it was doing and leaves it standing where it is.

functions.name: moveTo
functions.description:
Moves to `position`, cancels any patrol, and emits `npcIntentDone` once when the move ends.

The game's own movement steers a body straight at the point it is given and finds no way around anything, so routes come from the server's navigation mesh. The server plans the route and hands the simulating client one corner at a time, the next before the body reaches the last, so it walks through bends without stopping; a dormant NPC is walked along the same route by the server. Routes only use doorways whose door stands open.

`auto` (the default) routes on the server whenever a mesh is loaded. Without one, a simulating client steers straight at `position` and a dormant NPC moves in a straight line. `game` steers straight at `position` and waits while dormant; if the body reports `blocked` and a mesh is loaded, the server tries a route before emitting `npcIntentDone`. `server` always routes on the server and throws without a loaded mesh, preserving the previous order.

A missing or partial route ends with `blocked`, and a blocked route is not retried. Route plans are queued and spread over ticks; the move reads `running` meanwhile.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Where to walk to.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `speed` defaults to `walk`; `radius` is the arrival distance in metres (default 1.5). `pathfinding` defaults to `auto`.

returns.description: True when the order went out; false for an invalid NPC or destination.

functions.name: patrol
functions.description:
Walks the waypoints in order. The server stores the route and replicates the current target. `npcIntentDone` fires once per leg, after its final mesh corner or a movement failure.

A leg that ends `blocked` or `failed` is skipped after at least 2 seconds. When every leg of a lap has failed in a row, the patrol is abandoned and that last leg reports `failed` instead.

parameters.name: points
parameters.description: Waypoints, a named route handle, or its stable id. Named routes are copied at start.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Point arrays retain their defaults: loop, walk, zero wait. Named routes use their authored defaults. Call options override route defaults; waypoint overrides take priority. Use mode for once, loop or pingPong; do not combine mode and loop. radius is the arrival distance. pathfinding uses the moveTo modes for every leg.

type.name: { speed?: 'walk' | 'jog' | 'run'; loop?: boolean; mode?: 'once' | 'loop' | 'pingPong'; radius?: number; waitSeconds?: number; pathfinding?: 'auto' | 'game' | 'server' }

returns.description: True when the route was accepted; false for an empty route, more than 256 waypoints, a waypoint that is not finite or lies outside the world, or a `waitSeconds` that is not a number. Throws if server mode has no loaded mesh, leaving the previous order intact.

functions.name: attack
functions.description: Orders native combat against a live player or NPC in the same visible world within 128 metres. Another order stops it. The order fails when its target dies, disappears or leaves that range. It waits while dormant; no offline damage is simulated. Bow attacks stop within 18 metres and use native projectiles. Equipped NPC arrows are replenished while shooting.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: The combatant to pursue and attack.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Defaults to melee. Bow requires an equipped bow and compatible arrows.

returns.description: True when accepted. Invalid targets leave the previous order unchanged.

functions.name: follow
functions.description: Keeps the NPC near somebody as they move, steering straight at them. `npcIntentDone` reports `reached` the first time it catches up, and the follow carries on. If the body reports `blocked`, a loaded mesh lets the server route to the target's current position before reporting it. After recovery it resumes following the moving target.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Who to follow, as a handle or a network ID.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `radius` is how close it tries to stay, in metres; `speed` is the pace.

returns.description: True when the order went out.

functions.name: flee
functions.description:
Sends the NPC away from a place, or from a player or NPC; `npcIntentDone` reports `reached` once the requested distance separates them.

An animal runs the game's own escape: its own mind picks the pace and the path, and runs as far as its kind runs, so `reached` comes only when that run takes it the requested distance clear. A mind that has not taken the escape within five seconds fails the order. That mind keeps the animal until another order replaces this one, so once clear it goes on as the game's animals do; a client that takes the animal over after `reached` holds it where it stands. A dormant animal waits for a client to run it.

Anyone else steers straight away from the place, or from where the player or NPC stood when ordered, until the requested distance separates them. If that body reports `blocked`, a loaded mesh lets the server try a route to a point past that distance, on the ground at the NPC's own height, before reporting it.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Who or what to run away from: a player or NPC, as a handle or a network ID, or a place.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `radius` is how far away is far enough; `speed` is the pace, `run` by default. An animal picks its own pace.

returns.description: True when the order went out; false for a player or NPC that is not there, or for the NPC itself.

functions.name: lookAt
functions.description: Turns the NPC's head, and its body when it has to, without moving it.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Who or what to look at.

returns.description: True when the order went out.

functions.name: teleport
functions.description: Moves the body outright, whoever is simulating it. Unlike a player teleport this is a write rather than a request: the server bumps the body's epoch, so a pose the simulator had already sent cannot put it back.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Where to put it.

parameters.name: rotation
parameters.description: Optional facing; a Quaternion, or Euler angles in degrees.

returns.description: True when the position was usable.

functions.name: playAnimation
functions.description:
Makes the NPC play one of the game's animations -- chopping wood with an axe in hand, drawing water, sitting, drinking -- on every client, the one simulating it included. It is state rather than a one-off: a client that streams the NPC in, and the next one to simulate it, play it too, until `stopAnimation` or the next `playAnimation`, which both cut it at once.

Give it something to do that keeps it in place, `hold` or `lookAt`: an order to walk makes the legs fight a full-body animation. A hit or a fall can cut the animation short; `loop` starts it again, and keeps a one-shot going pass after pass with no gap.

`npcAnimationEnd` fires once when the animation this request started is over, and says how.

parameters.name: fragment
parameters.description: A Mannequin fragment, as `Animations.list` names it -- or, as before, a row of the shipped emote catalog, which plays that gesture once and is not remembered.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `clip` plays a clip the server streams instead of a fragment (`animations/kcdc/<resource>/wave.caf`, the fragment left `""`), `tags` pick the variant, `loop` repeats it until stopped, `props` puts up to two models in its hands. `lockMovement` does nothing here: an NPC standing still is its intent's business.

type.name: { clip?: string; tags?: string; loop?: boolean; lockMovement?: boolean; props?: { item?: string; model?: string; hand?: 'right' | 'left'; joint?: string; position?: Vector3 | Partial<Vector3>; rotation?: Quaternion | Vector3 | Partial<Vector3> } | { item?: string; model?: string; hand?: 'right' | 'left'; joint?: string; position?: Vector3 | Partial<Vector3>; rotation?: Quaternion | Vector3 | Partial<Vector3> }[] }

returns.description: True when the request went out; false for a dead NPC. Throws for a prop or option it cannot use.

functions.name: stopAnimation
functions.description: Ends what `playAnimation` started at once, takes its props away and hands the body back to its intent. The stand-up `standUp` asks for is an animation of its own and raises its own `npcAnimationEnd`.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `standUp` plays the game's own way back to standing when the animation held the body in a sitting or lying stance tag: `StandUp` or `GetUp`, in the variant that fits. Without it the body goes straight back to standing.

returns.description: True when the request went out.

functions.name: setFacialExpression
functions.description:
Sets the NPC's facial expression on every client, alongside whatever its body plays. It is state: a client that streams the NPC in, and the next one to simulate it, show it too, until the next call.

The expression is the eyes, brows and mood; it never moves the mouth, which is `setTalking`. A mood tag is one of the body's own tags, so it can change the mood of its idle too.

parameters.name: fragment
parameters.description: A fragment on the face's own scope: `FE_Default`, `FE_DialogueIdle` or `FE_DialogueSpeaking` for a held mood, or an `ADLG_FA_*` gesture (`ADLG_FA_Smile`, `ADLG_FA_Wink`, `ADLG_FA_Laugh`, `ADLG_FA_Surprise`...) that plays once. `""` hands the face back to the game.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `tags` pick the variant: for the `FE_*` fragments the mood, `happy`, `angry`, `sad`, `nervous`, `pensive`, `arogant` or `drunk`, as `Animations.list("FE_")` spells them.

returns.description: True when the request went out; false for a dead NPC. Throws for an argument it cannot use.

functions.name: setTalking
functions.description: Moves the NPC's mouth as if it were talking, on every client, until told to stop. Pair it with `say` for a line of text. It is a looping talk animation, not lip-sync: it follows no words, and the game's own lip-sync wins while the NPC speaks a voice line of its own.

parameters.name: talking
parameters.description: Whether the mouth moves.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: How: `neutral` (the default), `happy`, `drunk` or `chew`.

returns.description: True when the request went out; false for a dead NPC. Throws for a style it does not know.

functions.name: say
functions.description: Puts a line of speech over the body on every client that can see it.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: What it says, up to 256 characters.

returns.description: True when the line went out.

functions.name: wear
functions.description: Dresses the body in exactly these items, replacing what it had on. Existing items are reused and missing ones are added to stock. An empty list undresses it and retains its clothes as loose inventory.

parameters.name: itemClasses
parameters.description: Item class GUIDs in the dashed form the game's own tables spell them.

returns.description: True when every GUID names an item class this build has. Otherwise nothing changes, and each refused GUID is logged.

functions.name: setOutfit
functions.description: Dresses the body in one of the game's own outfits.

parameters.name: preset
parameters.description: Clothing preset GUID from the game's own table.

returns.description: True when the preset is one this build has.

functions.name: setAppearance
functions.description: Changes the body under the clothes -- face, hair, beard and skin. Unlike a player's, this is a write rather than a request: nobody owns an NPC's body but the server.

parameters.name: appearance
parameters.description: The parts to change; anything left out keeps what it is wearing.

returns.description: True when the appearance was accepted.

functions.name: damage
functions.description: Takes health off the ledger, raising `npcDamage` and, if it is the last of it, `npcDeath`. Refused for an invulnerable or already-dead body.

parameters.name: amount
parameters.description: Health to take off.

parameters.name: attacker
parameters.description: Who did it, for the events this raises.

functions.name: kill
functions.description: Kills it outright, through the same path damage takes -- including an invulnerable one, which is the difference between this and `damage`.

parameters.name: attacker
parameters.description: Who to credit with it.

functions.name: revive
functions.description: Brings a dead NPC back at full health. Every client makes a fresh body for it, because the one they have is a corpse.

functions.name: pin
functions.description: Pins simulation of this NPC to one player's client, whatever the distances say. What a scripted scene wants: the actor has to be run by the machine the scene is being played to. A pinned NPC goes dormant rather than migrating when that player leaves range, and is unpinned automatically if they disconnect.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: Whose client should run it, or null to hand it back to the election.

functions.name: create
functions.description:
Spawns an NPC and replicates it. Omitted or undefined `locomotion` defaults to `native`; other values must be exactly `native` or `kinematic`, otherwise it throws before spawning. It exists on the server from this moment: every client near enough makes a body for it, one of them is elected to run it, and the rest draw what that one reports.

The body is not simulated until somebody is close enough to run it, which is not a failure -- a guard on the other side of the map has nothing to do that anybody can see. Read `simulator` to tell.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `soul` is a role from `Npc.roles()`, an animal name from `Npc.animals()`, or a soul GUID; `position` is where to put it. Everything else has a default.

type.name: { soul?: string; class?: string; name?: string; outfit?: string; wearing?: string[]; appearance?: Partial<Appearance>; position?: Vector3 | Partial<Vector3>; rotation?: Quaternion | Vector3 | Partial<Vector3>; faction?: number; health?: number; maxHealth?: number; locomotion?: 'kinematic' | 'native'; invulnerable?: boolean; frozen?: boolean; interactable?: boolean; nametag?: boolean; lootable?: boolean; virtualWorld?: number }

returns.description: The new NPC's handle.

functions.name: adopt
functions.description: Takes over one of the level's own NPCs instead of spawning a new body. Locomotion is validated as for `create`. A level `EntityGuid` is the same number on every machine, so every client finds the same body -- which is how doors, gates and stashes are already addressed. Adopting the same guid twice returns the NPC that already has it without applying the options again.

parameters.name: levelGuid
parameters.description: `EntityGuid` of the body the level already placed.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: The same options a spawn takes; `soul` and `class` are ignored, since the body already exists.

type.name: { soul?: string; class?: string; name?: string; outfit?: string; wearing?: string[]; appearance?: Partial<Appearance>; position?: Vector3 | Partial<Vector3>; rotation?: Quaternion | Vector3 | Partial<Vector3>; faction?: number; health?: number; maxHealth?: number; locomotion?: 'kinematic' | 'native'; invulnerable?: boolean; frozen?: boolean; interactable?: boolean; nametag?: boolean; lootable?: boolean; virtualWorld?: number }

returns.description: The NPC handle for that body.

functions.name: all
functions.description: Lists every server-owned NPC.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to list; omitted lists every one of them.

returns.description: One handle per live NPC, in no particular order.

functions.name: getById
functions.description: Looks an NPC up by its network entity ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

returns.description: The NPC's handle, or null when no live NPC has that ID.

functions.name: removeAll
functions.description: Despawns NPCs, emitting npcDestroy for each.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to clear; omitted clears every one of them.

returns.description: How many were despawned.

functions.name: roles
functions.description: The named kinds of NPC this build ships -- `guard`, `bandit`, `townswoman` and the rest. Each is a real soul out of the game's own tables, so a role spawns a body that already looks the part. Animal names are listed separately by `Npc.animals()`. Other values are taken as soul GUIDs.

returns.description: The role names.

functions.name: placements
functions.description: Authored human NPC placements in the configured level with matching catalog souls. These are initial placements, not current NPC schedules or proof that a quest layer is loaded. Does not spawn or adopt anything.

type.name: { name: string; guid: string; level: string; layer: string; soul: string; actorClass: string; position: { x: number; y: number; z: number }; rotation: { w: number; x: number; y: number; z: number } }[]

functions.name: animals
functions.description: Animal souls with matching native classes. Pass a name or soul to Npc.create. Chickens use flock entities and are excluded.

type.name: { name: string; soul: string; actorClass: string }[]

functions.name: animalSpawnpoints
functions.description: Level-authored animal spawners. Positions are markers and must be projected onto navigation. GUIDs are hex strings. Counts and respawn days describe the original game; scripts decide their population and respawn policy.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Defaults to the running server's level. Pass * for all levels.

type.name: { level: string; guid: string; name: string; layer: string; soul: string; actorClass: string; position: Vector3; count: number; respawnDays: number; spawnInFlock: boolean; spawnAreaGuid: string }[]

properties.name: soul
properties.description: GUID of the soul the body was spawned against, or empty for an adopted level body. Read-only: a soul decides what the body is, so a different one is a different NPC.

properties.name: actorClass
properties.description: Native entity class, including `NPC`, `NPC_Female`, or the matching animal class from `Npc.animals()`.

properties.name: levelGuid
properties.description: `EntityGuid` of the level body this NPC adopted, or 0 for a spawned one.

properties.name: name
properties.description: What every client shows over the body and in conversation. Empty leaves the name its soul was born with.

properties.name: faction
properties.description: Faction row used for relationship and crime decisions; 0 is no faction.

properties.name: health
properties.description: The server's ledger of this body's health, clamped to `maxHealth`. Combat damage arrives here after the server has agreed to it.

properties.name: maxHealth
properties.description: Health the body starts with and is revived to.

properties.name: alive
properties.description: False once health reached zero. A dead NPC is still an entity -- it is a corpse, and it can still be looted or revived.

properties.name: invulnerable
properties.description: Whether damage is refused before it reaches the ledger.

properties.name: frozen
properties.description: Whether the body holds its pose whatever its intent says.

properties.name: interactable
properties.description: Whether clients watch the use key against this body and raise `npcInteract`. On by default.

properties.name: nametag
properties.description: Whether its name is drawn over it the way a player's is.

properties.name: lootable
properties.description: Whether its corpse keeps its inventory for whoever searches it.

properties.name: locomotion
properties.description: How the client simulator moves the body. `native` (default) uses the game's movement controller and walk animations. `kinematic` moves the body directly without walk animation. Only these exact, case-sensitive strings are accepted; invalid values throw without changing the mode. Neither finds a way around anything: the game's movement controller steers straight at the point it is given. Routes come from server pathfinding, which hands either mode mesh corners -- see `moveTo`.

properties.name: intent
properties.description: What the NPC has been told to do: `hold`, `moveTo`, `follow`, `flee`, `lookAt`, `playAnim`, `talk` or `attack`.

properties.name: patrolState
properties.description: Current patrol snapshot and progress, or null when not patrolling. Updating a route does not change a running patrol.

properties.name: status
properties.description: What has become of the current order: `idle`, `running`, `reached`, `blocked` or `failed`. A move reads `running` from the moment it is given -- while its route is planned and while it walks the route's corners -- until it ends, and then the outcome `npcIntentDone` announced, which stays until the next order. A follow reads `reached` while it is within its radius. Dormant moves in `auto` or `server` mode are carried out and decided by the server; dormant `game` moves wait for a client simulator.

properties.name: appearance
properties.description: The body under the clothes, as the game's own component names. Write it with `setAppearance`.

properties.name: wearing
properties.description: Its worn item classes. Before default stock is established an empty list leaves the soul's own outfit; afterward empty means undressed. Write it with `wear`, `setOutfit` or `Inventory.set`.

properties.name: simulator
properties.description: The player whose client is currently running this NPC, or null while it is dormant. Dormant is not broken: nobody is near enough for it to matter, and the server keeps its route advancing until somebody is.

symbols.name: PatrolPoint
symbols.description: One authored stop, independent of actor type.

properties.name: position
properties.description: World-space waypoint.

properties.name: speed
properties.description: Overrides the route and call speed for this leg.

properties.name: waitSeconds
properties.description: Wait after arrival, 0 to 3600 seconds.

properties.name: radius
properties.description: Arrival radius in metres.

symbols.name: PatrolRouteDefinition
symbols.description: The format saved by World Builder and accepted by PatrolRoute.create.

properties.name: id
properties.description: Stable globally unique id, up to 128 bytes. Use a namespace such as town.guard-loop.

properties.name: name
properties.description: Display name, up to 256 bytes.

properties.name: points
properties.description: 1 to 256 ordered waypoints.

properties.name: mode
properties.description: Defaults to loop. Ping-pong visits each endpoint once per turn.

properties.name: speed
properties.description: Default leg speed; walk when omitted.

properties.name: waitSeconds
properties.description: Default arrival wait, 0 to 3600; defaults to zero.

properties.name: radius
properties.description: Default arrival radius; 1.5 metres when omitted.

symbols.name: PatrolState
symbols.description: A running patrol's snapshot. Indices and laps start at zero.

properties.name: routeId
properties.description: Stable route id; null for an anonymous point-array patrol.

properties.name: waypointIndex
properties.description: Target waypoint index.

properties.name: lap
properties.description: Completed loops or round trips.

properties.name: direction
properties.description: 1 forward, -1 backward.

properties.name: phase
properties.description: Whether the actor is approaching or waiting at the waypoint.

symbols.name: PatrolRoute
symbols.description: Named patrol definition. Actors snapshot it when ordered; update or destroy affects future starts.

functions.name: toJSON
functions.description: Returns an independent definition, or null after destruction.

functions.name: destroy
functions.description: Removes the definition. Active patrols keep their snapshots.

functions.name: update
functions.description: Updates defaults or waypoints atomically. Invalid input throws; a destroyed handle returns false.

parameters.name: changes
parameters.description: Fields to replace; id cannot change.

functions.name: create
functions.description: Registers a route. Invalid data or a duplicate id throws.

parameters.name: definition
parameters.description: The route to register.

functions.name: getById
functions.description: Looks up a registered route.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Exact route id.

functions.name: all
functions.description: Lists registered routes in creation order.

properties.name: exists
properties.description: False after destruction.

properties.name: id
properties.description: Stable id; empty after destruction.

properties.name: name
properties.description: Display name.

symbols.name: Quest
symbols.description: Replicated journal quest handle.

constructor.name: constructor
constructor.description: Creates a script wrapper for an existing quest with this ID; use Quest.give() to write one.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

functions.name: toString
functions.description: Formats this quest handle for logging and debugging.

returns.description: The quest ID, its key, its state and how many objectives it carries.

functions.name: remove
functions.description: Takes this quest out of every journal it was written into.

functions.name: setProgress
functions.description: Moves the quest on. There is no way back to unstarted: a quest nobody should see any more is removed.

parameters.name: progress
parameters.description: Where the quest now stands.

parameters.name: announce
parameters.description: Whether to raise the game's quest-updated toast; defaults to true. Pass false for a correction the player should not be told about.

functions.name: setObjective
functions.description: Rewrites one line of the quest in place.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Which objective to rewrite, counting from zero. An index past the end is ignored.

parameters.name: objective
parameters.description: The line, as text or as an object carrying its state.

type.name: string | { text: string; progress?: 'active' | 'done' | 'failed'; optional?: boolean; position?: Vector3 }

parameters.name: announce
parameters.description: Whether to raise the quest-updated toast; defaults to true.

functions.name: setObjectives
functions.description: Replaces the quest's objective list.

parameters.name: objectives
parameters.description: The whole list, at most eight entries; anything past that is dropped.

type.name: (string | { text: string; progress?: 'active' | 'done' | 'failed'; optional?: boolean; position?: Vector3 })[]

parameters.name: announce
parameters.description: Whether to raise the quest-updated toast; defaults to true.

functions.name: objectives
functions.description: Reads the quest's objectives back.

returns.description: One entry per objective, in journal order. `position` is present only on an objective that has one.

type.name: { text: string; progress: 'active' | 'done' | 'failed' | 'none'; optional: boolean; position?: Vector3 }[]

functions.name: track
functions.description: Makes the game follow this quest, exactly as the journal's track button does: it is listed in the HUD tracker, and every active objective that has a `position` is drawn as the game's own quest marker on the map and the compass. It is an instruction, not a lock -- the player can untrack it from the journal -- and the outcome arrives as `questTrackingChanged` like any other change. A quest given a moment ago can be tracked at once; the client waits for it to arrive.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: Network id of the player who should follow the quest. Omitted, everyone who has the quest follows it: its one owner, or every player in its world.

returns.description: How many clients were told. Zero when the player does not have this quest.

functions.name: untrack
functions.description: Makes the game stop following this quest, which takes its markers off the map and the compass. The outcome arrives as `questTrackingChanged`.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: Network id of the player who should stop following the quest. Omitted, everyone who has the quest stops.

returns.description: How many clients were told.

functions.name: give
functions.description: Writes a quest into the game's own journal. It is a replicated entity, so a player who joins late, reloads or walks away still finds it in their log -- which is what a quest needs and what a one-shot notification cannot do. What the player sees is the game's quest UI: its journal row, its diary page, its objective tracker and its quest-updated toast, all reading a quest node the client builds with the game's own constructor.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: What the quest is filed under: up to 64 letters, digits, underscores or dashes, unique within its virtual world.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: The line the journal row shows.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `description` is the diary page, `type` the journal section, `objectives` the lines under it -- each with an optional world `position` the game marks on the map and compass while the quest is followed -- `player` the network id of the one player it belongs to, `announce` whether to raise the toast, and `track` whether its recipients start following it.

type.name: { description?: string; type?: 'main' | 'side' | 'activity' | 'event' | 'micro' | 'racing'; objectives?: (string | { text: string; progress?: 'active' | 'done' | 'failed'; optional?: boolean; position?: Vector3 })[]; player?: number; announce?: boolean; track?: boolean }

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world the quest belongs to; omitted puts it in the global one.

returns.description: The newly written quest handle.

functions.name: all
functions.description: Lists every replicated quest the server currently has.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to list; omitted lists every one of them.

returns.description: One handle per live quest, in no particular order.

functions.name: find
functions.description: Looks a quest up by its key.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key the quest was given under.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to search; omitted searches every one of them.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: Network id of the player whose copy to find. Keys are unique per recipient, so this is how one player's errand is told from another's.

returns.description: The quest's handle, or null when no live quest has that key.

functions.name: getById
functions.description: Looks a replicated quest up by its network entity ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

returns.description: The quest's handle, or null when no live quest has that ID.

functions.name: removeAll
functions.description: Takes quests out of every journal they were written into.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to clear; omitted clears every one of them.

returns.description: How many quests were removed.

properties.name: key
properties.description: The key the quest is filed under, and the name the game knows the quest node by. Read-only: it is the quest's identity.

properties.name: title
properties.description: The line the journal row and the quest toast show. Assignment is silent; it does not raise a toast.

properties.name: description
properties.description: The body of the journal's diary page for this quest. Assignment is silent.

properties.name: type
properties.description: Which section of the journal the quest files under. Read-only: it is decided when the quest is given.

symbols.name: GroundItem
symbols.description: Replicated world stack handle.

constructor.name: constructor
constructor.description: Creates a script wrapper for an existing ground item with this ID; use GroundItem.spawn() to spawn one.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

functions.name: toString
functions.description: Formats this ground item handle for logging and debugging.

returns.description: The stack ID, its item class, how many of it there are and whether it has settled.

functions.name: destroy
functions.description: Takes this stack back out of the world on every client after emitting groundItemDestroy.

functions.name: spawn
functions.description: Lays a pickable stack of an item on the ground and replicates it, spawning it already at rest.

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: Item class to lay down, as either its GUID or its name (`arrow_crude`). The same spelling `player.giveItem` takes.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Optional world-space spawn position; omitted components default to zero. The stack is placed there rather than dropped, so put it where the ground is.

parameters.name: rotation
parameters.description: Optional resting orientation: a Quaternion, or a Vector3 of Euler angles in degrees.

parameters.name: amount
parameters.description: Optional number of units in the stack, from 1 to 10000; omitted lays down one. A stack is picked up whole.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world the stack belongs to; omitted puts it in the global one.

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: Optional condition of the item itself: `quality` as the game grades it, `health` and `condition` from 0 to 1. Each defaults to the class's own. Arrows and other missile classes are held to tighter bounds by the receiving client and are given a quality of 1 and full health when these are left out, since a stack outside those bounds is one no client would build. `carryable` makes it a prop people carry in their arms rather than stock: the game's pick-up prompt over it starts a carry (raising `playerCarryingItem`) and never puts it in an inventory. Only for a single item `player.carryItem` takes by name. `name`, up to 64 bytes of UTF-8, is what `groundItem.name` reads back, so a script finds the stack again.

type.name: { quality?: number; health?: number; condition?: number; carryable?: boolean; name?: string }

returns.description: The newly spawned ground item handle. Throws when the item is not a class in the game's tables, or when no client could build the stack as described.

functions.name: all
functions.description: Lists every stack lying in the world, however it got there.

returns.description: One handle per live stack, in no particular order.

functions.name: getById
functions.description: Looks a stack up by its network entity ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

functions.description: Removes stacks from the world, emitting groundItemDestroy for each one.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to clear; omitted clears every one of them.

returns.description: How many stacks were removed.

properties.name: itemClass
properties.description: The class of item lying here, as the same 32 hex digits `player.rightHandItem` and `player.equipment` use, so the three can be compared directly. The server holds no name for a class: naming one is an item database's job.

properties.name: amount
properties.description: How many units are in the stack. One entity however many that is: a stack is picked up whole or not at all.

properties.name: quality
properties.description: Quality the stack was made with, or 0 when it was left to the class's own.

properties.name: health
properties.description: Absolute item health from 0 to 1, or -1 when it was left to the class's own.

properties.name: condition
properties.description: Displayed condition from 0 to 1, or -1 when it was left to the class's own.

properties.name: resting
properties.description: Whether the stack has settled where it will stay. A stack a script spawned is resting from the start; one a player dropped is false while the nearest client simulates its fall, and its position moves until then. A resting stack's pose is the server's and does not move again.

properties.name: carryable
properties.description: Whether this is a prop people carry in their arms -- one a carry put down, or one spawned `carryable` -- rather than stock. Taking it up is a carry: the game's pick-up prompt or `player.carryItem(groundItem)`, never an inventory.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The name `GroundItem.spawn` or a World Builder export gave the stack, so a script finds it again; empty for none.

properties.name: droppedById
properties.description: Network ID of the player who dropped this stack, or 0 when the server spawned it.

properties.name: droppedBy
properties.description: The player who dropped this stack, or null when the server spawned it or that player has since left.

functions.name: getHerbs

parameters.name: radius

parameters.name: virtualWorld

functions.name: removeHerbs

parameters.name: position

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: Inclusive 3D radius in metres, from 0 to 100000.

parameters.name: virtualWorld

functions.name: setRespawnTime

Equal bounds fix the duration; (0, 0) disables timed regrowth while manual respawn remains available. Applies to every virtual world.

parameters.name: minHours

functions.name: resetRespawnTime

returns.description: Number of active picked or script-removed sources restored. Invalid arguments throw.

functions.name: respawnAll

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Only this virtual world; defaults to 0.

returns.description: Number of active picked or script-removed sources restored. Invalid arguments throw.
