symbols.name: Door
symbols.description: Replicated handle for a door: one of the level's own, or one a script or a world resource hung with `Door.spawn`.

constructor.name: constructor
constructor.description: Creates a script wrapper for a door the server already knows; use `Door.spawn` to hang a new one, or `Door.find` for one the level places.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

functions.name: toString
functions.description: Formats this door handle for logging and debugging.

returns.description: The door ID, its level GUID and whether it is open and locked.

functions.name: setOpen
functions.description: Opens or closes the door with nobody pushing it. Every client that has the door built plays the game's own swing; one arriving later finds it posed the same way. Opening a locked door unlocks it, as the game's own `Open` does.

parameters.name: open
parameters.description: True to open the door, false to close it.

parameters.name: fromFront
parameters.description: Which side the leaf is worked from, and so which way it swings. Omitted keeps the side it was last worked from.

returns.description: False when the door is already that way.

functions.name: destroy
functions.description: Takes the door out. A door a script or a world resource hung is taken down for good. A door the level places is taken out of this handle's virtual world, collision and all, through a level edit that every client seeing that world applies -- a player in the global world sees every world, so it is hidden for them too; the copy in the global world takes it out of every world. `Door.restore` puts a level door back, and `Door.removed` lists the ones that are out. Kept in memory only, like every level edit: a removal is undone when the server restarts or the resource that made it stops.

functions.name: toJSON
functions.description: The definition `Door.spawn` takes to hang this door again, with whether it is locked now: what a script saves. The server keeps nothing past a restart. It is one entry of a World Builder map's `doors` array.

returns.description: Null for a door the level places.

functions.name: all
functions.description: Lists every door: the level's own, all of which exist from boot in the global world, and every door a script or a world resource hung. In another virtual world a level door is built the first time anything there reaches it, so this lists only those. A level door taken out of a world is not listed for it; `Door.removed` lists those.

returns.description: One handle per known door, in no particular order.

functions.name: spawn
functions.description: Hangs a working door where the level has none: every player in the virtual world sees it, opens and closes it, keys or picks its lock, and the server judges every use by the same rules as the level's own doors. It starts closed. Kept in memory only: hang it again on boot. The resource that hangs it owns it, so it goes when that resource stops. NPCs do not path through it: the level's navigation mesh has no link for it.

parameters.name: definition
parameters.description: The leaf, where it hangs and how it locks, in the format of one entry of a World Builder map's `doors` array.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world whose players see it; the global one when omitted.

returns.description: The door. Throws for an unknown model, a transform that is not finite, a lock name that is not one of the four, or a key that is not an item class.

functions.name: models
functions.description: Lists every leaf mesh the shipped levels hang doors from, which is every model `Door.spawn` takes.

returns.description: One row per mesh, sorted by path.

functions.name: remove
functions.description: Takes a door the level places out of a virtual world, collision and all, as `door.destroy()` does, without needing its handle. Taking out a door that is already out of that world, or of the global one, does nothing; taking out one that has a level edit in that world, a move or a swap, replaces that edit.

parameters.name: guid
parameters.description: The level door's EntityGuid as hex, as `door.guid` prints it.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to take it out of; the global one, and so every world, when omitted.

returns.description: Throws for a GUID that is not one of the level's doors.

functions.name: restore
functions.description: Puts back a level door that a script, a world resource or any other level edit took out of a virtual world. It comes back closed, and locked as the level builds it.

parameters.name: guid
parameters.description: The level door's EntityGuid as hex, as `Door.removed` lists it.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to put it back in; the global one when omitted. A door taken out of the global world is only put back from there.

returns.description: The door, or null when that world had no such removal.

functions.name: removed
functions.description: Lists the doors the level places that are taken out of a virtual world, by a script or a World Builder export alike.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to list; omitted lists every one of them.

returns.description: One row per removal, in no particular order.

functions.name: getById
functions.description: Looks a door up by its network entity ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

returns.description: The door's handle, or null when no live door has that ID.

functions.name: find
functions.description: Looks a door up by the level's own identity for it, which survives a restart and is the same on every machine. A door the level places is found in any virtual world it has not been taken out of. A door a script hung is found by `door.guid` in the world it hangs in.

parameters.name: guid
parameters.description: The door's level EntityGuid as hex, with or without an `0x` prefix, as `door.guid` prints it.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to look in; omitted looks in the global one, where every body starts.

returns.description: The door's handle, or null when there is no such door there.

functions.name: getForArea
functions.description: Lists the doors the level links to an area as its `crime_door`s, with their GUID, name, position and link type, straight from the level catalog -- so a door that no client has reported yet is listed too. Pass a `guid` to `Door.find` for the live handle and its `locked` state. Only native links: a script area has none.

parameters.name: areaId
parameters.description: The area's id, as `area.id` prints it.

returns.description: The doors; empty for an unknown area or one with no links.

functions.name: queryNearest
functions.description:
Asks a player's client which door their body is standing at. The server knows every door the level places but has no world to measure distances in, so this is how a command finds the door in front of a player, and the answer is what that client sees now rather than what the replica last carried.

The promise always settles: on the answer, on a five-second timeout, or when the player leaves, with `found` false and `reason` saying which.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: The player to ask. The question goes to their own client.

returns.description: The answer, once that client has given one.

properties.name: guid
properties.description: The door's EntityGuid, as sixteen lowercase hex digits, the same on every machine; `Door.find` takes it back. A level door's never changes, so it is the identity to store one under. A hung door's lasts only until the server stops: store its `toJSON()` instead.

properties.name: stateToken
properties.description: Bumped on every durable change. Clients act on the edges rather than the value, so it only tells one change from the next.

properties.name: open
properties.description: Whether the door is standing open. Change it with `setOpen`, which also says which way it swings.

properties.name: openedFromFront
properties.description: Which side the leaf was last worked from, which decides the way it swings. A player arriving later poses the door from this, so everyone sees it swung the same way.

properties.name: locked
properties.description: Whether the door is locked. Assignment reaches every client that has the door streamed in, including one already standing at it. A door locked from here can only be opened again from here or with a lockpick: a player unlocking it by hand or with a key is refused.

properties.name: lockedByServer
properties.description: Whether the lock was set by a script or an operator rather than by the level. It clears when the door is unlocked, by any route the server accepted.

properties.name: usable
properties.description: Whether players may work the door. False hides its prompt to open, close, unlock or pick it, and a player's use is refused on their own machine before the door or the body moves -- no round trip, no swing back. A report against it is refused here too, for a client that did not. Assignment reaches every client that has the door streamed in, including one already standing at it. The door stays as it is: `setOpen` and `locked` still work, and NPCs still pass it. Per door, not per player: refuse one player with a client `doorInteract` handler.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The entity name the level gives the door; for a hung door, the `name` it was hung with, or `spawned_door_<n>` without one.

properties.name: keyItem
properties.description: The item class GUID of the key the level assigns to the door's keyhole, as `player.giveItem` takes it. Empty when it takes none of its own -- most doors open to the generated home or shop key instead. The server does not see inventories, so this is for a resource that keeps its own.

properties.name: lockpickable
properties.description: Whether the level lets this door be lockpicked. A lockpick reported on one that cannot be is refused.

properties.name: areas
properties.description: The level areas that link this door as one of their `crime_door`s -- the house, workshop or storage room it belongs to, as the level itself records it. Nothing is inferred from where the door stands.

properties.name: startsLocked
properties.description: Whether the level builds this door locked, which is the state it has at boot; for a hung door, whether it was hung locked.

properties.name: spawned

symbols.name: SmartObject
symbols.description: A bench, a bed, a dice table, an alchemy table, a smithy, a drying rack or a smokehouse a script or a World Builder export placed. Every player in its virtual world can sit on it, sleep in it or work at it as they would at the level's own. It never moves: assigning `position` or `rotation`, or calling `setVirtualWorld`, is put back on the next tick.

constructor.name: constructor
constructor.description: Wraps a smart object the server already holds; use SmartObject.spawn to place one.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

functions.name: toString
functions.description: Formats this handle for logging and debugging.

returns.description: Its id, blueprint and kind.

functions.name: destroy
functions.description: Takes the smart object down for every player. A player sitting on it or working at it is let go.

functions.name: toJSON
functions.description: The definition `SmartObject.spawn` takes to place it again: what a script saves. The server keeps nothing past a restart. It is one entry of a World Builder map's `smartObjects` array.

returns.description: Null once it is gone.

functions.name: spawn
functions.description: Places one of the game's interactive prefabs -- its furniture, solid, and the entities its interaction runs on -- for every player in the virtual world, built on each client under the same GUIDs, so sitting on it and working at it replicate as they do at the level's own. A placed dice table, crafting station, drying rack or smokehouse joins `Dice.tables()`, `Crafting.stations()` and the server's checks like the level's own. Kept in memory only: place it again on boot. The resource that places it owns it, so it goes when that resource stops. NPCs do not use it. A `bare` definition places the entities without the furniture, where a prop of your own stands.

parameters.name: definition
parameters.description: What to place and where, in the format of one entry of a World Builder map's `smartObjects` array.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world whose players see it; the global one when omitted.

returns.description: The smart object. Throws for an unknown blueprint, a transform that is not finite, or `bare` on a blueprint that cannot stand bare.

functions.name: all
functions.description: Lists the smart objects scripts and World Builder exports placed.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to list; omitted lists every one.

returns.description: One handle per placed object, in no particular order.

functions.name: getById
functions.description: Looks a placed smart object up by its network entity ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

returns.description: The handle, or null.

functions.name: blueprints
functions.description: Lists everything `SmartObject.spawn` can place.

returns.description: One row per blueprint, sorted by name.

functions.name: stations
functions.description: Lists every station players in a virtual world can use: the level's dice tables, crafting stations, drying racks and smokehouses, minus any a level edit took out of that world, and every placed one there or in the global world.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to list for; the global one when omitted.

returns.description: One row per station, in no particular order.

functions.name: remove
functions.description: Takes one of the level's stations out of a virtual world through a level edit on its entity: listed nowhere, refused for any new session by the server (one already running at it finishes), and hidden on every client seeing that world -- a player in the global world sees every world. The furniture around it is the level's own scenery and stays; take it out with `LevelEdit.apply` or the World Builder. A placed smart object goes with `destroy()` instead. Kept in memory only, like every level edit.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The level station's GUID, as `SmartObject.stations()` lists it.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to take it out of; the global one, and so every world, when omitted.

returns.description: Throws for an id that is not one of the level's stations.

functions.name: restore

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The level station's GUID, as `SmartObject.removed()` lists it.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to put it back in; the global one when omitted.

returns.description: False when that world had no such removal.

functions.name: removed
functions.description: Lists the level's stations a level edit has taken out, by a script or a World Builder export alike.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to list; omitted lists every one.

returns.description: One row per removal, in no particular order.

properties.name: blueprint
properties.description: The blueprint it was placed from, as `SmartObject.blueprints()` lists it.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: What it is for.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The name it was placed with; empty for none.

properties.name: bare
properties.description: Whether it was placed without its blueprint's furniture: only the place a body takes, or the station, and the prompts that offer it.

properties.name: stationId
properties.description: The GUID of its station part as sixteen lowercase hex digits: the `id` `Dice.tables()` and `SmartObject.stations()` give it. `Crafting.stations()` lists an alchemy table or a smithy as `<level>:<stationId>`. Empty for a seat or a bed. It lasts only until the server stops.

properties.name: seats
properties.description: The GUIDs of the places a body sits or lies on, as a seated player's stance and `DiceTableInfo.seats` name them.

properties.name: accepted
properties.description: Whether a cycle started.

properties.name: reason
properties.description: Why nothing moved, as a phrase that reads after the gate's name: `is already open`, `is already closing`. Empty when a cycle started.

properties.name: opening
properties.description: The direction taken, or the one that was refused.

properties.name: seconds
properties.description: How long the motion still has to run. 0 when nothing moved.

symbols.name: Gate
symbols.description: Replicated handle for one of the level's castle gates.

constructor.name: constructor
constructor.description: Creates a script wrapper for a gate the server already knows; gates are the level's own and are never spawned.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

functions.name: toString
functions.description: Formats this gate handle for logging and debugging.

returns.description: The gate ID, its level GUID, what kind it is and where it is in its cycle.

functions.name: toggle
functions.description: Starts a cycle. The motion is never streamed: every client plays it out from the server clock it started on, and a gate reversed mid-cycle picks up where it is rather than snapping to the far end.

parameters.name: open
parameters.description: true opens, false closes. Omitted heads away from whichever end the gate is at, reversing one already moving.

returns.description: What happened, and the phrase to explain it with when nothing did.

functions.name: all
functions.description: Lists every gate the level places, all of which exist from boot in the global world. In another virtual world a gate is built the first time anything there reaches it, so this lists only those.

returns.description: One handle per gate, in no particular order.

functions.name: getById
functions.description: Looks a gate up by its network entity ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

returns.description: The gate's handle, or null when no live gate has that ID.

functions.name: find
functions.description: Looks a gate up by the level's own identity for it, which survives a restart and is the same on every machine. A gate the level places is always found, in any virtual world.

parameters.name: guid
parameters.description: The gate's level EntityGuid as hex, with or without an `0x` prefix, as `gate.guid` prints it.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to look in; omitted looks in the global one, where every body starts.

returns.description: The gate's handle, or null when the level places no such gate.

functions.name: nearest
functions.description: Finds the gate nearest a point. Gate positions come from the level's own data, so unlike a door this needs no round trip to anybody's client.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: World-space point to measure from.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: How far to look, in metres. Castle architecture is visible from a long way off, so this is tens of metres rather than a couple.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to look in; omitted looks in the global one.

returns.description: The nearest gate within the radius, or null when there is none.

properties.name: guid
properties.description: The level's own EntityGuid, as sixteen lowercase hex digits. The same on every machine, so it is the identity to store a gate under; `Gate.find` takes it back. A `gate` has no entity of its own, so its key is the GUID of the layer that draws it shut.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: What piece of architecture this is: `drawbridge` or `portcullis`, which animate, or `gate`, a pair of leaves the level swaps between drawn open and drawn shut -- the Ratborsch and Nebakov fortress gates and the Ruthard palace gate. A `gate` opens and closes at once.

properties.name: cycle
properties.description: Where the gate is in its cycle: `closed`, `opening`, `open` or `closing`. Open always means passable -- a portcullis raised, a drawbridge lowered. Named `cycle` because every entity already has a `state`, which is its state bag.

properties.name: openness
properties.description: How far open the gate is, from 0 shut to 1 fully open, read off the pose curve mined from the asset's own animation at the point the server clock says the motion has reached. It follows the bars, not the clock: a portcullis reads 0 within the first fifth of its close, and holds there while the clip finishes.

properties.name: moving
properties.description: Whether a cycle is running. `toggle` reverses a moving gate from where it has got to rather than refusing it.

properties.name: openDuration
properties.description: How long opening takes, in seconds, from the key range the asset's animation database stores. A gate with no opening clip runs its closing one backwards, so this is that clip's length. 0 for a `gate`.

properties.name: closeDuration
properties.description: How long closing takes, in seconds, from the asset's animation database.

properties.name: accepted
properties.description: Whether the engine did it.

properties.name: reason
properties.description: Why it did not, as a phrase that reads after the engine's name: `is not loaded`, `cannot fire: the target is further than the engine can throw`. Empty when it did.

properties.name: seconds
properties.description: How long until the step it started is over: the whole load for `load`, until the projectile is let go for `fire`. 0 when nothing happened.

symbols.name: SiegeEngine
symbols.description: Replicated handle for a trebuchet or a cannon.

constructor.name: constructor
constructor.description: Creates a script wrapper for an existing siege engine with this ID; use SiegeEngine.spawn() to build one.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

functions.name: toString
functions.description: Formats this engine handle for logging and debugging.

returns.description: The engine ID, its kind and where it is in its cycle.

functions.name: load
functions.description: Starts the reload cycle of an idle engine. `siegeEngineReady` fires when it can shoot.

returns.description: What happened, and the phrase to explain it with when nothing did.

functions.name: fire
functions.description: Turns a loaded engine to face the target and shoots at it. A trebuchet's arm lets the stone go at one angle, so its speed is solved for the distance; a cannon fires at one speed, so its elevation is. The stone is let go partway through the shot (`seconds`), then every client nearby draws it along the same arc. It comes down where the world stops it, which the attacker is asked to report when near enough, else the player nearest the target, or on the target when nobody can.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Where the projectile should come down.

parameters.name: attacker
parameters.description: The player credited with whatever it hits, in `playerDamage`, `npcDamage` and `siegeImpact`.

returns.description: What happened, and the phrase to explain it with when nothing did.

functions.name: aim
functions.description: Turns the engine to face a point without shooting. `fire` turns it anyway; this is for showing where it will shoot.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: The point to turn towards.

returns.description: What happened, and the phrase to explain it with when nothing did.

functions.name: canHit
functions.description: Whether the engine can reach a point from where it stands.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: The point to test.

returns.description: Empty when it can; otherwise why not, as a phrase.

functions.name: setAimGuide
functions.description: Shows or hides the operator's aim guide: a translucent red beam along the shot's path -- out of a trebuchet's sling and along its arc, or straight from a cannon's muzzle -- to where it would come down, with a ball there. Off by default, which leaves laying the engine to the eye; the Fire hint says how far the shot goes either way.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Whether the operator sees the beam.

functions.name: getAimGuide
functions.description: Whether the operator sees the aim guide; see `setAimGuide`.

returns.description: True when the beam is shown.

functions.name: repair
functions.description: Makes the engine whole again: `health` back to `maxHealth`, and a wreck idle and unloaded.

functions.name: setOperator
functions.description: Puts a player in the engine's place without asking them, or takes whoever is there out of it. A player holds one place at a time, so they leave any other engine or winch first. Raises no `siegeEngineUse`.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: Who takes the engine's place, or null to empty it.

returns.description: False for a player who is no longer connected.

functions.name: destroy
functions.description: Removes the engine on every client after emitting `siegeEngineDestroy`. A projectile already in the air still lands.

functions.name: spawn
functions.description: Builds and replicates a siege engine, unloaded. The trebuchet is the game's own model and plays its own winch, load and fire animations; the cannon is the game's static gun.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: `trebuchet` or `cannon`.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: World-space position of the engine's base.

parameters.name: rotation
parameters.description: Optional initial orientation: a Quaternion, or a Vector3 of Euler angles in degrees. `fire` and `aim` turn it to face their target.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world the engine belongs to; omitted puts it in the global one.

returns.description: The new engine's handle.

functions.name: all
functions.description: Lists the siege engines the server has.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to list; omitted lists every one.

returns.description: One handle per engine, in no particular order.

functions.name: getById
functions.description: Looks an engine up by its network entity ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

returns.description: The engine's handle, or null when no live engine has that ID.

functions.name: destroyAll
functions.description: Removes siege engines, emitting `siegeEngineDestroy` for each one.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to clear; omitted clears every one.

returns.description: How many were removed.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: What the engine is: `trebuchet` or `cannon`. The game ships no catapult and no ballista.

properties.name: cycle
properties.description: Where the engine is in its cycle: `idle` (unloaded), `drawing` (a trebuchet's arm being winched down), `loading` (the crew laying the projectile), `ready` or `firing`. Named `cycle` because every entity already has a `state`, which is its state bag.

properties.name: loaded
properties.description: Whether the engine is ready to fire.

properties.name: speed
properties.description: How fast the cycle runs, from 0.1 to 20; 1 is the game's own pace, which takes a trebuchet's crew nearly two minutes to load and lets the stone go 3.5 seconds into the shot. Changing it mid-step carries on from where the engine has got to.

properties.name: damage
properties.description: Health taken from anything at the point of impact; a player has 100. A quarter of it reaches the edge of `damageRadius`. 0 leaves hits to `siegeImpact`.

properties.name: damageRadius
properties.description: How far from the point of impact anything is hurt, in metres, up to 100.

properties.name: usable
properties.description: Whether players may work the engine. A player within 2 m of an empty one gets the game's own action hint on the use key to take its place, and becomes its `operator`; near a trebuchet with a `crewRequired`, a free winch is offered too. Each ask raises `siegeEngineUse` first, which may refuse it. Off by default.

properties.name: range
properties.description: How far a shot goes along the operator's facing when they fire before laying the engine anywhere, in metres; kept between `minRange` and `maxRange`. 150 for a trebuchet and 120 for a cannon to start with.

properties.name: minRange
properties.description: The closest the engine can be aimed, in metres along the ground.

properties.name: maxRange
properties.description: The furthest the engine can be aimed, in metres along the ground.

properties.name: loadDuration
properties.description: How long `load` takes at the engine's speed, in seconds.

properties.name: maxHealth
properties.description: What the engine can take before it is wrecked; 0, the default, means nothing harms it. Setting it heals the engine to the new maximum and repairs a wreck. A blast within `damageRadius` of an engine -- any engine's, its own included -- takes its share of that shot's `damage` off it, raising `siegeEngineDamage`.

properties.name: health
properties.description: What is left of `maxHealth`. Setting it to 0 wrecks the engine and raising it from 0 repairs one; ignored while `maxHealth` is 0.

properties.name: wrecked
properties.description: Whether the engine's health ran out. A wrecked cannon shows the game's broken gun and a wrecked trebuchet leans and settles; nothing loads, aims or fires it, and its operator and crew are let go, until `repair` or a new `maxHealth`.

properties.name: ammo
properties.description: Shots left to load; each `load` takes one, and an engine with none refuses to load. -1, the default, never runs out; any negative value means the same.

properties.name: crewRequired
properties.description: How many of the engine's winches must be manned for its arm to be winched down; 0, the default, winds it by itself. With fewer hands than this the winding holds where it is, and goes on when they come back. Players near a usable engine that needs them are offered its winches, and each one there plays the game's own pull. Kept to `crewPlaces`.

properties.name: crewPlaces
properties.description: How many winches the engine has: 2 on a trebuchet, 0 on a cannon.

properties.name: operator
properties.description: The player in the engine's place, or null. They lay it where they look while they hold the block key, load it with the torch key, fire it with the attack key and step away with the use key; walking off lets go of it too. `setOperator` puts somebody there.

properties.name: crew
properties.description: Who mans each winch, in place order, with null for an empty one.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: Its name: `siege`, `tall`, `short` or `low`.

properties.name: model
properties.description: The mesh it stands as, a path from the shared prop catalog.

properties.name: height
properties.description: How far up its rungs go, in metres.

properties.name: lean
properties.description: How far it leans towards the wall standing, in degrees about its own X; it leans towards its forward.

symbols.name: SiegeLadder
symbols.description: Replicated handle for a siege ladder leaning on a wall.

constructor.name: constructor
constructor.description: Creates a script wrapper for an existing siege ladder with this ID; use SiegeLadder.spawn() to place one.

functions.name: destroy
functions.description: Removes the ladder on every client after emitting `siegeLadderDestroy`.

functions.name: spawn
functions.description: Places one of the game's own ladders leaning on a wall, the way the Suchdol and Nebakov sieges stand theirs: the game's climb, and the game's step off over the palisade at its top, which wants the top a little over the walk.

functions.description: What one kind of ladder is: its mesh, its climb and its lean -- what a placement preview needs to show it as it will stand.

parameters.name: kind

returns.description: The kind, or null for a name that is not one.

functions.description: Lists the siege ladders the server has.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to list; omitted lists every one.

returns.description: One handle per ladder, in no particular order.

functions.name: getById
functions.description: Looks a ladder up by its network entity ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

returns.description: The ladder's handle, or null when no live ladder has that ID.

functions.name: destroyAll
functions.description: Removes siege ladders, emitting `siegeLadderDestroy` for each one.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to clear; omitted clears every one.

returns.description: How many were removed.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: Which of the game's ladders it is: `siege` (the Suchdol siege ladder, 9.75 m), `tall` (5.5 m), `short` (3.25 m) or `low` (2 m).

properties.name: pose
properties.description: `standing` against its wall, `pushed` (a defender's swing, then its fall), `down`, `raising` or `broken`. Named `pose` because every entity already has a `state`, which is its state bag.

properties.name: height
properties.description: How far up its rungs go, in metres: its top rests this high above its foot on the wall's top. Pick the kind whose height meets the walk.

properties.name: climbable
properties.description: Whether the game's own climb is offered on it: while it stands and nobody has started to push it.

properties.name: usable
properties.description: Whether players are offered the push at its top and the raise at the foot of a fallen one, each raising `siegeLadderUse` first. On by default. The climb is the game's and is offered whenever the ladder stands.

properties.name: pusher
properties.description: Who last pushed it, or null.

symbols.name: StonePile
symbols.description: Replicated handle for a pile of hurling stones on a battlement.
