functions.name: destroy
functions.description: Removes the pile on every client after emitting `stonePileDestroy`. A stone already thrown still lands.

functions.name: spawn
functions.description: Places the game's own battlement pile of hurling stones, the Nebakov and Suchdol defenders' heap. Its prompt, the lift and the heave over the wall are the game's stone throwing; each stone is a real rigid body that falls where it falls.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Where the thrower stands on the walk, behind the parapet.

parameters.name: rotation
parameters.description: Its facing: forward is the way the stones go, over the wall. A Quaternion, or a Vector3 of Euler angles in degrees.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world the pile belongs to; omitted puts it in the global one.

returns.description: The new pile's handle.

functions.name: all
functions.description: Lists the stone piles the server has.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to list; omitted lists every one.

returns.description: One handle per pile, in no particular order.

functions.name: getById
functions.description: Looks a pile up by its network entity ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

returns.description: The pile's handle, or null when no live pile has that ID.

functions.name: destroyAll
functions.description: Removes stone piles, emitting `stonePileDestroy` for each one.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to clear; omitted clears every one.

returns.description: How many were removed.

properties.name: stones
properties.description: Stones left to throw; each throw takes one, and a pile with none offers nothing. Players see at most nine in the heap. -1, the default, never runs out; any negative value means the same.

properties.name: usable
properties.description: Whether players are offered the game's own prompt at the pile. On by default.

properties.name: damage
properties.description: Health taken from anyone at the point a stone comes down, up to 1000; a quarter of it reaches the edge of `damageRadius`. 60 to start with; a player has 100.

properties.name: damageRadius
properties.description: How far from where a stone comes down anyone is hurt, in metres, up to 10. 1.5 to start with.

properties.name: id
properties.description: The area's identity, unique among script areas. It may not be sixteen hex digits, which is how a level area's GUID reads.

properties.name: name
properties.description: A readable name; the id when omitted.

properties.name: type
properties.description: CryEngine's own area shapes: `AreaBox`, `AreaShape` (a closed polygon with a height) and `AreaSphere`.

properties.name: position
properties.description: Where the shape is placed from; the origin when omitted.

properties.name: rotation
properties.description: The shape's orientation: a Quaternion or {x, y, z, w}, or Euler angles in degrees.

properties.name: min
properties.description: box: the corner nearest negative infinity, relative to `position` before rotation.

properties.name: max
properties.description: box: the opposite corner. Every component must be above `min`'s.

properties.name: points
properties.description: shape: 3 to 256 corners relative to `position` before rotation, closed back to the first. As in the engine, the floor is the lowest corner.

properties.name: height
properties.description: shape: how far above its lowest corner the area reaches; 0, the default, for no ceiling.

properties.name: radius
properties.description: sphere: its radius around `position`.

properties.name: labels
properties.description: Free-form labels, found again with `Area.withLabel`.

properties.name: metadata
properties.description: Anything JSON can hold, kept on the area for scripts.

properties.name: virtualWorld
properties.description: The one virtual world it belongs to; every world when omitted.

properties.name: collision
properties.description: Invisible boundary collision from both sides; false when omitted. Polygons need a simple outline and positive height. Boxes and polygons get side walls only unless `collisionFloor` or `collisionCeiling` asks for more; spheres use a tessellated shell.

properties.name: collisionFloor
properties.description: box and shape: also close the bottom of the boundary with a plate across the whole interior; false when omitted.

properties.name: collisionCeiling
properties.description: box and shape: also close the top of the boundary with a plate across the whole interior; false when omitted.

properties.name: collisionThickness
properties.description: The boundary's thickness in metres, centred on the outline: 0.2 when omitted, from 0.05 to 2.

properties.name: enabled
properties.description: Whether it starts enabled; true when omitted.

properties.name: guid
properties.description: The door's level EntityGuid as hex, which `Door.find` takes.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The entity name the level gives the door.

properties.name: position
properties.description: Where the level places the door.

properties.name: link
properties.description: The `crime_doorKind` the level gives the link: the way in, an inner door, or a storage room's.

symbols.name: Area
symbols.description: Handle for one area: one of the level's own gameplay areas, or one a script or the World Builder drew. The server tests who is inside itself, by the game's own rule for that kind of area.

constructor.name: constructor
constructor.description: Wraps an area handle the server already holds; use Area.create, Area.getById or the lookups to get one.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: Internal area handle.

functions.name: toString
functions.description: Formats this area for logging and debugging.

returns.description: Its id, kind, type and name.

functions.name: contains
functions.description: Tests a position the way the game tests its own areas, whether or not the area is enabled and in whatever world.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: The world position to test.

returns.description: True when the position is inside.

functions.name: containsPlayer
functions.description: Tests where a body stands right now, and in which world: an area bound to another virtual world does not contain it. This is containment only -- whether the game considers the player to be trespassing is decided by its own crime system on the player's client.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: The body to test; a player who has not reported a pose yet is never inside.

returns.description: True when the body is inside.

functions.name: setShape
functions.description: Moves, turns or reshapes a script area. Bodies standing where it now is, or was, get their `areaEnter` and `areaExit` on the next tick. A level area cannot be reshaped.

parameters.name: definition
parameters.description: The shape fields to change; any left out keep their value. `id`, `labels`, `metadata` and the rest are ignored here.

returns.description: False for a level area, a gone one, or a shape the engine could not build.

functions.name: destroy
functions.description: Removes a script area. Every body still inside gets its `areaExit` first, while the handle still resolves.

returns.description: False for a level area or one already gone.

functions.name: toJSON
functions.description: The definition `Area.create` takes to build this area again, which is what a script saves: the server keeps nothing past a restart. It is the format the World Builder exports too.

returns.description: Null for a level area, which the level always builds.

functions.name: getHerbs
functions.description: Lists available authored herbs whose source positions are inside this area's current geometry. Works without nearby players. Picked and script-removed plants are excluded. Ignores area.enabled; an area in another world or a destroyed area returns an empty array.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: One virtual-world bucket; defaults to the area's world, or 0 for an area in every world. Pass player.virtualWorld for a player's bucket. 0xffffffff selects only the global bucket. Invalid IDs throw.

functions.name: removeHerbs
functions.description: Removes authored herbs inside this area's current geometry for one world, including plants already waiting to regrow. Gives no items or experience and raises no harvest events. Plants stay removed until an explicit respawn or server restart, even if the area's geometry, enabled state or lifetime changes.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: One virtual-world bucket; defaults to the area's world, or 0 for an area in every world. Pass player.virtualWorld for a player's bucket. 0xffffffff selects only the global bucket. Invalid IDs throw.

returns.description: Number of sources newly marked for removal; repeated removal returns 0. Includes picked plants whose regrowth was disabled.

functions.name: respawnHerbs
functions.description: Restores picked and script-removed herbs inside this area's current geometry in one world. Restores vegetation for connected players and future arrivals. Ignores area.enabled; an area in another world or a destroyed area changes nothing.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: One virtual-world bucket; defaults to the area's world, or 0 for an area in every world. Pass player.virtualWorld for a player's bucket. 0xffffffff selects only the global bucket. Invalid IDs throw.

returns.description: Number of active harvested or removed sources restored.

functions.name: create
functions.description: Builds a script area. Bodies already standing in it get `areaEnter` on the next tick. Kept in memory only: save `area.toJSON()` wherever the resource keeps its data, and create it again on boot.

parameters.name: definition
parameters.description: The area to build, in the format `area.toJSON()` and the World Builder export write.

returns.description: The new area. Throws for an id already taken or a shape the engine could not build.

functions.name: getById
functions.description: Looks an area up by its stable identity.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A script area's id, or a level area's GUID in hex as `area.definition.id` prints it.

returns.description: The area, or null when there is none.

functions.name: getAt
functions.description: Every enabled area containing a position, level and script alike.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: The world position to test.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional world; when given, a script area bound to another world is left out.

returns.description: The areas, in no particular order.

functions.name: getAtPlayer
functions.description: Every enabled area the body stands in right now, in its own world.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: The body whose position and world to test.

returns.description: The areas; empty for a player who has not reported a pose yet.

functions.name: nearby
functions.description: Every area whose bounds come within a radius of a position, enabled or not.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Where to look from.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: How far, in metres, from the area's bounds.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional world; when given, a script area bound to another world is left out.

returns.description: The areas, nearest first.

functions.name: withLabel
functions.description: Every area carrying a label, such as `private` or `castle`.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label, compared without regard to case.

returns.description: The areas, level ones first.

functions.name: all
functions.description: Every area the server knows.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Optional: only the level's areas, or only script ones.

returns.description: The areas, level ones first.

properties.name: exists
properties.description: False once a script area has been destroyed; every other read then returns its empty value.

properties.name: id
properties.description: The stable identity to store an area under. A level area's is its EntityGuid as sixteen lowercase hex digits, the same on every machine and every boot, as `door.guid` prints a door's; a script area's is the id it was created with.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: Whether the level placed it or a script built it.

properties.name: type
properties.description: A level area's entity class -- a `TriggerArea` prism, an `AreaUnion` of them, or a `SmartAreaShape` -- or a script area's shape.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The level's entity name, or the script area's name. Only a script area's can be changed.

properties.name: labels
properties.description: The level's own `Label` values -- `private`, `personal`, `interior`, `prohibited`, `castle` and the rest the game's AI reads -- or a script area's labels. Only a script area's can be changed.

properties.name: metadata
properties.description: Whatever a script keeps on a script area: ownership, a type, rules. Stored as JSON, so read it, change it and assign it back. Always empty on a level area.

properties.name: collision
properties.description: Invisible boundary walls block both directions while enabled, leaving the interior empty. Authored areas only; invalid collision shapes throw.

properties.name: collisionFloor
properties.description: Whether a box or polygon boundary also closes its bottom with a plate across the whole interior. False by default, for side walls only. A sphere is always one closed shell. Authored areas only.

properties.name: collisionCeiling
properties.description: Whether a box or polygon boundary also closes its top with a plate across the whole interior. False by default, for side walls only. A sphere is always one closed shell. Authored areas only.

properties.name: collisionThickness
properties.description: How thick the boundary is, in metres, centred on the drawn outline: 0.2 by default, from 0.05 to 2. Throws when the shape is too small for it while collision is on. Authored areas only.

properties.name: enabled
properties.description: Whether crossings are raised and the lookups find it. Switching it off raises `areaExit` for everyone inside on the next tick; switching it on, `areaEnter`. Works on level areas too.

properties.name: virtualWorld
properties.description: The one virtual world a script area belongs to, or null for all of them. A body in another world still crosses it, with `matchingVirtualWorld` false. A level area is in every world.

properties.name: position
properties.description: A script area's origin, which its shape is placed from; assignment moves it. A level area's is the centre of its bounds.

properties.name: rotation
properties.description: A script area's orientation; assignment turns it. A level area's shape is already in world space, so its rotation is the identity.

properties.name: height
properties.description: How far above its lowest point a prism reaches, in metres; 0 for a shape with no ceiling. A TriggerArea's comes from the level's baked prism.

properties.name: location
properties.description: For a SmartAreaShape bound to one of the game's map locations, that location's English name, e.g. a settlement. Empty otherwise.

properties.name: bounds
properties.description: The world box around the area. An area with no ceiling reaches far above and below.

properties.name: members
properties.description: For an AreaUnion, the TriggerAreas it joins; it contains whatever one of them does. Empty otherwise.

properties.name: doors
properties.description: The doors the level itself links to this area as its `crime_door`s, which is how the game knows a house's doors. Only native links: nothing is inferred from where a door stands.

properties.name: players
properties.description: Every player inside as of the last tick, in any world.

properties.name: occupants
properties.description: Every body inside as of the last tick: players, horses, carts and server NPCs.

symbols.name: WorldResource
symbols.description: A named world export loaded from mod.world_resources. Server-owned, with live access to its surviving props, effects, level edits, doors, smart objects, items, areas and patrol routes. Obtain handles through all or find; runtime loading, reloading and unloading are not exposed.

functions.name: all
functions.description: Lists config-loaded world exports in configuration order. Empty before successful startup and after shutdown.

returns.description: A fresh array of resource handles.

functions.name: find
functions.description: Finds a config-loaded export by name. Throws for a non-string argument.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Exact, case-sensitive resource name.

returns.description: The resource, or null when absent or startup has not completed.

properties.name: name
properties.description: Unique case-sensitive resource name: the filename without .world.json, or the explicit config name. Empty after shutdown.

properties.name: path
properties.description: Resolved absolute source file path, in UTF-8. Empty after shutdown.

properties.name: level
properties.description: The exported game level, checked against the server level at startup. Empty after shutdown.

properties.name: loaded
properties.description: Whether this export is registered. Remains true even if scripts destroy all of its contents.

properties.name: props
properties.description: A fresh array of surviving props in export order. Changing the array does not change membership; the handles support normal Prop operations.

properties.name: lights
properties.description: A fresh array of surviving point lights in export order, excluding destroyed lights.

properties.name: effects
properties.description: A fresh array of surviving effects in export order, excluding destroyed effects.

properties.name: levelEdits
properties.description: A fresh array of surviving level edits in export order, excluding restored edits.

properties.name: doors
properties.description: A fresh array of the surviving doors the export hangs, in export order, excluding destroyed ones. A door the export takes out of the level is a level edit, in `levelEdits`; `Door.removed` lists those.

properties.name: smartObjects
properties.description: A fresh array of the surviving seats, beds, tables and stations the export places, in export order, excluding destroyed ones. A level station the export takes out is a level edit, in `levelEdits`.

properties.name: items
properties.description: A fresh array of the stacks the export lays on the ground that nobody has picked up yet, in export order. Each one's `name` is the name the export gave it.

properties.name: areas
properties.description: A fresh array of surviving exported areas in export order, excluding destroyed areas.

properties.name: patrolRoutes
properties.description: Surviving exported patrol definitions, in export order.

properties.name: ready
properties.description: True after every configured export has loaded successfully, even when the config list is empty. Check this before subscribing to worldResourcesReady when a script may start later.

symbols.name: Stash
symbols.description: Container handle for a spawned chest, a level chest, or virtual stock without a world entity.

constructor.name: constructor
constructor.description: Creates a script wrapper for an existing container with this ID; use Stash.spawn() for a chest, Stash.createVirtual() for stock without a chest, or Stash.find() for one the level places.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

functions.name: toString
functions.description: Formats this container handle for logging and debugging.

returns.description: The stash ID, its level GUID, how much is in it, who has it open and whether it is locked.

functions.name: destroy
functions.description: Destroys this scripted chest or virtual stash and forgets what was in it. Anything inside goes with it. Does nothing to a container the level places.

functions.name: open
functions.description: Opens a virtual stash from anywhere in its virtual world. Calls stashInteract before granting exclusive access. Returns false for a physical stash, a locked or busy stash, an unavailable player, or a script refusal. A true result requests the screen; the client releases access if it cannot open.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: Player whose native transfer screen should open.

functions.name: getInventory
functions.description: Reads what the container holds. A linked child reads its master's.

returns.description: A copy of its rows, or null once the container is gone.

functions.name: addItem
functions.description: Puts items in the container, as `Inventory.add` gives them to a player.

type.name: { item: string; amount: number; metadata?: Record<string, unknown>; revision?: number }

functions.name: removeItem
functions.description: Takes exact units out of named rows, every one of them or none.

functions.name: setInventory
functions.description: Replaces everything in the container, which is how saved contents come back. At most 128 rows. An empty list empties it.

type.name: { items: { id?: string; item: string; amount: number; metadata?: Record<string, unknown> }[]; revision?: number }

functions.name: createVirtual
functions.description: Creates empty server-owned stock without spawning a chest on any client. Supports the same inventory methods and events as physical stashes. Use open(player) to show the native transfer screen, and destroy() to discard it. Contents last until destroyed or the server restarts.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: World whose players may open it, as a uint32 number; defaults to the global world. Invalid values throw before creating stock.

functions.name: spawn
functions.description: Spawns and replicates an empty container. Fill it with `addItem` or `setInventory`, or let players put things in it.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Optional world-space spawn position; omitted components default to zero.

parameters.name: rotation
parameters.description: Optional initial orientation: a Quaternion, or a Vector3 of Euler angles in degrees.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world the container belongs to; omitted puts it in the global one.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `model` builds it as any .cgf, .cga or .cdf -- a cabinet such as `objects/manmade/common_furniture/cabinets/cabinet_fancy_d.cgf` -- instead of the default chest. Throws on any other path. A mesh without the game's open and close clips stays shut while it is looted.

returns.description: The newly spawned container handle.

functions.name: all
functions.description: Lists every container the server currently has: every one the level places, which exist from boot in the global world, and every scripted chest or virtual stash. In another virtual world a level container is built the first time anything there reaches it, so this lists only those.

returns.description: One handle per live container, in no particular order.

functions.name: getById
functions.description: Looks a container up by its network entity ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Network entity identifier.

returns.description: The container's handle, or null when no live container has that ID.

functions.name: find
functions.description: Looks a container up by its EntityGuid: one the level places, by the level's own identity for it, which survives a restart and is the same on every machine, and is found in any virtual world; or one a script spawned, in the virtual world it was spawned in, for as long as it exists.

parameters.name: guid
parameters.description: The container's EntityGuid as hex, with or without an `0x` prefix, as `stash.guid` prints it.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to look in; omitted looks in the global one, where every body starts.

returns.description: The container's handle, or null when no container has that GUID there.

functions.name: nearest
functions.description: Finds the physical container nearest a point, level or spawned. Virtual stock is excluded. The server knows where every container the level places stands, so this answers at once, without asking a client.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: The point to measure from, usually a player's position.

parameters.name: maxDistance
parameters.description: How far to look, in metres; omitted looks 5 m, about the reach the game gives a chest.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to look in; omitted looks in the global one.

returns.description: The nearest container's handle, or null when none is that close.

functions.name: destroyAll
functions.description: Destroys scripted chests and virtual stashes, including everything inside. The level's own stay.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to clear; omitted clears every one of them.

returns.description: How many containers were removed.

properties.name: stashId
properties.description: The server-minted identity of a scripted chest or virtual stash, from 1. Distinct from the network entity id. Virtual stashes use it for an inventory GUID without creating a chest. 0 for a level chest.

properties.name: guid
properties.description: The EntityGuid every client finds this container under, as sixteen lowercase hex digits: the level's own for a container the level places, the one minted when a script spawned it otherwise. Empty for virtual stock; `Stash.find` takes physical container GUIDs back.

properties.name: levelGuid
properties.description: The level's own EntityGuid for a container the level places, as sixteen lowercase hex digits; empty for a scripted chest or virtual stock. The same on every machine, so it is the identity to store a container under; `Stash.find` takes it back.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The entity name the level gives the container, or `spawned_stash_<stashId>` for a scripted chest; empty for virtual stock.

properties.name: itemCount
properties.description: How many rows the server is holding. A container linked to another in the level opens that one's contents, and reads them here too.

properties.name: isOpen
properties.description: Whether a player holds its view. Physical chests animate their lid by it; virtual stashes have no lid.

properties.name: isVirtual
properties.description: Whether this stash has stock without a chest entity. Open it with open(player); its position and rotation do not govern access, and guid is empty.

properties.name: holderId
properties.description: The network ID of the player who has its contents open, or 0. While it is held, every other player's open is refused before their transfer screen appears.

properties.name: locked
properties.description: Whether the container is locked. Assignment reaches every client that has it streamed in. A locked container offers only its key and its lockpick; a script locking one marks it `lockedByServer`, which the generated home or shop key does not open. Unlocking it by any route the server accepted clears both.

properties.name: lockedByServer
properties.description: Whether the lock was set by a script rather than by the level. The generated home or shop key does not open a container locked from here.

properties.name: lockpickable
properties.description: Whether the container offers the lockpick while locked. Starts as the level authored it; assignment reaches every client, and a pick on one that cannot be is refused.

properties.name: lockDifficulty
properties.description: How hard the lockpicking minigame is, from 0 to 1, or null for what the level gave it. The game's prompt names it in fifths: below 0.2 very easy, then easy, average, hard, and from 0.8 very hard. Assignment reaches every client and applies from the next pick; null gives the level's back.

properties.name: lockFanciness
properties.description: Which lock the lockpicking minigame shows, or null for the level's. Assignment reaches every client.

properties.name: model
properties.description: The model a scripted container was spawned with, or empty for the default chest and for one the level places.

properties.name: keyItem
properties.description: The item class GUID of the key that unlocks the container, as `player.giveItem` takes it. Reads the level's own key until a script assigns one; empty when it has none. Assigning a class makes every client ask for that class instead, so a player holding it is offered "unlock and open"; assigning an empty string restores the level's. An unknown class is refused and logged. The server does not see inventories: which key a player holds is their client's to say, and `stashInteract` is where a script checks its own record.

properties.name: useDirection
properties.description: The horizontal unit direction a player has to face the container along to be offered it: the game's own use check only offers a chest to a body standing behind this axis and looking along it. Stand at `position - useDirection * distance` to face it.

properties.name: startsLocked
properties.description: Whether the level builds this container locked, which is the state it has at boot. False for one a script spawned.

symbols.name: World
symbols.description: The server's own clock and weather, which every client follows, and the three questions it can ask a client's engine about the level itself.

functions.name: pointsOfInterest
functions.description: Points of interest in the configured level only, from the compiled game catalog. Positions are ground-marker clusters checked against the level navmesh; a teleport still needs the destination to stream on the client.

type.name: { name: string; group: string; level: string; position: { x: number; y: number; z: number } }[]

functions.name: setTime
functions.description: Winds the clock forward to an absolute day and hour, which is how a saved clock is restored.

parameters.name: day
parameters.description: Absolute day to wind forward to, as the `day` property counts them. Must be whole.

parameters.name: hour
parameters.description: Hour of that day, from 0 up to but not including 24.

returns.description: True when the clock moved; false when that moment is already past, or the day or hour is out of range.

functions.name: setHour
functions.description: Winds the clock forward to the next time it is this hour, rolling into tomorrow when it has passed today. The clock never runs backwards: clients cannot be wound back with it.

parameters.name: hour
parameters.description: Hour to wind forward to, from 0 up to but not including 24.

returns.description: True when the clock moved; false when the hour is out of range.

functions.name: setTimeScale
functions.description: Sets how fast the day passes for everyone.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: Game seconds per real second, from 0 to 200. 0 freezes the clock where it stands.

returns.description: True when the scale was taken; false when it is out of range.

functions.name: setWeather
functions.description: Blends the sky to another of the game's time-of-day presets, and raises `worldWeatherChange`. Only a client can tell whether a preset exists, so a name the game does not know leaves every sky where it is.

parameters.name: preset
parameters.description: Name of one of the game's own time-of-day presets, such as `cloudless_sunny`.

parameters.name: seconds
parameters.description: Game seconds to blend over, up to 21600. Omitted, the sky changes at once.

returns.description: True when the blend started; false while an earlier one is still running, or when the name or duration is out of range.

functions.name: setRain
functions.description: Sets the rain, which is separate from the sky preset: a preset can be overcast without a drop falling. Starting or stopping it restarts the phase the ground soaks and dries over.

parameters.name: intensity
parameters.description: How hard it rains, from 0 to 1. 0 stops it.

parameters.name: amount
parameters.description: How much of the rain is drawn, from 0 to 1; defaults to all of it.

returns.description: True when the rain was taken; false when either value is out of range.

functions.name: setWind
functions.description: Sets the wind for everyone. There is nothing to blend against -- the engine takes a vector and holds it -- so a gust is a script ramping this itself. It also drives a physical wind area, which is why the length is capped.

parameters.name: wind
parameters.description: Wind velocity in metres per second, world space; omitted components are zero. Its length may not exceed 50.

returns.description: True when the wind was taken; false when a component is not finite or it blows harder than 50 m/s.

functions.name: raycast
functions.description:
Traces a segment through the world and reports the first thing it meets.

The server has no world of its own, so this asks that player's client and waits for it to answer. Three things follow: the answer is a round trip late; it covers only what that machine has streamed in, so a point far from the player reads as empty world; and it is a client's word, which is fine for a prompt and is not fine for anything a player gains by lying about. The promise always settles -- on the answer, on a five-second timeout, or when the player leaves -- and `answered` says which.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: Whose client is asked. Their machine is the one that answers, so pick a player near the point in question.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Where the ray starts, in world-space metres.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Where it ends. Up to 4096 metres away; a ray of no length is refused.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `mode` picks which of the game's own three traces to run: `cover` asks whether the world is in the way -- static geometry, props and doors block, and bodies cannot, which is what a line of sight wants; `anything` asks what is under the ray, bodies included, which is what a pick wants; `ground` sees only surfaces a player could stand on. It defaults to `cover`, and a name that is none of the three is rejected rather than guessed at.

returns.description: The trace, once that client has run it.

functions.name: raycastAll
functions.description:
Traces a segment and reports everything solid along it, nearest first.

The server has no world of its own, so this asks that player's client and waits for it to answer. Three things follow: the answer is a round trip late; it covers only what that machine has streamed in, so a point far from the player reads as empty world; and it is a client's word, which is fine for a prompt and is not fine for anything a player gains by lying about. The promise always settles -- on the answer, on a five-second timeout, or when the player leaves -- and `answered` says which.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: Whose client is asked. Their machine is the one that answers, so pick a player near the point in question.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Where the ray starts, in world-space metres.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Where it ends. Up to 4096 metres away; a ray of no length is refused.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `mode` is as `World.raycast` documents it. `maxHits` is how many things along the ray to report, up to 8 and 8 by default; each is a separate solid hit, found by re-tracing past the one before, so a window does not hide the wall it is set in.

returns.description: The trace, once that client has run it.

functions.name: resolveGround
functions.description:
What is underfoot at a point: its height in `hit.position.z`, the slope it landed on, and what the surface is made of.

A trace rather than a terrain height, so it stands on whatever is actually there -- a bridge, a floor, a castle roof -- and not on the heightmap underneath it. There is no bare-number form here, because a promise has to be able to say that nothing answered.

The server has no world of its own, so this asks that player's client and waits for it to answer. Three things follow: the answer is a round trip late; it covers only what that machine has streamed in, so a point far from the player reads as empty world; and it is a client's word, which is fine for a prompt and is not fine for anything a player gains by lying about. The promise always settles -- on the answer, on a five-second timeout, or when the player leaves -- and `answered` says which.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: Whose client is asked. Their machine is the one that answers, so pick a player near the point in question.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: The point to look under, in world-space metres. Its own z is where the probe is centred.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: How far above the point the probe starts and how far below it reaches, in metres. 5 and 200 by default -- the 5 above is what lets a point already slightly underground still resolve -- and up to 512 each.

returns.description: The probe, once that client has run it.

functions.name: replicasInRadius
functions.description:
The server's own replicated entities near a point, nearest first -- players, horses, dogs, props, dropped items, doors, gates and stashes, each as its own handle.

This needs no client: the server already knows where its replicas are, so unlike `entitiesInRadius` it is immediate and authoritative. It sees only what the server replicates, which is the other half -- the level's own entities are what `entitiesInRadius` is for.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: World-space point to measure from.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: How far to look, in metres.

parameters.name: virtualWorld
parameters.description: Optional virtual world to look in; omitted looks in the global one, where every body starts.

returns.description: The handles, nearest first.

functions.name: entitiesInRadius
functions.description:
Every entity that client's engine has inside a sphere, nearest first.

It reads the engine's own spatial grid, so it costs what the sphere covers rather than what the level holds. This reports the level's entities -- doors, props, bodies -- and not the server's replicas; correlate them by `guid`.

The server has no world of its own, so this asks that player's client and waits for it to answer. Three things follow: the answer is a round trip late; it covers only what that machine has streamed in, so a point far from the player reads as empty world; and it is a client's word, which is fine for a prompt and is not fine for anything a player gains by lying about. The promise always settles -- on the answer, on a five-second timeout, or when the player leaves -- and `answered` says which.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: Whose client is asked. Their machine is the one that answers, so pick a player near the point in question.

parameters.name: centre
parameters.description: The centre of the sphere, in world-space metres.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: Its radius in metres, up to 256.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `class` reports only entities of that engine class -- `AnimDoor`, `NPC_NAI`, `GeomEntity` -- and a class the engine does not know matches nothing rather than everything; omitted, every class is reported. `max` is how many to report, nearest first, up to 64. `physicalOnly` skips entities the engine has built no physics for, which is the filter the game's own proximity query applies, and is off by default.

type.name: { class?: string; max?: number; physicalOnly?: boolean }

returns.description: The entities, once that client has looked.

properties.name: level
properties.description: The configured level loaded by every client in this server session.

properties.name: day
properties.description: Whole days the clock has run, from the level's own midnight. Starts at 0 and only grows.

properties.name: hour
properties.description: Hour within the current day, from 0 up to but not including 24, with the minutes as the fraction. 13.5 is half past one.

properties.name: timeScale
properties.description: How many game seconds pass per real second. 15 is the game's own pace, 0 stops the clock, and the server drops it to 0 by itself at the clock's ceiling.

properties.name: weather
properties.description: The time-of-day preset the sky is blending towards, which is where it settles. Set it with `setWeather`.

properties.name: previousWeather
properties.description: The preset the sky is blending from; the same as `weather` once it has settled.

properties.name: weatherBlending
properties.description: Whether a blend is still running. `setWeather` is refused while it is: a half-finished blend has no single preset to leave from.

properties.name: weatherRemaining
properties.description: Game seconds left of the blend, and 0 once the sky has settled. `setWeather` is refused until then.

properties.name: rainIntensity
properties.description: How hard it is raining, from 0 to 1.

properties.name: rainAmount
properties.description: How much of the rain is drawn, from 0 to 1. Thins the downpour without stopping it.

properties.name: wind
properties.description: The wind every client is blowing, in metres per second, world space. It bends the trees, drags the cloth and slants the rain, and it is the one part of the weather the game itself never touches. Set it with `setWind`.

properties.name: windSpeed
properties.description: How hard the wind is blowing, whichever way: the length of `wind`, from 0 to 50.

properties.name: wetness
properties.description: How wet the ground has become, from 0 to 3. Derived from how long it has been raining, so it is read-only, and it dries far slower than it soaks.

properties.name: puddles
properties.description: Puddle coverage, from 0 to 1. Derived like `wetness`, and only starts filling after the rain has run a while.

symbols.name: WorldRayHit
symbols.description: One thing a trace met, as the machine that traced it saw it.

properties.name: position
properties.description: Where the ray met it, in world-space metres.

properties.name: normal
properties.description: The surface normal at that point, as a unit vector.

properties.name: distance
properties.description: How far along the ray it sits, in metres.

properties.name: surface
properties.description: The surface type's own name, spelled the way the game's tables spell it in `Libs/MaterialEffects/SurfaceTypes.xml` -- `mat_wood`, `mat_rock`, `mat_soil`, `mat_water`. It says what the thing is made of, which is how footsteps and blows sound, not what it is: a plank wall is `mat_wood` as much as a trunk is, so tell a tree by `category`. Among the 74 the game defines: `mat_wood`, `mat_wood_soft`, `mat_vegetation`, `mat_bushes`, `mat_rock`, `mat_rock_unwalk`, `mat_rock_horse_ignore`, `mat_stairs_stone`, `mat_gravel`, `mat_soil`, `mat_mud`, `mat_grass`, `mat_road`, `mat_metal`, `mat_glass`, `mat_plaster`, `mat_thatch`, `mat_fabric`, `mat_flesh`. Empty only before the material tables are up.

properties.name: terrain
properties.description: Whether the ground itself was hit rather than anything placed on it. Nothing lies behind the terrain, so a trace stops there. The same as `kind` being `terrain`.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: What sort of thing the ray stopped on. `entity` is anything with an `entityClass` -- doors, props, NPCs, players. `vegetation` is an instance the level paints on: trees, bushes, plants, and boulders painted the same way. `brush` is a static mesh placed one by one: walls, houses, rocks and cliffs. `static` is static geometry that is neither, or whose source the engine does not record. Trees and rocks are not entities, so for them this, `model` and `category` are what say what was hit.

properties.name: model
properties.description: The mesh of a vegetation instance or a brush, as the path the game loads it from -- `objects/natural/vegetation/trees/normal_trees/quercus_robur/quercus_robur_big_a.cgf`. Null for terrain, entities and `static`. A tree or a rock has no GUID, but its `model` and `position` together are the same on every client on the same level, which is what a server keeps a felled tree or a mined rock by.

properties.name: category
properties.description: Which of the game's own folders of natural objects `model` comes from: `tree` for `objects/natural/vegetation/trees` -- living, dead, fallen and stumps alike, which `model` tells apart -- `bush` for its bushes, `plant` for the rest of its vegetation (grass, ferns, mushrooms, branches), and `rock` for `objects/natural/rocks` and `objects/natural/stones`. Null for anything else, man-made included.

properties.name: material
properties.description: The material drawn where the ray met it, as the path the material manager keys it by, the sub-material when the mesh has several -- a trunk's bark rather than the tree's whole material. Null for terrain and when nothing names one.

properties.name: entityGuid
properties.description: The level's own identity for what was hit, as sixteen lowercase hex digits -- the same on every machine, and what `Door.find` and the other GUID lookups take. Null for terrain, for static geometry and for anything the session spawned, none of which the level names.

properties.name: entityName
properties.description: The name the level gives it, often empty. Null when nothing that carries a name was hit.

properties.name: entityClass
properties.description: The engine class it belongs to -- `AnimDoor`, `NPC_NAI`, `GeomEntity`. Null when nothing that carries a class was hit.

properties.name: levelObject
properties.description: The object the level placed that was hit, named the way `LevelEdit.apply` finds it again on every machine, with where the level put it and how it turned and sized it. A tree, a rock or a wall is one; so is a door or any other entity the level gives a GUID. Null for terrain, for static geometry the engine records no source for, and for anything the session spawned -- props, players, NPCs. Spread it into a definition to take the object out or swap it: `LevelEdit.apply({ ...hit.levelObject, model: stump })`.

symbols.name: WorldLevelObject
symbols.description: An object the level placed, as a level edit keys it, and the pose the level gave it. Every field a `LevelEditDefinition` needs to find it again.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: A `brush` is a static mesh or a vegetation instance -- a wall, a rock, a tree -- found by its mesh and where the level put it. An `entity` is found by its GUID.

properties.name: name
properties.description: A brush's mesh path, the same as the hit's `model`; an entity's name.

properties.name: guid
properties.description: An entity's level GUID as sixteen lowercase hex digits; absent for a brush.

properties.name: class
properties.description: An entity's engine class; absent for a brush.

properties.name: at
properties.description: Where the level put it: its pivot, not the point the ray met. Unchanged while an edit has moved it, since it is the key.

properties.name: rotation
properties.description: How the level turned it, for a prop or effect standing in its place. `LevelEdit.apply` reads a rotation only with a `position`, so spreading this into a definition moves nothing.

properties.name: scale
properties.description: How the level sized it, per axis. Read only with a `position`, as `rotation` is.

symbols.name: WorldNearbyEntity
symbols.description: One entity a sphere reported, and where it stood when it did.

properties.name: position
properties.description: Where it is, in world-space metres.

properties.name: distance
properties.description: How far it is from the centre of the sphere, in metres.

properties.name: guid
properties.description: The level's own identity for it, as sixteen lowercase hex digits. Null for anything the session spawned, which the level does not name.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The name the level gives it, often empty.

properties.name: class
properties.description: The engine class it belongs to -- `AnimDoor`, `NPC_NAI`, `GeomEntity`.

properties.name: physicalized
properties.description: Whether the engine has built physics for it, which is what makes it something a trace could also find.

symbols.name: WorldTraceResult
symbols.description: What a trace came back with, and whether it came back at all.

properties.name: answered
properties.description: Whether the client ran the trace. False when it has no world loaded, is in another level, did not answer in time, or left.

properties.name: reason
properties.description: Why it did not answer. Empty when it did.

properties.name: hit
properties.description: The nearest thing the ray met, or null when it met nothing and whenever `answered` is false.

properties.name: hits
properties.description: Everything it met, nearest first. One entry at most unless `maxHits` asked for more; empty whenever `answered` is false.

symbols.name: WorldRadiusResult
symbols.description: What a sphere came back with, and whether it came back at all.

properties.name: answered
properties.description: Whether the client ran the query. False when it has no world loaded, is in another level, did not answer in time, or left.

properties.name: reason
properties.description: Why it did not answer. Empty when it did.

properties.name: entities
properties.description: The entities inside the sphere, nearest first. Empty whenever `answered` is false.

symbols.name: NavigationPath
symbols.description: A walk across the mesh.

properties.name: points
properties.description: The corners to walk through, first the point on the mesh nearest `from`. Straight lines between them stay on the mesh.

properties.name: complete
properties.description: Whether it reaches `to`. False when `to` cannot be reached, and the path then ends at the nearest point the mesh allows.

properties.name: length
properties.description: Its length in metres.

symbols.name: NavigationRay
symbols.description: How far a straight walk across the mesh gets.

properties.name: hit
properties.description: Whether the edge of the mesh -- a wall, a drop, a locked door -- stops it before `to`.

properties.name: point
properties.description: Where it stops: the edge, or the point on the mesh under `to`.

symbols.name: Navigation
symbols.description:
Queries the level's navigation mesh on the server. The mesh includes walkable floors, bridges and stairs.

Copy the game's `Data/Levels/<level>/recast.pak` to the server's `files/<level>/` directory. The server searches `files/` recursively at startup. An optional `mod.navmesh` in `server.json` takes priority and can name a game install, level folder or pak file. The game data must be supplied separately. Without a mesh, `ready` is false and geometry queries return null or false. Points are world-space metres, Z up. Every query takes an optional options object. `searchRadius` and `searchHeight` limit how far a point may be from the mesh, across the ground and up or down: 2 metres by default, up to 64, and 4 by default, up to 128. Keep `searchHeight` under a storey's height, or a point on one floor snaps to the floor above. `doors` picks which doors a query walks through: `unlocked`, the default, is how an NPC treats a door -- open or shut, it goes through unless the door is locked; `open` only through doors that stand open; `any` ignores locks; `none` treats every doorway as a wall. Door states are read in the global world, except validatePatrol with an actor, which uses that actor's world. A field given with the wrong type or out of range throws.

functions.name: validatePatrol
functions.description: Checks all legs, including the closing leg of a loop and reverse legs of ping-pong. Uses the patrol runner's search budget. A single waypoint is checked against itself. Missing mesh reports available false; partial paths are incomplete. This does not start or change an actor's order.

parameters.name: route
parameters.description: A registered route or its id.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Optional actor chooses door policy in its virtual world: unlocked doors for humanoids, no doorways for horses and animals.

type.name: { available: boolean; complete: boolean; legs: { fromIndex: number; toIndex: number; complete: boolean; path: NavigationPath | null }[] }

functions.name: closestPoint
functions.description: Snaps a point to the nearest walkable surface.

parameters.name: point
parameters.description: The point to snap; omitted components default to zero.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: How far to look, and which doors count.

returns.description: The nearest point within the search limits, or null when none is found or no mesh is loaded.

functions.name: floorAt
functions.description: Returns the height of the nearest walkable surface, including upper floors, bridges and stairs.

parameters.name: point
parameters.description: The point to measure; omitted components default to zero. Its z estimates the floor height and selects the storey.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: How far to look.

returns.description: The height in metres, or null when none is found or no mesh is loaded.

functions.name: findPath
functions.description: Plans a path around obstacles on the mesh. Plan when a destination changes; avoid recalculating every NPC's path each tick.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Where the walk starts; omitted components default to zero.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Where it should end; omitted components default to zero.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: How far to look for each end, and which doors to walk through.

returns.description: The path, or null when an endpoint cannot be found, the query fails or no mesh is loaded. A partial path has `complete: false`.

functions.name: canReach
functions.description: Checks reachability by calling `findPath`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Where the walk starts; omitted components default to zero.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Where it should end; omitted components default to zero.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: How far to look for each end, and which doors to walk through.

returns.description: True when a complete path exists; false otherwise, including when no mesh is loaded.

functions.name: raycast
functions.description: Checks a straight line across the mesh and reports where it stops.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Where the walk starts; omitted components default to zero.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Where it heads; only its x and y are used, the walk follows the surface.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: How far to look for `from`, and which doors let the walk through.

returns.description: The result, or null when `from` is off the mesh, the query fails or no mesh is loaded.

functions.name: randomPoint
functions.description: Returns a random walkable point reachable from `center` and no further from it across the ground than `radius`. A point drawn outside the circle is drawn again, a bounded number of times. Without a centre, samples the whole level, choosing each tile with equal probability.

parameters.name: center
parameters.description: The point to scatter around; it has to be on the mesh, and omitted components default to zero. Omitted entirely, the point can be anywhere on the level's mesh; pass `undefined` for it and for `radius` to give options.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: How far from `center`, in metres, up to 512. Required with a centre.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: How far to look for `center`, and which doors the point may lie behind.

returns.description: The point, or null when `center` is off the mesh, no draw lands within `radius`, the query fails or no mesh is loaded.

functions.name: enableOverlay
functions.description: Enables an overlay. Where overlays overlap, the last enabled takes precedence. Subsequent queries use the updated mesh.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: An entry of `overlays`.

returns.description: False for a name the level does not ship, one already enabled, one whose tiles cannot be read or loaded (the server log says why), or without a mesh.

functions.name: disableOverlay
functions.description: Disables an overlay, restoring the previous enabled overlay or the base mesh in that area.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: An entry of `activeOverlays`.

returns.description: False for a name that is not enabled, or when part of the area could not be restored (the server log says why); the overlay is disabled either way.

properties.name: ready
properties.description: Whether a mesh loaded from `mod.navmesh` or the server's `files/` directory. False when no usable copy is found; the server log gives the reason.

properties.name: overlays
properties.description: Available overlay names, sorted. Overlays contain replacement navigation data for quest states. Enabling one replaces the covered part of the mesh. Empty without a mesh.

properties.name: activeOverlays
properties.description: Enabled overlays in activation order. Initially empty; the level starts with its base mesh.

symbols.name: CustomBuffDefinition
symbols.description: Immutable custom effect, with an existing native buff supplying its icon.

properties.name: name
properties.description: Display name; 1 to 256 UTF-8 bytes.

properties.name: description
properties.description: Optional description, up to 4096 UTF-8 bytes.

properties.name: visual
properties.description: Existing game buff name or GUID; only presentation is borrowed.

properties.name: duration
properties.description: Positive real seconds up to seven days, or -1 for permanent; default -1.

properties.name: tickInterval
properties.description: Server lifecycle callback interval in seconds; zero disables, otherwise 0.1 to 86400. Default zero.

properties.name: stackable
properties.description: Default false. When true, each application has its own native timer and modifiers.

properties.name: maxStacks
properties.description: Integer 1 to 16; default 1.

properties.name: refresh
properties.description: Default true. At the stack limit, replaces the oldest instance with a full-duration instance; false ignores applications at the limit.

properties.name: modifiers
properties.description: Optional native modifiers. A number adds points. Buffs.modifiers lists supported names. healthRegeneration adds health per second. Effective stat changes do not change earned XP.

symbols.name: BuffInfo
symbols.description: What the game's own tables say about one status effect.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The name the game's own buff tables give the effect, and the spelling every buff verb takes.

properties.name: class
properties.description: The kind of effect it is -- `poison`, `alcohol`, `injury`, `potion`. `Buffs.classes` lists the ones a server can take over.

properties.name: aiTag
properties.description: The family `player.clearBuffs` would take it off with, or null for the majority that belong to none.

properties.name: duration
properties.description: How long the effect runs from start to finish, in real seconds, and negative for one with no end.

properties.name: custom
properties.description: Whether this definition was registered with Buffs.register.

properties.name: displayName
properties.description: Registered display text for a custom effect; null for a native effect.

properties.name: description
properties.description: Registered description for a custom effect; null for a native effect.

symbols.name: BuffState
symbols.description: One status effect currently on a body: everything `BuffInfo` says about it, plus how long it has been there and who put it there.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The name the game's own buff tables give the effect, and the spelling every buff verb takes.

properties.name: class
properties.description: The kind of effect it is -- `poison`, `alcohol`, `injury`, `potion`. `Buffs.classes` lists the ones a server can take over.

properties.name: aiTag
properties.description: The family `player.clearBuffs` would take it off with, or null for the majority that belong to none.

properties.name: duration
properties.description: How long the effect runs from start to finish, in real seconds, and negative for one with no end.

properties.name: custom
properties.description: Whether this definition was registered with Buffs.register.

properties.name: displayName
properties.description: Registered display text for a custom effect; null for a native effect.

properties.name: description
properties.description: Registered description for a custom effect; null for a native effect.

properties.name: since
properties.description: How long it has been on the body, in real seconds. `duration - since` is roughly what is left, and roughly is the best anyone can do: the game advances buff time from each client's own frame delta. 0 for an effect that was already there when the player connected.

properties.name: source
properties.description: Whether this server put it there, or the game did -- a potion they drank, an injury they took.

symbols.name: Buffs
symbols.description: The game's status-effect table, and which of it this server decides.

functions.name: register
functions.description: Registers a custom native effect and publishes it to connected and future clients. An identical registration is idempotent; an existing id with another definition throws. Returns a GUID accepted by the existing player buff methods, like Items.register.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique resource-qualified identifier, such as my_resource:blessing.

parameters.name: definition
parameters.description: Immutable definition; unknown keys, unsupported modifiers and invalid values throw.

returns.description: Custom buff GUID.

functions.name: find
functions.description: Looks a status effect up, so a resource can check a name is real before handing it to a player and can see what the effect is before applying it.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: An effect's name, as the game's buff tables spell it, or its GUID.

returns.description: What the tables say about it, or null for a name they do not carry.

functions.name: claim
functions.description:
Takes over whole kinds of effect. Every client then turns down an effect of that kind the game tried to give its own player, and raises `playerBuffBlocked` instead -- which is where the resource decides what really happens, usually `player.addBuff` with its own rule applied. A claim nothing listens to does not move the gameplay here, it removes it.

Two things to plan around. The refusal covers the game's follow-on effects too: claim `alcohol` and the six `alcoholism_level*` steps stop arriving along with the drink, so the resource owns the whole progression. And an effect has no strength -- the handler can block it, swap it for another, or let it through, but it cannot make the drink half as strong.

Replaces the previous claim rather than adding to it, and reaches every connected client at once.

parameters.name: classNames
parameters.description: The kinds of effect to decide, from `Buffs.classes`. `[]` hands them all back. Throws for anything else.

returns.description: The kinds now claimed.

properties.name: modifiers
properties.description: Supported custom modifier names: progression tracks, charisma, maxStamina (stamina alias), maxHealth, carryCapacity, runSpeed, armorRating, bodyArmor, hungerDrain, energyDrain, staminaRegeneration and healthRegeneration. Native query bounds and contexts still apply.

properties.name: classes
properties.description: The kinds of effect a server can take over, which is what `claim` accepts: the ones carrying state nobody can work out for themselves -- potions, poison, injury, drunkenness, illness, unconsciousness. The game has other kinds, and they read back in `BuffInfo.class`, but they either shadow something that already replicates or are the game's own plumbing, so there is no decision in them to take.

properties.name: tags
properties.description: The families the game groups effects into, which is what `player.clearBuffs` takes: `poison`, `bleed`, `alcohol_drunk`, `unconscious` and nineteen more. These are the game's own words, and its own AI reasons in them.

symbols.name: Progression
symbols.description: The game's skills, stats and perks, and the rules this server puts on how players move along them.

functions.name: tracks
functions.description: Every skill and stat a player levels: the fifteen skills the character sheet shows, then strength, agility, vitality, speech and prestige.

returns.description: The tracks, in that order.

functions.name: findPerk
functions.description: Looks a perk up.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: A perk's name, as the game's perk tables spell it, or its GUID.

returns.description: What the tables say about it, or null for a name they do not carry.

functions.name: perks
functions.description: Lists the game's perks: 945 of them, most of them hidden system perks. `Progression.perks({ visibleOnly: true })` is the perk screen.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: `track` keeps the perks one tree pays for -- a track name, or `main`; `visibleOnly` keeps the perks the perk screen shows.

returns.description: The perks, sorted by name.

functions.name: xpForLevel
functions.description: The total XP a track costs from level 0 to `level`, on the game's own curve: each level costs `base + diff * level`, with base and diff from the game's RPG tables.

parameters.name: track
parameters.description: A track name.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: The level to reach.

returns.description: The XP. Throws for a track name the tables do not carry.

functions.name: setNativeXp
functions.description: Switches off XP from play. Every gain the game produces is dropped on the player's own client, and only `player.addXp` and `player.setLevel` move a track -- for servers where progression comes from jobs, trainers or quests a resource runs.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: False to stop players' own games from earning XP at all.

returns.description: Nothing.

functions.name: setXpRate
functions.description: Scales the XP players earn by playing. Applied before the player's own perk multipliers, which still work as they do in single player. `player.addXp` is not scaled.

parameters.name: track
parameters.description: A track name, or `*` for every track.

parameters.name: rate
parameters.description: What a gain is multiplied by before it is granted: 1 is the game's own pace, 0.5 half, 0 none at all.

returns.description: Nothing.

functions.name: setXpBudget
functions.description: Limits how fast a track can be ground. The budget holds a minute's worth and refills steadily, so a burst after a quiet spell goes through and a loop -- two players sparring for sword XP, a lock picked over and over -- runs dry. `player.addXp` is not limited.

parameters.name: track
parameters.description: A track name, or `*` for every track.

parameters.name: xpPerMinute
parameters.description: How much XP a player may earn on the track per minute, before multipliers. 0 is unlimited.

returns.description: Nothing.

functions.name: setLevelCap
functions.description: Stops a track at a level. Gains close to it are granted exactly what is left, so no multiplier carries the track past it. `player.setLevel` and `player.addXp` can still go beyond: the cap rules over what is earned.

parameters.name: track
parameters.description: A track name, or `*` for every track.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: The highest level XP from play may reach, at most the game's own 30.

returns.description: Nothing.

functions.name: blockPerks

symbols.name: Appearances
symbols.description:
The game's own character-component catalog: every face, hairstyle, beard and skin a player's body can be given.

Everyone on a fresh server is Henry, because a body with nothing chosen is the one the game hands out. This is where the alternatives come from; `player.setAppearance` is what puts one on somebody.

functions.name: options
functions.description:
Every option the game ships for one part. The male tree has 212 faces, 262 hairstyles, 51 beards and 47 skins; the female tree has 61, 71, none and 41.

The hairstyle count is large because the game ships each style once per colour rather than colouring one. Group by `option.group` to get the styles back.

The 51 beards are the whole catalog, not what any one body can wear: a beard is modelled per face and only exists for the faces it was modelled for. `Appearances.beards` is the list to show somebody.

parameters.name: part
parameters.description: Which part to list.

parameters.name: gender
parameters.description: Which half of the catalog to read; male by default.

returns.description: The options, in the catalog's own order.

functions.name: beards
functions.description:
The beards that face can actually grow.

A beard is modelled against one head's mesh and stored under that head's own folder, so asking for one the artists never made for the face wearing it does nothing at all -- no error, no beard, a body that comes back clean-shaven. The owning client refuses such a pair outright, so filter a chooser through this rather than through `options("beard")`.

The 164 generic faces carry 24 each, Henry's face carries the 15 the game's own barber offers, and 14 faces carry none.

parameters.name: head
parameters.description: The face to ask about -- a name from `Appearances.options("head")`. Omitted or empty means the face a body nobody has chosen one for wears.

parameters.name: gender
parameters.description: Which half of the catalog the head came from; male by default.

returns.description: The wearable beards, in the catalog's own order. Empty for a female body, for a face with none, and for a name the catalog does not carry.

functions.name: find
functions.description: Looks one component name up, so a resource can check a name is real before handing it to a player.

parameters.name: part
parameters.description: Which part the name is for.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The component name to look up.

parameters.name: gender
parameters.description: Which half of the catalog to look in; male by default.

returns.description: What the catalog says about it, or null for a name it does not carry.

functions.name: random
functions.description:
Picks one option for every part, which is the cheapest way to stop a server full of Henrys. Hand the result straight to `player.setAppearance`.

Uniform over the catalog rather than over what looks good together: the game's own faces and hairstyles are authored for particular NPCs, so a random body is recognisably random. The beard is drawn after the face and only from what that face can wear, so the result is always one a client will accept.

parameters.name: gender
parameters.description: Which half of the catalog to draw from; male by default.

returns.description: A complete appearance. `beard` is empty for a female one, which the catalog has none of, and for the fourteen male faces no beard was modelled for.

symbols.name: AnimationInfo
symbols.description: One animation the game plays on a human body: a Mannequin fragment and the tags that pick its variant, as a row of the game's own `actor_anim_action` table.

properties.name: fragment
properties.description: The fragment's name, which is what `playAnimation` takes.

properties.name: tags
properties.description: The tags that select this variant, `+`-separated, which is what `playAnimation`'s `tags` option takes. Empty for the fragment's default.

properties.name: duration
properties.description: How long one pass lasts, in seconds.

properties.name: oneShot
properties.description: Whether it ends by itself. One that does not is a loop and plays until something replaces it, `loop` or not.

properties.name: fullBody
properties.description: Whether it takes the whole body. A full-body animation stops the legs, so a player playing one is held still unless `lockMovement` says otherwise.

properties.name: rightHand
properties.description: What the right hand is animated holding, as the game names the kind (`bucket`, `axe_tool`), or empty for nothing. Match it against `AnimationPropInfo.hand` to find a prop that fits.

properties.name: leftHand
properties.description: The same for the left hand.

properties.name: male
properties.description: Whether the game has it for a man's body.

properties.name: female
properties.description: Whether the game has it for a woman's body.

properties.name: sequence
properties.description: The in/loop/out sequence this fragment is a part of, shared by every fragment in it (`BakerMill` for `BakerMillIn`, `BakerMillLoop` and `BakerMillOut`), or empty when it is not part of one. The game does not record sequences; this is read from the fragment names, so treat it as a strong hint rather than a guarantee.

properties.name: phase
properties.description: Which part of its `sequence` this is: the way in, the middle part the body stays in, the way out, or a variation played in place of the middle. `loop` is the middle whether or not it ends by itself -- `oneShot` says that, and `playAnimation`'s `loop` repeats it. Empty when `sequence` is.

properties.name: partner
properties.description: The fragment a second actor plays against this one, for the game's two-person animations (`TiedUpOut_Master` for `TiedUpOut_Slave`), or empty. Each actor plays its own fragment; read from the fragment names, like `sequence`.

properties.name: slaveBody
properties.description: Whether, with these tags, the fragment also animates a second character the game binds to the body -- a corpse carried, a horse groomed, a smith's workpiece. `playAnimation` binds none, so only this body moves.

symbols.name: AnimationPropInfo
symbols.description: A model the game puts in a body's hand: one of its tools, from the item tables.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The item's name, which is what a prop's `item` takes.

properties.name: model
properties.description: The model it is drawn with.

properties.name: hand
properties.description: The kind of thing it is (`bucket`, `axe_tool`), which is what `AnimationInfo.rightHand` and `leftHand` name.

symbols.name: Animations
symbols.description: Every animation the game plays on a human body, and the props it gives one to hold. `player.playAnimation` and `npc.playAnimation` play them.

functions.name: list
functions.description: Lists the animations the game plays on people -- over six thousand, from waves and bows to chopping wood, drinking and every tavern pose. These are the game's own combinations, so each one is known to play; `playAnimation` also takes fragments and tags this does not list, and plays whatever the body's animation database makes of them.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Only rows whose fragment or tags contain this, ignoring case. Everything when left out.

returns.description: One row per fragment and tag combination, sorted by fragment.

functions.name: props
functions.description: Lists the tools and carried objects the game puts in people's hands, by item name. Pick one whose `hand` matches the animation's `rightHand` or `leftHand` and it sits in the hand the way the animation was made for.

returns.description: Every prop, sorted by name.

symbols.name: Voice
symbols.description: Server-side proximity voice rules: how far voice carries, and who may talk to or hear whom.

functions.name: setRange
functions.description: Sets how far voice carries for talkers with no override of their own. Connected clients are told, so their playback fades out at the same distance.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: Audibility radius in world units; values <= 0 restore the default of 25.

functions.description: Reads the server-wide proximity range.

parameters.description: Player whose voice carries the given distance.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: Player to query.

returns.description: Radius in world units.

functions.name: setTierRange
functions.description: Sets how far a voice tier carries. Players switch tier themselves; whisper starts at 3, shout at 25, and normal carries the server-wide range. Set a tier to 0 to make it carry the server-wide range, which takes it away. Connected clients are told.

parameters.name: tier
parameters.description: Voice tier: 0 whisper, 1 normal, 2 shout.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: Audibility radius in world units; values <= 0 make the tier carry the server-wide range.

functions.name: getTierRange
functions.description: Reads how far a voice tier carries, with the server-wide range already resolved.

parameters.name: tier
parameters.description: Voice tier: 0 whisper, 1 normal, 2 shout.

parameters.name: tier

parameters.name: player

symbols.name: PendingConnection
symbols.description: A player asking to join, handed to `playerConnecting`. Every identifier is reported by the player's own client and is not verified by the server.

functions.name: reject
functions.description: Turns the player away before they receive anything. Takes effect on the next server tick, whatever other handlers are still doing. Does nothing once the connection is decided or the player has left.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Shown to the player as written, up to 512 bytes. Omitted, they read that the server refused the connection.

functions.name: update
functions.description: Shows the waiting player a line of status and restarts the admission timeout, so a queue that keeps updating its players is never timed out. Does nothing once the connection is decided or the player has left.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: One line for the player's connecting screen, up to 256 bytes: 'Checking the whitelist', 'You are 4th in the queue'.

functions.name: isPending
functions.description: Checks whether this connection is still waiting on a decision.

returns.description: False once it was let in or turned away, or the player gave up and left; a queue drops such entries.

symbols.name: StateBag
symbols.description: Arbitrary key/value state attached to one replicated entity, reached as `entity.state`. Keys set on the server replicate to every client that can currently see the entity.

functions.name: get
functions.description: Reads one key from this entity's state.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Key to read.

returns.description: The stored value, or undefined when the key is not set.

functions.name: has
functions.description: Checks whether this entity's state holds a key.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Key to test.

returns.description: True when the key is set.

functions.name: keys
functions.description: Lists the keys this entity's state holds, sorted.

returns.description: Every key currently set, in ascending order.

functions.name: toObject
functions.description: Copies this entity's whole state into a plain object.

returns.description: Every key and value currently set. The copy does not track later changes.

functions.name: onChange
functions.description: Watches this entity's state. The filter is applied before the handler runs, so a listener watching one key of one entity is not woken by unrelated changes. The subscription is dropped when the registering resource stops.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Only report this key, or null to report every key of this entity.

parameters.name: handler
parameters.description: Called as (key: string, value: any, previous: any) with the changed key, its new value and the value before it. `value` is undefined when the key was removed and `previous` is undefined when it held nothing.

returns.description: A zero-argument function that cancels this subscription.

functions.name: set
functions.description: Writes one key of this entity's state and replicates it to whoever the scope names. Throws when a limit is reached.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Key to write; at most 64 UTF-8 bytes.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Value to store. Booleans, numbers and strings travel as themselves; anything else is serialized as JSON. At most 4096 bytes.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Who the key reaches: every client that can see the entity (the default), only its owning client, or nobody -- server-side storage that never goes on the wire.

returns.description: True when the value changed, false when it was already stored.

functions.name: remove
functions.description: Removes one key from this entity's state, telling every client that held it.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Key to drop.

returns.description: True when the key was set and has been removed.
